title: CSR as a Systemic Buffer Against External Disruption: Panel Evidence on COVID-19 Resilience and Firm Performance in Korean-Listed Firms
summary: Background: Whether corporate social responsibility (CSR) helps firms withstand external disruption, and how any advantage evolves as a shock unfolds, remains unresolved. Drawing on stakeholder theory, conservation of resources theory, and a systems-resilience perspective, we set out two competing predictions for the acute phase of COVID-19: an insurance-based loss-mitigation view and a resource-premium view. Methods: We use a balanced panel of 100 KOSPI-listed non-financial firms observed annually from 2016 to 2024 (900 firm-year observations) and estimate two-way fixed-effects difference-in-differences and event-study models, classifying firms by pre-crisis (2016–2019) CSR and clustering standard errors by firm. Results: Firms with higher pre-crisis CSR show a positive return-on-assets differential that appears in 2020, is statistically clear from 2021, and persists through 2024 without attenuating, although the recovery-phase differential is not statistically larger than the acute-phase differential. Each ESG sub-dimension is associated with the post-COVID-19 differential when examined separately, but only governance remains so when all three are included jointly. Conclusions: The estimates describe differential performance trajectories associated with pre-crisis CSR status rather than causal effects, and the design cannot identify the mechanism. The persistence pattern is somewhat more consistent with a resource-premium than a loss-mitigation view.

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on Enterprise Performance
summary: Under the background of restructuring the global industrial chain and increasing downward pressure on the economy, there is no unified conclusion in the academic circle as to whether the digital transformation can break through the traditional "Solow paradox" and effectively stimulate the performance growth. Based on the panel data of China's A- share listed companies, this paper uses fixed effect model and intermediary effect test method to empirically analyze the impact of digital transformation on enterprise performance and the specific transmission mechanism. The research results show that digital transformation can obviously improve the business performance of enterprises. After a series of robustness and endogenous tests, this conclusion is still valid. The results of mechanism analysis show that digital transformation indirectly promotes performance improvement by optimizing the allocation efficiency of fixed assets, activating supply chain finance and enhancing supply chain toughness. Heterogeneity analysis further found that this boosting effect is more obvious in non-state-owned enterprises and high-tech industries. This research breaks the inherent cognition that performance loss is inevitable in the early stage of digital transformation, not only enriches the theoretical system of digital technology empowerment, but also solves the problem of resource mismatch for micro-enterprises, the realization of precise policy implementation by macro policies provides important empirical reference.

title: Review of the conference book Corporate governance: Theory and the best practices by I. Galavotti, A. Kostyuk, & M. Situm
summary: The conference proceedings book Corporate Governance: Theory and the Best Practices, edited by Ilaria Galavotti, Alexander Kostyuk, and Mario Situm, presents a multidisciplinary collection of contemporary research addressing the evolving nature of corporate governance in an increasingly complex global business environment. The proceedings originate from the International Online Conference held on June 4, 2026, and bring together contributions organized into four principal thematic sessions: board of directors’ practices, environmental, social, and governance (ESG) and Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) practices, reporting and disclosure, and general issues of corporate governance. The volume reflects the growing recognition that corporate governance extends beyond conventional monitoring mechanisms and regulatory compliance to encompass strategic decision-making, sustainability, technological innovation, organizational accountability, and long-term value creation.

title: Integration of Environmental, Social and Governance Principles in Commercial Banks: A Study on Their Impact on Risk Management, Credit Decision-Making, and Long-Term Performance
summary: Against the backdrop of intensifying global climate risks, an increasingly sophisticated regulatory framework, and growing stakeholder awareness of sustainable development, the Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) philosophy has become a core guiding principle for transformation and upgrading in the financial sector, driving significant innovation in commercial banks' traditional risk assessment and operational management frameworks. This paper employs a literature review approach to systematically examine the logical relationship between commercial bank performance and the ESG philosophy. It integrates relevant policies and regulatory documents—such as those pertaining to climate risk management and sustainable finance frameworks—to focus on exploring specific pathways for incorporating ESG principles into commercial banks' risk management systems and credit decision-making processes. The study analyzes the mechanisms through which ESG factors influence banks' long-term operational performance and sustainable development capabilities, and compares differences in the implementation of ESG practices among commercial banks in various countries. The research findings indicate that ESG factors represent a significant extension and expansion of commercial banks' traditional risk management systems; they can effectively address the limitations of risk identification based on traditional financial indicators and help standardize banks' credit resource allocation practices.

title: Transformation of documentation support in the digital economy: the historical aspect
summary: Traditional document management methods are giving way to electronic systems integrated with business processes, as the conditions of digitalization inevitably introduce drastic changes in approaches to information management. The purpose of the article is to analyze current trends and challenges in the era of global digitalization, identify promising areas of development and identify progressive models of transformation of documentation support to improve the efficiency of document management in organizations. The relevance of the work is due to the need to adapt traditional office management systems to the requirements of automation, end-to-end data management and ensuring the legal significance of electronic document management. The research objectives include: reconstructing the current state of documentation support as a historically constituted institution entering a new phase of transformation on the path toward digital platforms; uncovering the inner logic of the transition from paper-based and hybrid document flow to a fully digital model built on unified repositories and API integrations — a transition comparable, in the scale of its institutional consequences, to earlier stages in the unification of Russian record-keeping; assessing the impact of digital technologies on the reliability and speed of document processing, as well as determining the specifics of digital transformation's impact on the processes of value appraisal, storage, and use of archival documents and other materials generated within electronic document flow systems. The research uses methods of theoretical analysis, synthesis, search, selection, systematization of sources, and comparison of research results from leading Russian companies. The methods of content analysis and case study were used to systematize the data. A problematic research field on the problems and prospects of transformation of documentation support for business process management in the digital economy is analyzed. A particular place in the article is occupied by the historical dimension of document flow: its digital transformation is treated not as an isolated technical and managerial phenomenon, but as another — and by no means final — link in the centuries-long chain of transformations of Russian document flow, from the prikaznoe record-keeping of the Muscovite state and the kollezhskoe system codified by the General Regulations of 1720, to the unified state record-keeping systems of the Soviet period (the Unified State Records System of 1973, the State System of Documentation Support for Management of 1988). Such a historical-genetic perspective allows the digitalization of document flow to be seen not as a break with tradition, but as its logical continuation.

title: Analyzing FinTech and sustainable development through the triple bottom line framework using bibliometric analysis
summary: The present study explores the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of FinTech-enabled sustainable development through the Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework. The paper highlights the use of FinTech innovations to advance sustainable development while balancing the economic (Profit), social (People), and environmental (Planet) dimensions. A bibliometric study was conducted using publications in the Scopus database. Bibliometric analysis, including publication trends, influential journals, leading authors, countries and institutions, co-authorship analysis, keyword co-occurrence analysis, and thematic mapping, was employed using Biblioshiny and VoSviewer to identify emerging directions in the field. This paper examined 3375 records extracted from the Scopus database on 28th January 2026, related to FinTech and to economic, social, and environmental sustainability between 2015 and 2026. The findings show a decent growth in FinTech and sustainable development research, with China emerging as the most influential country in the field for substantive study. The TBL-based classification reveals a concentration of study within the ‘People’ and ‘Profit’ dimensions, whereas the ‘Planet’ dimension remains relatively understudied. The field is rapidly evolving, with an average article age of approximately 2.69 years, reflecting the recent and growing scholarly interest in FinTech-enabled sustainable development. The study integrates FinTech literature with the TBL framework through a bibliometric analysis. It extends previous studies by systematically categorizing research themes across ‘People-Planet-Profit’ dimensions. The findings suggest theoretical, practical, and policy implications for promoting sustainability in the FinTech ecosystem by placing greater emphasis on green finance, climate-focused innovation, and inclusive digital financial services.

title: Research on the Impact of Digital Economy on Urban Low-Carbon Development
summary: Against the backdrop of accelerating digital transformation, the relationship between the development of the digital economy (DE) and urban low-carbon development (ULCD) has become an important issue in current research. Using 29 cities data covering from 2011 to 2022, this study constructs an ULCD index through the entropy-weighting method and employs a fixed-effects model to examine whether the DE contributes expansion to ULCD. Research has found that: (1) The DE can significantly promote UULCD. The coefficient of DE in the benchmark regression is 0.0000796. (2) After tail reduction and one period lag test, the DE coefficients were 0.0000973 and 0.0001041, respectively, and the research conclusion remained stable. (3) After heterogeneity testing, it can be found that the strength of the role of the DE in ULCD varies with the regional economic development status, and the promotion effect is more pronounced in low economic development areas, with a regression coefficient of 0.0002727.

title: Supply chain resilience in the era of geopolitical disruptions: a capability-based co-evolutionary framework for supply chain resilience
summary: Purpose This study aims to systematically synthesize the literature at the intersection of geopolitical risk (GPR) and supply chain resilience (SCR) to investigate how modern theoretical models and advanced predictive tools are utilized to integrate GPR into SCR frameworks, ultimately proposing a capability-based framework for building resilient supply networks. Design/methodology/approach We used a multi-stage methodological framework anchored in the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 guidelines. Following a systematic search and screening process that yielded a final corpus of 75 high-impact academic articles, we conducted bibliometric analysis via RStudio (Biblioshiny), followed by structural topic modeling (STM) using R, and finally a NotebookLM-assisted qualitative synthesis, with all outputs manually cross-checked against the original articles. Findings The theoretical foundation of SCR has evolved through three distinct themes: SCR models and frameworks; geographic, operational and strategic reconfiguration; and artificial intelligence, predictive analytics and digital integration. The study proposes a novel capability-based co-evolutionary framework, encompassing proactive anticipation and semantic risk sensing, agile response and shock absorption, collaborative recovery and stabilization, and strategic value chain restructuring to integrate GPRs into SCR. Practical implications A capability-based co-evolutionary framework was proposed from the literature synthesis that enables SCR across the pre- and post-disruption phases of geopolitical events. This provides managers with an actionable, iterative roadmap to transition from reactive risk mitigation to proactive, AI-driven resilience in a fragmented global economy. Originality/value This paper addresses a critical gap by providing a unified synthesis of fragmented GPR and SCR research. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is among the first to comprehensively map how macro-level geopolitical indices, advanced AI-driven predictive analytics and structural network adaptations interact to safeguard long-term supply chain viability.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation in the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency, 2014-2026
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital transformation have increasingly become important instruments for improving efficiency, transparency, accountability, decision-making, and service delivery in public organisations. This study examined Artificial Intelligence and digital transformation in the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (NESREA) from 2014 to 2026. Specifically, the study sought to examine the influence of machine learning on bureaucratic imperatives and the influence of digital data management systems on decision-making. The study adopted the survey research design and used primary and secondary data. The population of the study comprises 300 officials from which 171 respondents were determined using Taro Yamane’s formula and purposively selected. Structured questionnaire were administered to elicit information from the 160 retrieved questionnaire which was subsequently analysed, representing a 93.6% retrieval rate. The research instrument was validated by experts, while reliability was determined using Cronbach’s Alpha. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and Pearson Product-Moment Correlation in SPSS. Findings showed that machine learning improved on administrative imperatives, with a grand mean of 2.98 and a positive relationship with bureaucratic efficiency at; r = 0.684, p = 0.000. Digital data management systems enhanced decision-making at; grand mean = 3.04; r = 0.721, p = 0.000. The study concluded that digital technologies significantly strengthened administrative performance in NESREA. The study thus, recommended that NESREA should adopt stronger machine learning, and improved digital data infrastructure, as well as staff capacity development, and technical support in other to improve and sustain NESREA environmental governance capacity.

title: The Last-Mile Problem in Green Finance: Why Small Businesses Struggle to Access Sustainable Finance, and a Readiness Index to Measure It
summary: Abstract Green finance has expanded quickly over the last decade, but most of that growth has reached borrowers that already have the reporting systems and collateral that lenders expect. Small businesses, which make up the bulk of enterprises and jobs in emerging economies, sit at the far end of the chain. This is the last mile of green finance. The paper approaches the problem from the borrower's side rather than the investor's and asks why small firms struggle to reach sustainable finance even where suitable credit lines exist. Building on work about information asymmetry, financial literacy and the diffusion of innovations, it identifies seven barriers: ESG data, documentation, awareness, collateral, financial literacy, perceived complexity and green investment knowledge. These are turned into a composite instrument, the Small Business Green Finance Readiness Index (SB-GFRI), scored from 0 to 100. Because primary survey data are still to be collected, the empirical section applies the index to a sample of 320 firm profiles built only to demonstrate and stress-test the analytical workflow; the results show how the method behaves and are not evidence about real firms. Six hypotheses are tested with logistic regression, one-way ANOVA, Welch's t-test, Spearman correlation and Friedman's test. The index proved internally consistent (Cronbach's alpha = 0.85) and insensitive to the weighting scheme, and the workflow returned interpretable readiness tiers linked to practical support measures. The paper closes with implications for lenders, regulators and business-support intermediaries.

title: Corporate Governance, ESG Disclosure and Firm Value in an Emerging Market
summary: Purpose: This paper examines how corporate governance and the disclosure of environmental, social and governance (ESG) information have co-evolved in Vietnam between 2015 and 2024, and through which channels the two are expected to bear on firm value in an emerging market where the state remains a dominant owner. Design/methodology/approach: The study adopts a qualitative design that combines systematic document analysis of 18 regulatory and soft-law instruments issued between 2012 and 2024 with an integrative review of published empirical evidence on Vietnamese listed companies and secondary benchmark data from the ASEAN Corporate Governance Scorecard and a ten-year census of disclosure practices. Material was coded deductively against agency, stakeholder, legitimacy, signalling and institutional theory, and inductively for emergent themes. Findings: Vietnam’s regime moved through three phases: Mandated entry (2015 to 2017), soft-law consolidation (2017 to 2020) and statutory upgrading with climate alignment (2021 to 2024). Disclosure spread rapidly in breadth, yet depth lagged. Standalone reports rose only from about 1 percent to 7 percent of listed firms, GRI referencing stayed near 22 percent throughout the decade, and third-party assurance remained rare. Vietnam’s mean governance score in the 2024 regional assessment (60.15 points) sat 31 points below the ASEAN mean. The empirical literature reports a mostly positive association between disclosure and value, but the evidence is concentrated among large firms and is sensitive to how disclosure is measured. We argue that governance shapes value less through the volume of ESG disclosure than through its credibility, and we formalise this argument in a conceptual framework with five propositions. Originality/value: The paper offers the first decade-long, regulation-anchored synthesis of the governance, disclosure and value nexus in Vietnam. It distinguishes formal adoption from substantive practice and proposes a credibility-centred mechanism that can be tested once longitudinal, assurance-adjusted disclosure data become available.

title: Boundary Conditions of Institutional Investors' Impact on Stock Price Crash Risk
summary: Institutional investors are central participants in the capital market, and stock price crash risk is directly tied to the stability of that market. Existing studies mainly focus on how investors from institutions influence stock price crash risk, yet few studies summarize the boundary conditions under which this influence operates. This paper systematically reviews these boundary conditions from three dimensions: institutional investors' own heterogeneity, firms' own characteristics, and the external market and institutional environment. The literature review results indicate that under different boundary conditions, there are pronounced differences in the direction of institutional investors' impact on stock price crash risk (inhibition or exacerbation), as well as the strength of various mechanisms of influence. Finally, this paper identifies future research directions related to multi-boundary interaction effects and the ongoing reform of China's capital markets, providing a literature basis for deeply understanding the heterogeneous role of institutional investors and improving capital market regulation.

title: The relationship between executive remuneration and earnings management: incorporating the disclosure quality of financial reporting judgements
summary: Abstract According to managerial power theory, executives may be biased in their financial reporting judgements (FRJs), which can lead to accounting choices that increase earnings and potentially result in abnormal (excessive) executive remuneration. Global empirical studies suggest that the pursuit of higher executive remuneration can incentivise earnings management (EM) engagement. However, previous research on the relationship between EM and executive remuneration has mainly focused on developed countries, used accrual-based EM proxies, and often included only chief executive officer remuneration. The main objective of the study was to investigate the relationship between EM and executive remuneration in South Africa, a developing country, using the disclosure quality of FRJs as a measure of EM. Another unique contribution entails a more comprehensive measure of executive remuneration, covering all executive directors, and an indicator of whether the remuneration was deemed abnormal. Understanding this relationship in South Africa is vital, given the existing high levels of income inequality, particularly from a social justice perspective. Using a quantitative approach, the research examined 101 Johannesburg Stock Exchange-listed companies from 2020 to 2023. Applying regression analysis, the study found that executives may indeed be biased in their FRJs, leading to abnormal executive remuneration. The findings highlight the need for ongoing monitoring of remuneration and the quality of FRJ disclosures to mitigate the risk of rent extraction and to curb executives’ opportunistic behaviour. Without such oversight, using EM strategies to secure abnormal remuneration will erode public trust.

title: The role of CEO narcissism in shaping environmental reporting: insights from an emerging economy
summary: Purpose The study aims to investigate the association between chief executive officer (CEO) narcissism and environmental reporting in the banking industry of Bangladesh. Design/methodology/approach This study employs a sample of 245 firm-year observations from the listed banks of Dhaka Stock Exchange spanning the period during 2018–2024. To measure CEO narcissism, we used two distinct indicators: (1) the prominence of the CEO's photograph in the annual report and (2) the size of the CEO's signature. The analysis employs both static and dynamic panel estimations to test the hypotheses. Findings Consistent with upper echelons theory, the results reveal a positive and statistically significant association between CEO narcissism and the extent of environmental reporting. Further analyses indicate that the association is stronger in larger firms and is positively moderated by CEO compensation, suggesting that organizational visibility and financial incentives amplify the disclosure-enhancing effects of narcissistic leadership. Importantly, the findings indicate an increase in the extent of environmental disclosures, rather than necessarily reflecting substantive environmental performance. Practical implications The results highlight the need for boards, regulators and policymakers to critically assess the credibility of environmental disclosures, particularly in contexts where reporting is largely voluntary. Strengthened governance mechanisms, enhanced disclosure standards and independent assurance may help mitigate the risk of symbolic reporting and greenwashing under narcissistic leadership. Originality/value This study provides the first evidence from an emerging economy on how CEO narcissism shapes environmental reporting behavior. By distinguishing between disclosure extent and substantive commitment, it contributes to the literature on executive personality, voluntary disclosure and corporate sustainability in emerging-market contexts.

title: The Economics of Scarcity and Ecosystem Lock-in: NVIDIA's Premium Pricing, Market Power and Consumer Willingness to Pay in the AI Accelerator Market
summary: This study analyzes NVIDIA's high pricing model in the AI chip market by combining the concepts of product differentiation, market power, and consumer behavior. It suggests that NVIDIA has established very high switching costs with the CUDA ecosystem, making the price elasticity of demand very low, if not approaching zero, allowing them to charge a price well above the marginal cost. While this approach is based on using excess profits to invest in technological progress, it has also brought about demand-side issues such as distortions in the allocation of resources resulting from the "computing capacity tax" and consumer surplus reductions due to hardware-and-software bundling. At the industry level, it has exacerbated the excessive concentration of the market and created systemic risks. To address this, this study recommends steps to optimize these measures, like setting up interoperable technical standards, moving towards transparent tiered-pricing regulations, and enhancing the resilience of the supply chain. These measures are designed to maintain a balance between the corporate incentives for innovation, market fairness, and efficiency, and to offer a theoretical reference for the healthy development of the AI industry ecosystem and inclusive growth in the global digital economy.

title: Navigating digital transformation for inventory leanness through product and supply chain strategy
summary: Purpose This study examines why digital transformation has a non-monotonic effect on inventory leanness and how product diversification and supply-chain concentration condition this relationship. Design/methodology/approach The empirical analysis uses an unbalanced panel of 2,533 Chinese listed manufacturing firms and 19,299 firm-year observations from 2010 to 2023. Firm and year fixed effects are absorbed and conventional standard errors are reported in the primary models. Following Haans et al. (2016), the quadratic specification is treated as a parsimonious empirical approximation to a theory-derived marginal-effect pattern; the analysis tests endpoint slopes, the Lind–Mehlum joint U test, and Fieller confidence intervals; and evaluates conditional curvature, turning-point movement and shape-flip in the moderated models. Findings The findings reveal a U-shaped relationship between digital transformation and inventory leanness. Product diversification strengthens the curvature of this relationship, and this curvature-enhancing effect is further amplified by supplier concentration but weakened by customer concentration. Conditional analyses indicate that the complete U-shaped pattern depends on specific configurations, with limited shape reversals occurring only at the distributional tails. Practical implications Managers should distinguish exploration-related learning friction from the exploitation of retained digital routines. Product diversification raises the information-processing burden during early transformation but can create stronger inventory benefits after digital routines mature. Deep supplier coordination can reinforce these benefits through relation-specific digital assets, whereas dependence on a small number of powerful customers can limit portfolio-wide inventory optimization. Originality/value The study contributes by identifying two countervailing latent mechanisms – exploration-related learning friction and the exploitation of retained digital routines – that combine additively to generate a U-shaped relationship. It further shows how product complexity alters the curvature of this relationship and how supplier and customer concentration provide asymmetric boundary conditions. The analysis responds to methodological concerns in nonlinear research by separating curvature change, turning-point movement and shape-flip.

title: Beyond greenwashing? The politics of meaning in sustainable finance
summary: Sustainable finance is a prominent but contested feature of contemporary investment landscapes. Disclosure-based frameworks that require financial actors to publicly report how sustainability is reflected in their investment products amplify this dynamic. Two distinct analytical orientations structure scholarly debate on sustainable finance and its transformative potential. Structural perspectives explain why such regulatory approaches operate within rather than against financial logic, while actor-centered perspectives document heterogeneous constellations through which sustainable finance is constructed. Yet, neither theorizes the compliance process through which the macro-level regulatory architecture is translated into micro-level meaning-making, and, vice versa, how the conditions of the translation process shape what definitions of sustainability become institutionalized at macro-level. This commentary argues that a discursive-institutionalist lens illuminates the link between both accounts by focusing on the ideational and discursive dimensions of the compliance process and proposes a research agenda organized around three interrelated questions: under what institutional conditions the meaning of sustainable finance is collectively negotiated; how geopolitical and geoeconomic factors function as discursive occasions for revising those meanings; and finally, what governance through ambiguous disclosure-based regulations actually accomplishes.

title: Digital Transformation and Corporate ESG Performance: A Literature Review on Mechanisms of Action
summary: Digital transformation has also become one of the most important drivers of the sustainable development of enterprises under the influence of the digital economy. Being an assessment tool that assesses the overall performance of enterprises in environmental, social responsibility, and corporate governance, ESG has gained popularity among scholars and practitioners alike. Even though an increasing body of literature investigates the effect of digital transformation on corporate ESG performance, the results regarding the main effect have been inconclusive, and additional research on transmission paths and boundary conditions is possible. In accordance with the literature-review methodology, this paper selects appropriate articles in the CNKI and Web of Science databases published in 20182025. It summarizes the present studies along three dimensions: main effect, mediating transmission paths, and moderating boundary conditions, examines the reasons behind empirical divergences, identifies the gaps in research, and gives the directions to be followed in future research. The research reveals that digital transformation influences corporate ESG performance mostly via three channels: resource allocation, internal governance, and green innovation, and that these effects are conditioned by various internal and external variables. Most of the available research works center their attention on major A-share listed companies, whereas the mechanisms of testing small- and medium-sized companies require further study. This paper will serve as the basis of further empirical research and the practice of coordinated digital-green development in enterprises.

title: Bank Consolidation in a Turbulent Period: A Bibliometric Mapping of Publications Since 2020
summary: The COVID-19 pandemic, followed by multiple geopolitical conflicts, changed the overall functioning of banks and the global merger and acquisition (M&A) market. However, the development of research on bank M&As specifically since 2020 remains unmapped. This study analyses scholarly works on bank M&As published since 2020 using bibliometric analysis to examine publication trends, leading sources, authors, countries, collaboration patterns, thematic development, and the ongoing research agenda. Using a PRISMA-guided screening procedure, 179 Scopus-indexed documents in 138 sources and involving 427 authors were selected for performance analysis and science mapping. The findings show that research activity increased notably in 2024 and 2025, with a marked rise in publications from Asian and developing economies. Finance Research Letters and Journal of Risk and Financial Management emerge as the most productive publication venues. The study shows limited international collaboration among authors alongside a low concentration of author productivity. The bibliographic coupling and co-occurrence analysis show that the domain has moved beyond traditional concerns such as performance and efficiency, incorporating interdisciplinary themes such as organisational culture, fintech, corporate governance, financial stability, and regulatory issues.

title: EVALUASI DAN PENGENDALIAN DALAM MANAJEMEN STRATEGIK: TINJAUAN LITERATUR SISTEMATIS LINTAS SEKTOR BISNIS, PEMERINTAHAN, DAN PENDIDIKAN
summary: Evaluation and control represent the final yet most frequently neglected stage of the strategic management process, even though the success of strategy implementation depends heavily on an organisation's capacity to continuously monitor, measure, and correct performance deviations. This article synthesises the concepts, frameworks, and practices of strategic evaluation and control based on recent scholarly literature, while comparing their application across three distinct organisational contexts: the business/corporate sector, the government/public sector, and the education/non-profit sector. A systematic literature review was conducted following the PRISMA protocol, encompassing identification, screening, eligibility assessment, and inclusion. The search was carried out in June 2026 with a publication cut-off of 31 December 2025, so that only fully completed publication years were considered. The selection process yielded 23 journal articles indexed in Scopus and Sinta 1-2 published between 2021 and 2025, complemented by 15 reference books in strategic management and management control as the theoretical foundation, giving a total of 38 analysed sources. The findings indicate that strategic control comprises three interrelated levels, namely strategic control, management control, and operational control, all reinforced by instruments such as the balanced scorecard, internal control systems, internal audit, and management information systems. In the business sector, strategic control tends to be oriented toward financial performance and corporate governance; in the government sector, emphasis shifts toward public accountability and policy alignment; whereas in the education sector, strategic control centres on academic quality assurance. Digital transformation and organisational dynamic capabilities are identified as contextual factors that moderate the effectiveness of the entire process. This article offers an integrative conceptual model as a theoretical contribution toward the future development of cross-sector strategic control research.

title: Geopolitical forces and strategic decision-making in multinational firms: a scorecard and heatmap comparative analysis
summary: In an increasingly interconnected world, the knowledge economy-encompassing technology, education and research-faces complex challenges posed by the evolving geopolitical dynamics. This paper examines how multinational companies strategically respond to these shifts. Through a compre­hensive analysis of regulatory changes, political instability, trade policies and decarbonization concerns, this paper highlights the composite nature of geopolitical risks and their influence on corporate strate­gy. Methodologically, the research employs a scorecard and a heatmap to provide a systematic, organ­ization‑level framework for comparing firms’ strategic responses. The scorecard evaluates regulatory compliance, supply chain resilience, risk management, strategic partnerships, innovation and carbon reduction targets across Apple, SAP and Tesla, with scores ranging from 2.00 to 4.00. Apple achieves the highest overall score (3.33/4), followed by Tesla (3.00/4) and SAP (2.83/4), indicating differences in inno­vation, policy alignment and supply chain resilience. The heatmap compares TotalEnergies, Danfoss and General Electric across eight decarbonization indicators, showing Danfoss as the sustainability leader. General Electric exhibits strong renewable‑energy capabilities, but remains constrained by legacy infra­structure. By applying this comparative framework, the study identifies improvement areas and offers strategic recommendations to help multinational companies strengthen geopolitical risk management and maintain competitive advantage in a rapidly changing global environment.

title: Agricultural and Rural Big Data Policy and Agribusiness Supply Chain Resilience: Implications for Sustainable Agriculture in China
summary: Supply chain resilience supports sustainable agriculture by helping firms maintain operations and food supply during disruptions. This study examines whether agricultural digital public infrastructure strengthens agribusiness supply chain resilience, using China’s 2016 Agricultural and Rural Big Data Pilot Program as a quasi-natural experiment within a difference-in-differences design. The estimates indicate that the program significantly improves supply chain resilience. Exploratory channel analyses provide evidence consistent with bank-credit and corporate digital-transformation channels. The estimated gains are greater among state-owned enterprises, firms with digitally experienced executives, and firms in regions with higher internet penetration. Component analyses show positive estimates for agricultural data sharing, market-based investment and operational mechanisms, and big-data applications, whereas commodity-specific database development has no statistically detectable effect. These findings contribute to sustainability research by linking digital public infrastructure to the capacity of agribusinesses to withstand and recover from disruptions, an important foundation for the economic sustainability of agricultural supply chains. They also suggest that coordinated investment in data infrastructure, financing access, and digital capabilities may support more reliable agricultural supply and sustainable agricultural development, particularly in economies with fragmented production and limited information sharing.

title: Nonlinear Effects of Board Age on Corporate Social Responsibility in Vietnam: The Moderating Role of Product Market Competition
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether the relationship between average board age and corporate social responsibility (CSR) is nonlinear and whether product market competition conditions this relationship. Drawing on Upper Echelons Theory and stakeholder, agency, and institutional perspectives, we argue that increasing board age initially supports CSR through greater experience, stakeholder knowledge, and reputational awareness, but eventually constrains it as conservatism and risk aversion become more pronounced. Using 2201 firm‐year observations from 259 Vietnamese listed firms over 2015–2023, we estimate firm‐ and year‐fixed‐effects models and conduct extensive robustness and endogeneity analyses. The results reveal an inverted U ‐shaped relationship between board age and CSR. Because the estimated turning point is below the sample mean, most firms lie on the declining portion of the curve, producing a predominantly negative average association, especially for environmental and governance CSR. Product market competition serves as an important boundary condition: in less competitive industries (higher HHI), the negative effect associated with higher board age is weaker. The findings remain robust across alternative specifications, winsorized data, subgroup analyses, lagged models, fixed‐effects instrumental‐variable estimation, and two‐step system GMM. By integrating a threshold‐based account of board age with an external competitive boundary condition, this study explains when and why board demographics shape responsible corporate behavior in an emerging market.

title: O‘ZBEKISTON BANK TIZIMIDA RAQAMLI TRANSFORMATSIYANING RIVOJLANISH YO‘NALISHLARI VA XORIJIY KAPITAL ISHTIROKIDAGI BANKLARNING INSTITUTSIONAL AHAMIYATI
summary: This article investigates the development of digital transformation in Uzbekistan’s banking system and the potential institutional contribution of banks with foreign capital participation to technological modernization. The study aims to assess the digitalization of banking services, examine key financial indicators, and identify the conditions under which foreign capital may support digital development. Systemic analysis, comparative assessment, statistical grouping, and logical generalization are employed. Publicly available information from the Central Bank of Uzbekistan and the World Bank is used to examine banking assets, loans, deposits, and digital financing services. The findings indicate that remote banking, electronic payments, digital lending, and electronic factoring are expanding opportunities to access financial services. At the same time, cybersecurity, data quality, digital inequality, and technology integration costs remain important constraints. Banks with foreign capital participation may facilitate the adoption of international expertise, technological investment, and improved corporate governance. However, the actual outcomes depend not on ownership structure alone, but also on investment priorities, management quality, and adaptation to domestic market conditions. The article proposes measures to improve the assessment of digital banking performance and the effectiveness of technological investment

title: The Role of Green Adaptability and Circular Economy in Encouraging Green Innovation in Batik SMEs in Pekalongan
summary: This study examines the relationship between Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM), Green Adaptability, Circular Economy, and Green Innovation in the context of batik small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Pekalongan, Indonesia, a traditional cultural industry facing significant environmental challenges. Although GSCM is often considered important in sustainable business transformation, this study empirically tests the integration of these three constructs through Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) and finds that Green Adaptability significantly influences Circular Economy (β = 0.149, p < 0.001) and Green Innovation (β = 0.396, p < 0.001), while Circular Economy also positively contributes to Green Innovation (β = 0.119, p < 0.001). In contrast, GSCM does not significantly influence these three variables (p > 0.5). These findings indicate that in the context of batik SMEs, the implementation of GSCM practices tends to be operational in nature and has not yet developed into a strategic capability capable of supporting sustainable innovation. Theoretically, this study extends the application of Dynamic Capability Theory and the Resource-Based View by emphasizing that organizational adaptive capabilities are the primary drivers of green innovation compared to fragmented green supply chain practices. Its empirical contribution is also significant because it fills a research gap in traditional cultural industries that has received little attention in the sustainability and innovation literature. These findings provide practical implications for policymakers and business actors to focus on developing adaptive capabilities and circular production systems to strengthen green innovation and the sustainable competitiveness of batik SMEs.

title: The impact of digital transformation in management accounting on business performance: Evidence from an emerging market
summary: Digital transformation has become a strategic priority for modern enterprises; however, the organizational mechanisms through which it enhances business performance remain insufficiently understood. This study investigates how digital transformation in management accounting improves business performance by examining the mediating roles of management accounting information quality and management effectiveness. Data were collected from 312 enterprises in Vietnam and analyzed using Cronbach’s alpha, exploratory factor analysis (EFA), confirmatory factor analysis (CFA), and structural equation modeling (SEM). The results indicate that digital transformation has a strong positive effect on management accounting information quality (β = 0.816), which subsequently strengthens management effectiveness and enhances business performance. In addition, the significant direct and indirect effects provide evidence of partial mediation, demonstrating that digital transformation creates organizational value through multiple complementary mechanisms. The originality of this study lies in explaining the organizational mechanism through which digital transformation improves business performance by identifying management accounting information quality as the pivotal capability linking digital transformation to management effectiveness and organizational performance. The findings provide practical implications for managers and policymakers by suggesting that the success of digital transformation depends not only on technology adoption but also on the organization’s ability to transform digital capabilities into high-quality management accounting information that supports effective managerial decision-making and sustainable business performance.

title: Chanel: Future-Proofing the Business Model
summary: This case examines Chanel’s evolution from its founding by Gabrielle ‘Coco’ Chanel to a global luxury megabrand. It explores the company’s distinctive strategy – from its vertically integrated supply chain to its refusal to espouse e-commerce, menswear or creative collaborations – while maintaining an unwavering focus on desirability. During Karl Lagerfeld’s four-decade tenure as creative director, Chanel perfected its business model, in which high-end couture drove up consumer willingness to pay and translated into sales of high-margin, high-volume accessories and beauty products.The 2020 Covid-19 pandemic tested Chanel’s resilience. It navigated it through a spate of price increases and intensified marketing. With the appointment of Leena Nair as CEO in 2022, the company embarked on a modernisation effort emphasising diversity, inclusion and social sustainability. But as the post-pandemic luxury consumption boom ended, Chanel faced a complex transition, raising key questions. To what extent could it continue to sustain growth by increasing prices? Where could it find the next whitespace opportunity? Should it rethink its digital and omnichannel approach? And how could it adapt its culture to remain relevant to both customers and employees in the years ahead?

title: Green fiscal policy and green finance in mitigating environmental deterioration in Central European regions
summary: Environmental deterioration has intensified across Central Europe as rapid economic expansion continues to rely heavily on resource extraction, fossil fuel consumption, and industrial emissions. This growing ecological pressure has renewed interest in policy instruments capable of steering regions toward sustainable development. Motivated by these concerns, this investigation assessed how green fiscal policy (GFP), green finance (GRF), patent applications (PAP), renewable energy (REN), and natural resource rent (NAR) influence carbon emissions (CAR) in 13 Central European economies with data from 1990–2022. The analysis applies a series of diagnostics followed by the Cross Sectionally Augmented Autoregressive Distributed Lag (CS ARDL) model, supported by FMOLS robustness and Dumitrescu–Hurlin causality tests. The results reveal that GFP, GRF, and REN significantly reduce carbon emissions in both the short and long run. Conversely, NAR and PAP unexpectedly appreciate emissions, depicting inefficiencies in resource governance and the limited environmental orientation of current innovation activities. The D&H causality illustrated both unidirectional and bidirectional causality among the variables. These findings imply that Central European economies can accelerate their transition toward ecological sustainability by strengthening carbon pricing mechanisms, renewable energy investment, restructuring green finance portfolios to low carbon technologies, and enforcing sustainable resource extraction practices for long term carbon neutrality.

title: Review of Literature on Corporate Cash Holdings and Future Research Agenda in an ESG Framework
summary: ABSTRACT This study synthesizes the literature on corporate cash holdings under an ESG framework and develops a theoretically grounded future research agenda. Based on a systematic review of 116 studies screened from Scopus and Web of Science Core Collection, the literature is categorized into five streams: impacts of aggregate ESG, environmental, social, and governance factors on cash holdings, and reverse effects of cash holdings/financial slack on ESG‐related outcomes. ESG reshapes three established cash‐holding motives: the insurance value of liquidity, the financing wedge between internal and external funds, and agency costs of retained cash. The E, S, and G pillars present distinct mechanisms tied to environmental commitments, stakeholder/labor claims, and liquidity governance. Stronger ESG can reduce cash by lowering risk, financing frictions, or agency costs, while strategic liquidity needs, stakeholder commitments, and adverse ESG shocks may increase cash demand. Reverse evidence shows accumulated liquidity funds ESG investment and supports employment resilience, forming a dynamic bidirectional ESG‐cash relationship. Methodologically, OLS and fixed‐effects regressions dominate the literature, while quasi‐experimental, structural, and machine‐learning approaches remain rare. Future research could explore nonlinear, co‐determined ESG‐cash dynamics via E‐DSGE modeling, real‐options analysis, AI‐enabled liquidity management, and ESG contagion in strategic alliances.

title: Application of Internet of Things (IoT) on Improving Performance within Global Manufacturing Supply Chains
summary: Internet of Things (IoT) in the context of supply chains (SC) is mainly observed with integration to build resilience. It has discussed the rationale in terms of disruptions caused by the pandemic, the economic and political situation. It has elaborated on the issues such as labor and material shortages affecting demand and supply sides. IoT impacts greatly on the manufacturing SC to enhance efficiency and transparency. Besides this, the implementation of IoT technology has monitored manufacturing procedures and enhanced productivity to deliver a safer working space. In addition to this, this technology has improved supply chain performance to resolve the operational bottleneck and use OTA methods. The study has discussed the factors related to the vulnerabilities of IoT systems, and it has mainly focused on security issues leading to increased concerns. In the context of a SC system, organization and supplier networks are required to work together to get optimal performance. The study explores different methodologies for collecting data. Interpretivism philosophy, exploratory design, inductive approach, and secondary data collection methods have been chosen in this study. Data has been provided in support of the findings in linking them with objectives. It includes that IoT can use different techniques to improve the SC performance and advance the production process.

title: Rethinking resilience: bridging due diligence gaps to mitigate supply chain risks
summary: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine the key factors affecting supply chain due diligence (SCDD), evaluating their associated risks and proposing appropriate mitigation strategies that bridge due diligence gaps and strengthen resilience in global supply chains. Design/methodology/approach Key due diligence factors were identified through a comprehensive literature review and expert consultations. The study adopts a multimethod approach that integrates multiple theoretical perspectives, the Fuzzy Evidential Reasoning Algorithm (FERA) and risk profiling analysis. Findings The results identify critical due diligence factors, including regulatory compliance, transparency, supplier evaluation, ethical sourcing, data governance and sustainability practices, that significantly influence governance, operational stability and environmental performance. The study further develops targeted mitigation strategies based on risk intensity and strategic priority. Practical implications The proposed framework supports practitioners and policymakers in making risk-sensitive decisions to strengthen due diligence, improve transparency, enhance compliance and build more resilient and sustainable supply chain operations. Originality/value This study contributes to the SCDD literature by integrating governance, operational and sustainability dimensions within a unified prioritization framework, building on the established FERA rather than proposing a new computational technique. The framework offers a systematic approach for identifying and mitigating due diligence gaps in global supply chains, with SDGs 8, 9 and 13 addressed as an indicative conceptual mapping rather than a directly measured outcome.

title: Effect of Asset Diversification on Financial Performance of Deposit-Taking SACCOs in Kenya: The Moderating Role of Corporate Governance
summary: This study examined the effect of asset diversification on the financial performance of deposit-taking SACCOs (DT-SACCOs) in Kenya and the moderating role of corporate governance in this relationship. A positivist philosophy and an explanatory longitudinal design were adopted. Secondary panel data for 2015–2024 were extracted from the audited financial statements of 122 DT-SACCOs and SASRA reports. Asset diversification was measured by loans and non-loan assets as shares of total assets, financial performance by surplus and the dividend payout ratio, and corporate governance by a board accountability index. Fixed-effects (surplus) and random effects (dividend payout) panel models, selected by the Hausman test, and hierarchical moderated regression were estimated. The loan share was positively associated with surplus (β = 0.382, p < 0.01) but not with dividend payout, while the non-loan asset share was negatively associated with dividend payout (β = −0.092, p < 0.05). Board accountability was positively associated with both measures and strengthened the association of lending with surplus (β = 3.271, p < 0.01) and of non-loan assets with dividend payout (β = 0.130, p < 0.05). The results are associations based on secondary data, and governance is captured only through board meeting activity. The SACCO boards should treat member lending as the core business, appraise non-loan investments rigorously and strengthen board and audit committee accountability, while SASRA should monitor non-core investments.

title: Digitalisation and sustainable finance in SMEs: unpacking the causal mechanisms through a systematic review and integrative framework
summary: Purpose Digitalisation has emerged as an important enabler of sustainable finance for small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs). While prior studies have examined the roles of digital technologies, financial access and sustainability in SMEs, limited attention has been devoted to understanding the causal mechanisms through which digitalisation facilitates sustainable finance and contributes to sustainability outcomes. This study systematically reviews the literature to develop an integrated understanding of the pathways linking digitalisation, financial capability and sustainable firm performance. Design/methodology/approach A systematic literature review of 63 peer-reviewed articles published in Scopus-indexed journals between 2015 and 2026 was conducted. The review employs the theory-context-characteristics-methodology (TCCM) framework and the antecedents-decisions-outcomes (ADO) approach to synthesise the intellectual structure of the field, identify dominant research themes and develop an integrative conceptual framework. Findings The review demonstrates that digitalisation enables sustainable finance through several interrelated mechanisms, including enhanced information transparency, reduced transaction costs, improved risk assessment, greater financial inclusion and access to alternative financing channels. These mechanisms strengthen SMEs’ financial capability and digital readiness, thereby facilitating sustainable investments and improving sustainability performance. However, the effectiveness of these relationships depends on institutional support, regulatory environments, technological infrastructure, owner characteristics and firm-level capabilities. Based on these findings, the study proposes an integrative framework linking digital readiness, financial capability, sustainable finance and sustainability outcomes in SMEs. Originality/value This study advances the literature by unpacking the causal mechanisms connecting digitalisation and sustainable finance in the SME context. By integrating insights from diverse theoretical perspectives through the TCCM and ADO frameworks, the study develops a testable conceptual framework that explains how digitalisation influences sustainable finance and sustainability performance. The findings provide a future research agenda and offer practical implications for policymakers, financial institutions and SME managers seeking to foster digitally enabled sustainable development.

title: Exploring the Role of Social Audit and Social Accounting in Achieving Sustainable Corporate Social Responsibility: Evidence From India's Mining Sector
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines the roles of social audit (SA) and social accounting (SAC) in advancing sustainable corporate social responsibility (SCSR) within India's mining sector, with particular emphasis on accountability, transparency, and societal impact. Drawing upon stakeholder theory, legitimacy theory, and institutional theory, the study develops and empirically tests an integrated framework examining the direct relationships between SA, SAC, and SCSR, along with the mediating roles of corporate social innovation (CSI) and inclusive growth (IG). Primary data were collected from 409 beneficiaries of CSR initiatives implemented by mining companies in Odisha, India, using a structured questionnaire. The data were analyzed using exploratory factor analysis, confirmatory factor analysis, and structural equation modeling. The findings indicate that both SA and SAC are positively associated with SCSR. Furthermore, CSI demonstrates a significant partial mediating role between SA and SCSR, while IG partially mediates the relationship between SAC and SCSR. The results highlight the importance of accountability‐oriented governance mechanisms and socially innovative approaches in strengthening SCSR practices. This study provides important implications for policymakers, regulators, and corporate managers seeking to strengthen CSR governance frameworks, improve stakeholder trust, and align corporate practices with broader sustainable development objectives. The study also contributes to CSR literature by integrating SA, SAC, CSI, and IG within an integrated empirical framework in an emerging economy context.

title: Manufacturing Enterprises' Digital Asset Value Evaluation Based on Multi-period Excess Return Method and Case Analysis
summary: Data assets have become strategic resources for manufacturing enterprises due to digital transformation, but most remain off-balance-sheet, challenging stakeholders to evaluate their true value. Traditional methods like market and cost approaches fail to capture the dynamic nature of data assets, while the income approach still has limitations in predicting future earnings and discount rates. This work integrates the Multi-Period Excess Return Method (MPEEM) with the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) to accurately assess the value of data assets. The MPEEM isolates excess returns from data assets, and AHP separates the contribution of off-balance-sheet assets. Empirical analysis of Midea Group, BYD and Xiaomi shows that data assets significantly contribute to enterprise value, with core drivers including smart manufacturing data, consumer behavior analyses, and supply chain optimization data. This paper provides a robust framework for valuing data assets, supporting strategic decision-making and regulatory compliance in the manufacturing sector.

title: ETDP: a high-performance transportation delay prediction framework with explanations for supply chains
summary: Purpose This work aims to develop a transportation delay prediction framework to improve prediction performance while providing explanations for its predictions. Design/methodology/approach An ETDP (high-performance Transportation Delay Prediction Framework with Explanations) for supply chains is proposed, in which we design an LGFT (Local-Global Fusion Transformer) model for high-performance prediction, and integrate LGFT with SHAP to explain its predictions. LGFT captures local feature interaction patterns via 1D CNN and global nonlinear relationships via an MLP, which are then fused through a Transformer Encoder to model long-range contextual dependencies. Integrated with SHAP, ETDP formalizes a three-level explanation mechanism that can analyze global feature importance, key feature dependency, and instance-level attribution. Findings The ETDP framework is evaluated on three public supply chain datasets covering binary delay prediction, last-mile logistics, and five-class supply chain risk classification. On DataCo, ETDP achieves the highest precision and remains competitive across the other evaluation indicators. On India, it obtains the best recall, F1-score, and MCC in the held-out test evaluation. On Mendeley, it reaches the best accuracy, recall, MCC, and lowest FNR, while remaining descriptively close to XGBoost in F1-score, though below it in precision and probability-ranking metrics. Repeated-run analyses show statistically supported improvements over several representative baselines, although ETDP does not uniformly dominate every model and metric. Originality/value ETDP is a useful combination of predictive modeling and post hoc explainability for transportation delay prediction. Fusing local and global features, it contributes a high-performance prediction model. Integrating with SHAP, it provides a supply-chain-oriented three-level explanation workflow. It can support both early delay-risk sensing and more targeted intervention prioritization, such as strategic optimization, context-specific risk mitigation and specific order diagnostics. title: The Impact of Green Accounting and Corporate Social Responsibility Implementation on Company Values
summary: This study is entitled The Effect of Green Accounting Implementation and Corporate Social Responsibility on Firm Value. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the role of green accounting implementation and corporate social responsibility disclosure in influencing firm value in energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022-2024 period. The research problem focuses on whether these two variables have a significant effect on firm value. This study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from annual reports and sustainability reports. The sample was selected using the purposive sampling method, resulting in 11 companies with a total of 33 observation units. Data processing and analysis were conducted using panel data regression with the assistance of the EViews application. The results indicate that the implementation of green accounting has a positive and significant effect on firm value, reflecting that transparency related to environmental costs and activities can enhance investor confidence. In contrast, corporate social responsibility shows a negative and significant effect on firm value, suggesting that CSR disclosure has not yet been fully perceived as providing direct economic benefits by investors in the energy sector. This study is expected to contribute to the development of environmental accounting literature and serve as a reference for companies and investors in decision-making processes.

title: The Impact of Local Government ESG Performance on Foreign Direct Investment
summary: In the complex and ever-changing international economic environment, stabilizing existing foreign investment and promoting new inflows are key priorities for government administrations. The sustainable development philosophy embodied in ESG (Environment, Social Responsibility and Governance) practices provides entities with sufficient competitiveness and attracts the attention of international investors. Using panel data of 31 provinces in China from 2015 to 2020, this study employs a two-way fixed-effects model to examine the impact of local government ESG performance on FDI (foreign direct investment). The results indicate that good ESG performance significantly enhances foreign investment inflows and the mechanism test confirmed that optimizing the business environment and improving total factor productivity are crucial channels through which ESG practices attract foreign investment. Further analysis revealed that the positive effect of ESG performance on stabilizing foreign investment is more pronounced in regions with low resource dependence, and a developed digital economy environment amplifies the positive impact of ESG activities on foreign investment. However, ESG practices widen the FDI gap across regions, exhibiting a distinct “Matthew effect”. Consequently, this paper proposes several policy recommendations, such as improving local government ESG information disclosure and evaluation systems, enhancing ESG performance to create locational advantages, and formulating strategic plans tailored to local conditions.

title: The Evolution of GSS+ Bond Research following the Sustainability-Linked Bond Principles: A Bibliometric Analysis, 2021-2025
summary: Climate change and sustainability challenges have accelerated innovation in debt financing, especially through green bonds, social bonds, sustainability bonds and sustainability-linked bonds, collectively referred to as GSS+ bonds. This study reviews the development of GSS+ bonds research by combining bibliometric analysis and content analysis. Based on 152 English language articles indexed in Scopus from 2021 to 2025, the study uses Bibliometrix to conduct performance analysis and VOSviewer to science mapping, including publication trends, citation patterns, leading countries, institutions, journals, co-authorship networks, bibliographic coupling, co-citation analysis and three-field plot mapping. The results show that GSS+ bond research has expanded rapidly, with an annual growth rate of 59.67%, reflecting increasing academic attention to sustainable debt instruments. China, the United Kingdom, Italy, the United States, Germany and India are the most productive countries. The intellectual structure of the field remains strongly centered on green bonds, particularly pricing, greenium, issuer characteristics, ESG performance and climate finance. However, current academic research rarely focuses on social bonds, sustainability bonds and sustainability-linked bonds. Based on the findings of this paper, GSS+ bond studies are still new and incomplete. More research is needed on relevant rules, product credibility, impact evaluation and how these instruments can be used in emerging markets.

title: DOES CHIEF AUDIT EXECUTIVE TENURE AFFECT CEO OVERCONFIDENCE IN REAL EARNINGS MANAGEMENT?
summary: CEO overconfidence tends to make high-risk decisions, including engaging in real earnings management (REM); however, the role of Chief Audit Executive (CAE) tenure as a governance mechanism that may moderate this relationship remains underexplored. This study aims at examining the effect of CEO overconfidence on REM and the moderating role of CAE tenure in this relationship. The sample consists of manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2012–2019 period and was analyzed using a fixed-effects panel data regression model. The results showed that CEO overconfidence has a positive effect on REM, and longer CAE tenure effectively reduces REM practices. However, CAE tenure did not moderate the relationship between CEO overconfidence and REM. This study contributed by emphasizing the importance of considering CEO personality traits and CAE tenure length in formulating effective corporate governance policies.

title: Green Factory Certification and Corporate Green Innovation: Incremental Optimization or Track Transformation?—Evidence from Chinese Manufacturing Firms
summary: This study focuses on the national-level green factory certification program. Drawing on panel data of Chinese A-share listed manufacturing firms from 2004 to 2024 and employing a difference-in-differences (DID) approach, it investigates the impact of green factory certification on corporate green innovation and examines the underlying mechanisms, with the aim of providing empirical support and policy insights for the green transformation of the manufacturing sector. The findings are as follows. First, inclusion in the green factory list promotes both radical and incremental green innovation. However, firms show a stronger inclination toward deepening exploration within their existing knowledge base, as evidenced by an increase in patent output. Meanwhile, knowledge recombination exhibits a certain degree of concentration. Second, green factory certification significantly stimulates green innovation in traditional industries and non-heavily polluting sectors, but has no significant effect on firms in high-technology industries or heavily polluting sectors. Third, green factory certification facilitates corporate green innovation through two channels: internal drivers and external support. On the one hand, it strengthens environmental investment and fosters green awareness; on the other hand, it expands financing channels and attracts green capital.

title: The Rise of Carbon Finance: A Bibliometric Perspective
summary: ABSTRACT Carbon finance has emerged as a critical mechanism for mobilizing capital toward climate change mitigation and supporting the transition to low‐carbon economies. However, its intellectual development remains fragmented across environmental economics, financial economics, sustainability, and climate policy. This study provides a comprehensive bibliometric assessment of carbon finance research, examining its growth trajectory, intellectual structure, collaboration patterns, thematic evolution, and emerging research frontiers. Using 1610 Scopus‐indexed publications from 1993 to 2026, the study integrates performance analysis, citation impact, science mapping, network analysis, thematic visualization, Bradford's law, Lotka's law, journal quality indicators, and life cycle analysis. The findings reveal substantial growth, particularly following the Paris Agreement, alongside a concentrated intellectual structure in which China leads publication productivity, whereas the United States, the United Kingdom, and Japan demonstrate strong citation influence. Collaboration networks indicate increasing internationalization, although research remains concentrated among a limited number of authors and institutions. Thematic evolution demonstrates a shift from carbon markets, emissions trading, and environmental regulation toward green finance, sustainable investment, climate‐related financial risk, renewable‐energy financing, ESG integration, and digital finance. The study contributes by extending the temporal coverage of previous bibliometric reviews, integrating multiple analytical approaches, and explicitly tracing the progressive financialization of carbon finance. It reconciles divergent patterns in productivity, citation influence, collaboration, and development across countries and disciplines. By identifying structural patterns, emerging themes, and underexplored research frontiers, the study provides an evidence‐based agenda for future research and informs policymakers, standard‐setters, investors, and practitioners seeking to advance sustainable financial systems and climate transition strategies.

title: The Impact of the Rural Digital Economy on Ecological Product Value Conversion Efficiency from the Perspective of Production–Living–Ecological Functions
summary: The rapid expansion of the rural digital economy (RDE) has introduced new opportunities for enhancing ecological product value conversion efficiency (EPVCE), yet the mechanisms underlying this relationship remain insufficiently understood. Based on provincial panel data from 31 Chinese provinces during 2010–2019, this study constructs an RDE index system and evaluates EPVCE using a super-efficiency slack-based measure (SBM) model. Two-way fixed-effects models, bootstrap mediation analysis, heterogeneity tests, and spatial Durbin models are employed to examine the impact of RDE on EPVCE and explore the underlying mechanisms. The findings reveal that (1) RDE is significantly and positively associated with EPVCE, and this finding remains robust to alternative model specifications and variable measures, controls for climatic factors, a one-period lag of RDE, and an instrumental-variable approach; (2) production, living, and ecological functions constitute key transmission channels, with the ecological function exhibiting a relatively larger indirect effect; (3) the positive relationship is more pronounced in eastern China and non-resource-based provinces, indicating substantial heterogeneity; and (4) spatial analysis reveals that the relationship is primarily characterized by local effects rather than spatial spillovers. From a rural multifunctionality perspective, this study extends research on the RDE–EPVCE nexus and provides empirical evidence for coordinating rural digital transformation with ecological value realization.
