title: Towards an integrated framework for digital transformation in Moroccan higher education
summary: Digital transformation of public universities in developing countries raises a number of difficulties that relate to their institutions' characteristics and strategies. In Morocco, these challenges are amplified by structural, organizational, and technological limitations that hinder the deployment of comprehensive digital initiatives. Despite the presence of a wide range of DX Frameworks in literature, very few are adapted to the specific context of higher education institutions. This study follows a Design Science Research approach combining a systematic literature review with structured expert validation. The systematic literature review investigates how existing DX frameworks integrate critical success factors and to what extent they address the complex, multidimensional nature of transformation in higher education. Through this review, we selected and analyzed 22 relevant frameworks covering various sectors. This analysis reveals that most existing frameworks emphasize technology and strategy but often overlook essential dimensions such as change management, governance, evaluation or data integration. Based on these insights, we propose a holistic DX framework for Moroccan Public Universities (MPU). We structured our framework around seven interdependent dimensions: strategy & Governance, Organization & Processes, Technologies & Infrastructures, Human Capital & Organizational Culture & Change management, Pedagogy & Research, and Data & Evaluation & Continuous improvement. Each dimension is supported by sub-dimensions and interrelations that guide institutions through a structured and adaptive transformation process. We submitted the proposed framework to expert validation through the Content Validity Index (CVI) methodology, involving a panel of 22 domain Experts. Results confirmed strong content validity, with an overall S-CVI/Ave of 0.88 and seven of eight items validated above the operational threshold, particular regarding the framework's coherence, completeness and originality. Expert feedback also informed ten contextual refinements addressing financial sustainability, institutional continuity, and governance coordination. The proposed Framework aims to support decision-makers in planning, implementing, and sustaining digital initiatives in alignment with institutional realities and stakeholder expectations.

title: The Impact Mechanisms of the Carbon Emissions Trading Pilot Policy on Corporate ESG Performance: A Moderated Mediation Analysis
summary: As a key market-based policy instrument for promoting the low-carbon transition, the carbon emissions trading pilot policy is expected to encourage enterprises to strengthen environmental protection, fulfill social responsibilities, and improve their environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. Using data on Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2021, this study employs a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) model to examine the impact of the carbon emissions trading pilot policy on corporate ESG performance and its underlying mechanisms. Corporate green technological innovation is introduced as the mediating variable, while media attention and the strength of intellectual property protection are incorporated as moderating variables. The results show that: (1) The carbon emissions trading pilot policy significantly improves corporate ESG performance, and this effect is more pronounced among non-heavily polluting firms, firms in non-high-tech industries, and firms located in regions with lower levels of fiscal revenue; (2) The policy promotes corporate green technological innovation, which in turn improves corporate ESG performance; and (3) Media attention and the strength of intellectual property protection positively moderate the relationship between the carbon emissions trading pilot policy and corporate green technological innovation, thereby strengthening the mediating effect of green technological innovation.

title: Digital transformation and corporate ESG performance: green technological innovation, market concentration, and the twin transformation perspective
summary: This study examines whether, how, and under what market-structure conditions corporate digital transformation improves environmental, social, and governance (ESG) performance. Building on the twin green and digital transformation perspective, this study conceptualizes digital transformation as a dynamic green digital capability rather than merely the adoption of digital technologies. By integrating the Natural Resource-Based View, Stakeholder Theory, and the Porter Hypothesis, we develop a framework in which digital transformation enhances ESG performance by strengthening firms’ data-driven sustainability capabilities and enabling green technological innovation. Using panel data from Chinese A-share listed firms from 2009 to 2023, we find that digital transformation is positively associated with ESG performance, measured by Huazheng ESG ratings. Green technological innovation mediates this relationship, and the empirical results indicate that the mediation is partial and economically modest, suggesting that green innovation is only one mechanism within a broader set of digitalization–ESG channels. Market concentration strengthens the positive effect of digital transformation on ESG performance, indicating that firms in more concentrated industries are better able to appropriate returns from long-term digital and sustainability investments. Additional heterogeneity analyses show that the positive effect of digital transformation is observed across regions and ownership types. In pollution-related industry subsamples, the effect is significant among non-high-polluting firms but not statistically significant among high-polluting firms; however, the between-group difference is not statistically significant. This study contributes to the literature by clarifying the innovation mechanism and market-structure boundary condition through which digital transformation supports comprehensive ESG improvement. The findings suggest that the ESG value of digital transformation depends not only on whether firms adopt digital technologies, but also on whether they develop dynamic green digital capabilities and operate in market environments that support long-term sustainability investment.

title: Do ESG disclosures mediate the relationship between audit committee characteristics and audit quality? Evidence from the listed banks of Bangladesh
summary: In recent years, the sustainability and effectiveness of corporate governance mechanisms have revealed a growing trend toward measuring the overall firm's operational and managerial efficiency. The study aims to explore the influence of Audit Committee (AC) characteristics as measures of corporate governance and their effects on audit quality, as well as whether Environmental, Social, and Governance Disclosures (ESGD) have any relationship with audit quality in this regard. The study was conducted in the banking industry of Bangladesh based on an analysis of publicly available reports from 2019 to 2025. A quantitative research approach using the POLS method was employed, with audit quality proxied by Audit Fees (AF). The main factors associated with AC composition were included as independent variables. The bootstrap technique was adopted to analyze whether ESGD mediates the relationship. The findings of this study show a significantly positive relationship between AC size, independence, and ACGD and audit quality. The study contributes to the literature by identifying ESGD as a significant mediating mechanism between ACGD and audit quality, as ACGD is the only AC characteristic that improves audit quality through enhanced ESGD. Policymakers should prioritize inclusive and gender-diversified governance mechanisms. Focus should be given to ESG-based operations and standardized reporting tactics. A lack of diversification in industry and economic circumstances may limit the generalizability of the findings. Audit quality may also be influenced by factors other than audit fees.

title: Does ESG really create value? Evidence from profitability, dividend policy, and CSR in Islamic banking
summary: Purpose This study aims to analyze the influence of profitability, corporate social responsibility (CSR) and dividend policy on the value of Sharia Bank companies with Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) performance as a mediation variable. Design/methodology/approach The method used in this study is Structural Equation Modeling with Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) multiple linear regression. The data used were obtained from the company’s annual report, selected through purposive sampling. Findings The analysis indicates that profitability and dividend policy have a positive, statistically significant impact on the company’s value. However, profitability can undermine ESG considerations, whereas a dividend policy can enhance ESG. Additionally, ESG has been shown to have a positive, significant effect on a company’s value. Another important finding is that ESG plays a significant mediating role in the relationship between profitability and dividend policy on company value. This suggests that the greater a company’s attention to ESG factors, the greater the impact on its value. Research limitations/implications This research suggests that companies must strike a balance between financial performance and sustainability commitments to create more optimal long-term value. ESG can be a crucial strategy for building a reputation and enhancing investor confidence. Originality/value The researchers used a more representative sample of 12 Islamic banks in Indonesia, given the industry’s diverse characteristics and regulations. Research that specifically examines the role of ESG as a mediating variable in Islamic banking. The researcher examines how dividend policies affect the ESG performance of Islamic banks, given the importance of social and environmental factors in their operations. Researchers used more complex statistical methods, such as OLS in SPSS or panel data analysis, to analyze the relationships between variables in more depth. With this, it is hoped that a more comprehensive understanding of the factors that affect the value of Islamic bank companies, as well as the role of ESG in this context, can be obtained.

title: Facing the Retail Apocalypse: Majid Al Futtaim’s Digital Transformation (A)
summary: In just a few decades Majid Al Futtaim (“the Group”) had established an empire boasting major shopping malls, successful retail chains and popular entertainment centres across the Middle East, Asia, and North Africa (MENA) region. By 2020, however, its competitive landscape was changing fast, with diverse players striving to define the future of retail. Traditional powerhouses such as Walmart, with their extensive physical presences, and tech titans such as Amazon, rich with consumer data and technological prowess, were changing the way consumers shopped and interacted with brands. Whose business model would triumph in the dynamic environment of the Middle East? And how should traditional companies such as Majid Al Futtaim respond to the new landscape?

title: Value-Up Initiatives as a Strategy for Corporate Governance and Capital Market Development: Lessons from Asia
summary: Over the past several years, a new form of corporate governance and capital market intervention has spread across Asia. Beginning with Malaysia and gaining international prominence following the Tokyo Stock Exchange’s 2023 initiative, several Asian jurisdictions, including Korea, Taiwan, Mainland China, Thailand and Singapore have adopted what this article broadly refers to as “value-up initiatives.” We provide a comparative assessment of these initiatives, emphasising their potential and limitations as a strategy for corporate governance and capital market development. The article starts by explaining why value-up initiatives have emerged so prominently in Asia and how they have been designed differently across the region. By encouraging boards to confront questions of capital allocation and valuation while improving the information available to investors, we argue that value-up initiatives can serve as a valuable corporate governance tool. Their effectiveness, however, depends on the institutional and market environment in which they operate, and they should be understood as complements, rather than substitutes, for effective legal and enforcement mechanisms for protecting investors. The article concludes by explaining how the Asian experience with value-up initiatives can offer valuable lessons for jurisdictions seeking to strengthen corporate governance while contributing to the development of capital markets.

title: Design and validation of a measurement scale for digital transformation capabilities in agricultural settings
summary: Digital transformation is essential for strengthening agri-food systems in emerging economies. However, there is a lack of validated tools to assess both the capabilities and levels of digital maturity in agricultural production units. This research validates an instrument to measure Digital Transformation (DT) capabilities and levels of digital maturity in agricultural production units (APU) in an emerging economy. The instrument encompasses six dimensions: sensing, seizing and transforming capabilities, along with the stages of digital maturity, digitization, digitalization, and digital transformation. The validation process was developed in five stages, including theoretical foundation, item development, expert review, and exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses, applied to a sample of 68 potato farmers from south-central Chile. The final instrument consists of 32 items with promising psychometric properties; reliability and validity indicators met recommended thresholds across most dimensions, with a small number of exceptions discussed in the study. The results reveal that farmers widely recognize the value of digital technology and demonstrate a willingness to invest, despite being in early stages of digitalization, with widespread use of basic tools such as smartphones and messaging applications, but with limited adoption of more advanced technologies such as precision agriculture. This gap between perceived value and actual implementation highlights the role of structural barriers in rural contexts. This instrument offers researchers and policymakers a promising, albeit preliminary, tool to assess dynamic capabilities and digital maturity at the individual farmer level, representing an initial step toward diagnostic tools for digital transformation processes in this context.

title: ENHANCING THE ROLE OF ENTERPRISE VALUATION, CORPORATE GOVERNANCE, AND FINANCIAL TRANSPARENCY IN ATTRACTING FOREIGN INVESTMENT
summary: This study examines how enterprise valuation, corporate governance, and financial transparency jointly influence foreign investment attraction. It develops an integrated analytical framework combining discounted cash flow valuation, relative valuation, governance assessment, and disclosure quality. Uzbekistan provides the institutional context, supported by official enterprise statistics and national investment legislation. The analysis demonstrates that reliable valuation and transparent reporting can reduce information asymmetry, improve investor confidence, and strengthen access to international capital. The study proposes a practical framework for integrating financial, governance, and transparency indicators into investment-readiness assessments.

title: Digital Transformation of the Financial Model of a Global Technology Corporation: The Case of Microsoft
summary: The article is devoted to the analysis of the digital transformation of Microsoft's financial model under the company shifting from a licence- and product-centred logic towards a cloud-platform and AI-oriented architecture. The purpose of the study is to identify the mechanisms, through which cloud services, subscription monetisation, ecosystem integration, and artificial intelligence reshape the company’s revenue structure, operating leverage, capital intensity, and cash flows. The methodological basis is formed of the case method, systemic and comparative analysis, content analysis of corporate reporting and dynamic analysis of indicators for the fiscal years 2024–2026. It is established that revenue and operating income growth is accompanied by a sharp increase in capital inclusion of data processing and computing infrastructure. The research substantiates that the financial effect of Microsoft's digital transformation is awash with duplicity: recurring revenues and AI monetisation strengthen revenue resilience, while they increase capital intensity of the model. The practical significance of the research results may be used to assess digital strategies of large technology companies.

title: Regulatory Resilience: How Organisations Overcome Regulation‐Induced Resistance to Digital Transformation
summary: ABSTRACT Digital Transformation (DT) has become a strategic imperative for organisations to stay competitive. Yet, it often faces resistance. Regulation is often argued to be one source of resistance. However, regulation can also drive transformation: its role is multifaceted and especially its management in the context of DT is underexplored. Drawing on an empirical case study of an organisation undergoing large‐scale DT in a highly regulated industry, we conceptualise Regulatory Resilience as a socio‐technical organisational capability that enables organisations to dynamically respond to regulation‐induced resistance while leveraging regulatory forces for DT. Our findings reveal five distinct mechanisms through which Regulatory Resilience operates to mitigate the effects of both stable and volatile regulation and transform regulatory pressure into a capability‐building process. This study contributes to Information Systems research by challenging the view of regulation as a static, exogenous hurdle, repositioning it instead as a constitutive force that organisations actively manage through sociotechnical means. By identifying the specific mechanisms through which organisations reconcile regulatory pressures with innovation, we advance theory on the interrelated dynamics of resistance and resilience showing that Regulatory Resilience not only enables DT but is itself strengthened by DT's technological and organisational conditions, requiring organisations to deliberately cultivate it to sustain transformation.

title: Implementasi Good Corporate Governance sebagai Strategi Peningkatan Daya Saing Perusahaan Lokal di Kota Makassar
summary: Persaingan usaha yang semakin ketat menuntut perusahaan menerapkan tata kelola yang baik (good corporate governance/GCG) untuk menjaga keberlangsungan dan daya saing, termasuk perusahaan lokal di Kota Makassar. Penelitian ini bertujuan mendeskripsikan implementasi prinsip GCG (transparansi, akuntabilitas, responsibilitas, independensi, dan kewajaran), mengidentifikasi faktor pendukung dan penghambat, serta menelaah kaitannya dengan daya saing menurut pandangan informan. Pendekatan kualitatif deskriptif digunakan pada PT Ichiba Medical Indonesia, distributor alat kesehatan laboratorium di Kota Makassar. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara mendalam, observasi, dan dokumentasi dengan informan terpilih secara purposive sampling, lalu dianalisis melalui pengumpulan, reduksi, penyajian data, dan penarikan kesimpulan, serta diuji keabsahannya melalui triangulasi teknik. Hasil menunjukkan perusahaan menerapkan GCG sejak rekrutmen karyawan selaras visi-misi, mematuhi regulasi CDAKB, dan mengelola keuangan secara transparan. Dukungan pengurus berupa pelatihan dan perhatian pada kesejahteraan karyawan menjadi faktor pendukung, sedangkan faktor penghambat internal belum teridentifikasi. Menghadapi persaingan dengan distributor lokal dan produk Tiongkok, perusahaan bersaing melalui kualitas produk dan layanan purnajual, bukan harga. Menurut narasumber, penerapan GCG berkaitan dengan peningkatan penjualan, kepercayaan pelanggan, dan kepercayaan sektor permodalan. Temuan ini mengindikasikan GCG berpotensi menjadi strategi peningkatan daya saing, tetapi masih bersifat persepsi pada satu perusahaan sehingga belum dapat digeneralisasi.

title: Enterprise Architecture in Higher Education for Digital Transformation: An Integrative Review for Fragile Contexts with Application to Yemen
summary: Background Enterprise Architecture (EA) is a crucial facilitator for the digital transformation of organizations; however, its implementation in the higher education sector of fragile states is still insufficiently studied. This gap makes it harder for policymakers and higher education leaders in countries like Yemen to carry out structured, sector-wide modernization. Methods This study utilizes a systematic integrative review methodology, adhering to PRISMA principles. We synthesized and analyzed 30 peer-reviewed articles and high-credibility reports published between 2010 and June 2025 to identify transferable EA frameworks, governance models, and implementation strategies pertinent to resource-constrained contexts in higher education. Results Our analysis confirms that the TOGAF framework is the most widely used, but it also indicates that successful public sector implementations depend on hybrid adaptations and federated governance models to attain a balance between central policy and institutional autonomy. The most important things that lead to success are strong executive sponsorship and a phased, pilot-led implementation. The primary problems are lack of resources and resistance from within the organization. The results also show a clear link between EA outcomes, such as improved efficiency and resilience, and the main goals of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Conclusions This review expands EA theory into the inadequately explored area of public administration in fragile contexts. In practice, it provides Yemen with a new, evidence-based, phased implementation pathway. This pathway affords higher education sector leaders a real policy and management tool to help them build strong and useful digital ecosystems in tough places.

title: From digital transformation to environmental value: the role of green digital culture and circular economy adoption
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how green digital culture (GDC) and digital sustainability (DS) function as dynamic organizational capabilities that enable circular economy (CE) practices and enhance sustainable environmental practices among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Positioned within the broader context of Asia–Gulf economic integration and vision-driven sustainability reforms, the study explores how emerging Asian markets translate digital transformation into environmental value. Design/methodology/approach Grounded in dynamic capabilities theory and stakeholder theory, data were collected from 322 SME managers and decision-makers across the UAE using a structured survey instrument. The proposed model was tested using partial least squares structural equation modeling. Findings The results demonstrate that green digital culture (GDC) and DS significantly enhance sustainable environmental practices. DS exerts a particularly strong influence on CE adoption. CE practices partially mediate the relationship between digitally enabled capabilities and environmental practices, illustrating how SMEs operationalize sustainability through digitally supported circular strategies under evolving regulatory and stakeholder pressures. Research limitations/implications The study is based on cross-sectional data from a single emerging economy. Future research should undertake longitudinal and multi-country Asian comparisons to examine how institutional environments and policy ambition moderate digital–sustainability linkages. Practical implications The findings provide actionable insights for SME leaders and policymakers across Asia seeking to align digital transformation agendas with CE transitions. Strengthening DS capabilities and embedding GDC can accelerate environmentally responsible growth in resource-constrained emerging markets. Social implications By supporting SME-led sustainability transitions, digitally enabled circular practices can contribute to regional environmental resilience and advance national vision-driven sustainability commitments across Asia. Originality/value This study advances Asia business scholarship by explaining how digital transformation capabilities are converted into environmental performance through CE mechanisms in emerging Asian markets undergoing institutional and policy reform.

title: Institutional Adaptation in the Digital Transformation of Local Government Financial Governance: A Case Study of Balangan Regency
summary: Digital transformation in local government financial governance involves more than changes in technology and administrative mechanisms; it also requires institutional adjustments to ensure that such changes can be implemented and sustained over time. This study aims to analyze institutional adaptation in the digital transformation of local government financial governance in Balangan Regency, Indonesia. The study used a descriptive qualitative approach and collected data through interviews, observations, and document analysis. The study analyzed data interactively through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The analysis draws on institutional change and Problem-Driven Iterative Adaptation (PDIA), developed by Andrews, Pritchett, and Woolcock (2017), to examine institutional change and the development of adaptive capacity. The findings show that implementing SIPD/SIPD-RI, SIPANDA, the Cash Management System (CMS), SP2D Online, and non-cash transactions has prompted adjustments to regulations and work procedures, staff capacity, interorganizational coordination, infrastructure, and oversight mechanisms. Adaptation has occurred through a gradual, iterative process in which implementation challenges serve as learning opportunities that inform subsequent institutional adjustments. The findings indicate that institutional adaptation links digital transformation with the sustainability of changes in local government financial governance. The study implies that digital transformation policies should strengthen institutional learning, adaptive capacity, and organizational support alongside technological adoption.

title: Supplier ESG Activities and Trust Formation in Sustainable B2B Supply Chains: A Dyadic Perspective
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) activities have become increasingly important in sustainable supply chain management, yet limited research has examined how supplier ESG engagement influences interfirm trust and long‐term buyer–supplier relationships in B2B contexts. Drawing on 205 matched supplier–buyer dyads in South Korea, this study examines associations among supplier ESG activities, buyers' perceptions of warmth and competence, benevolence‐based and credibility‐based trust, long‐term orientation and relationship extendedness. The hypotheses were examined using covariance‐based structural equation modeling, supplemented by continuous moderation tests with heteroskedasticity‐robust standard errors and bootstrap confidence intervals. This study further examines buyer ESG awareness as a moderator of the associations between supplier ESG activities and relational perceptions. The findings show that environmental activities are positively associated with perceptions of warmth, whereas governance activities are positively associated with perceptions of competence. Both benevolence‐based and credibility‐based trust are positively associated with long‐term relational outcomes. The continuous moderation analysis identified one significant boundary condition: ESG awareness attenuated the association between supplier social activities and perceived warmth, supporting Hypothesis 8b. The remaining three moderation hypotheses were not supported. The study extends research on ESG‐related warmth and competence perceptions to B2B relationships by linking supplier‐reported activities with buyer‐reported perceptions, two dimensions of interfirm trust, and relational outcomes, while examining ESG awareness as a potential boundary condition. The findings identify cross‐sectional associations and do not establish a causal mediation process.

title: Turning strategy into employee adaptive performance: why empowering leadership matters in turbulent digital transformation
summary: Purpose This study examines why formal strategic planning does not always become employee action during digital transformation and environmental turbulence. It proposes that strategic plans are associated with stronger adaptive performance when perceived implementation is translated into empowering leadership and psychological empowerment. Design/methodology/approach Three-wave survey data from 1,000 employees in nine Chinese enterprises are analyzed using employee-level OLS models with organization fixed effects and HC3 standard errors, bootstrap estimates of the conditional indirect associations, and cluster-robust and random-forest sensitivity checks. Findings At the employee level, perceived strategic planning implementation is positively associated with empowering leadership, psychological empowerment and adaptive performance in sequence, and retains no detectable direct association with adaptive performance once the pathway is modeled. Digital transformation intensity strengthens the first two links, whereas environmental turbulence strengthens the final link. Practical implications Managers should convert strategic priorities into bounded decision rights, resources and feedback rather than relying on communication alone: creating room for local experimentation under intensive digital change, and shortening approval chains under turbulence. Originality/value Rather than introducing a new construct, the study extends existing strategic leadership and empowerment research contextually. Its contribution is stage specificity: digital transformation intensifies translation and internalization, whereas environmental turbulence intensifies enactment, locating two distinct failure points in strategy execution.

title: Digitalization, Energy Use, and Carbon Emission Efficiency: Testing the Digital Paradox
summary: The rapid expansion of digital technologies is reshaping economic and energy systems, but its implications for carbon efficiency remain uncertain. This study examines whether digitalization improves carbon emission efficiency (CEE), investigates the mediating role of green innovation, and tests whether ICTI conditions the digitalization–CEE relationship. Using a panel of 53 economies with varying energy intensities over 2002–2022, CEE is estimated through the Super-Efficiency Slack-Based Measure (SE-SBM), which incorporates energy consumption and carbon dioxide emissions as environmental inputs and undesirable outputs, respectively. Panel-corrected standard errors, Pooled Mean Group, System-GMM, and Driscoll–Kraay estimators are employed for robust inference. The results show that digitalization significantly reduces CEE (β = −0.1677), indicating that the energy and carbon pressures associated with expanding DII outweigh initial efficiency gains. In particular, the findings suggest that rising electricity and energy demand associated with data centers, communication networks, and ICT-intensive activities can intensify environmental pressure. Green innovation positively improves CEE (β = 0.0089) and partially mediates the adverse effect of digitalization, although digitalization itself significantly reduces green innovation (β = −0.0820). Moreover, the digitalization-ICTI interaction is negative and significant (β = −0.6864), indicating that higher ICTI amplifies the adverse environmental effect of digital expansion. Institutional quality improves CEE, whereas a resource-intensive industrial structure reduces it. A U-shaped relationship between economic growth and CEE is also confirmed. The findings highlight the need for energy-efficient DII, efficient ICT utilization, green innovation, stronger institutions, and sustainable industrial transformation to reconcile digital development with environmental sustainability.

title: Development of a transactional multifactor econometric platform for the integral assessment of the fundamental value of a public energy corporation in the context of geo-economic fragmentation, sanctions regimes and stochastic volatility of commodity markets on the strategic planning horizon of 2027-2030.
summary: In the context of modern geo-economic turbulence, characterized by the escalation of sanctions restrictions, the structural transformation of global energy markets, the monetary restriction of leading central banks and the increasing stochasticity of price indicators for hydrocarbons, traditional paradigms for assessing the investment attractiveness of public companies in the oil and gas sector demonstrate systemic insufficiency. This study is devoted to the development of a comprehensive transactional methodology that integrates quantitative analysis of a wide range of endogenous and exogenous determinants of corporate value, from global price targets and macroeconomic aggregates to indicators of corporate governance, technological sovereignty, ESG factors and force majeure. Using an ensemble of advanced machine learning algorithms, including gradient boosting on decision trees, recurrent neural network architectures with a selective attention mechanism and regularized regression models with an elastic network, a multifactorial model has been built that allows quantitative decomposition of the contribution of each factor to the dynamics of market capitalization and identification of key cost drivers in various phases of the economic cycle. Based on the identified correlation and regression dependencies, an end-to–end predictive platform has been developed that converges three classical assessment approaches – multiplier, cash flow discounting, and dividend discounting - each of which is modified through dynamic ML adaptation of key parameters to the current macroeconomic and geopolitical environment, taking into account nonlinear effects, interfacial interactions, and time lags. The final block of the methodological pipeline includes a multivariate scenario analysis with the generation of five development trajectories – from extremely pessimistic to extremely optimistic - based on the joint variation of key external parameters, the construction of probabilistic confidence intervals using multidimensional logit transformation and filtering of the estimates obtained through multi-technical indicators, dividend protection and qualitative adjustments that take into account premiums for ESG rating, corporate governance and technological sovereignty. Practical testing of the developed toolkit on a retrospective dashboard for 2010-2026 has allowed us to determine a reasonable fair value price range structured across five investment zones – from aggressive accumulation to full profit–taking - which provides institutional and private investors with a clear navigational tool for decision-making in the face of fundamental uncertainty. The proposed methodology, due to its modular architecture, multifactor saturation and the possibility of regular recalibration based on updated data, is a universal platform for evaluating companies in the commodity sector in turbulent economic conditions and can serve as a theoretical and methodological basis for further research in the field of financial engineering and investment analysis.

title: Leveraging FinTech to Combat Protection Fees in Township Economies: Advancing Sustainable Economic Resilience Through Digital Payment Solutions
summary: Criminal extortion and protection fees have emerged as significant threats to the sustainability of township businesses in South Africa, undermining entrepreneurship, formalisation, investment, and local economic development. This study examines how FinTech and complementary digital technologies may reduce the vulnerabilities associated with cash-based transactions while supporting longer-term economic resilience. It presents a qualitative systematic literature review of evidence published between 2016 and 2026, drawn from Scopus, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and supplemented by AI-assisted searching. The search yielded 8704 records, of which 114 were assessed in full-text and 48 were included in the final synthesis. The findings indicate that mobile money, digital payments, and blockchain-enabled systems may reduce cash dependency, improve transaction transparency and security, and strengthen financial participation. Complementary digital reporting and community platforms may further support collective responses to extortion. The review also identified a potential longer-term pathway from digital transaction records to greater financial visibility and formal financial participation; however, digital adoption does not automatically produce access to credit or eliminate extortion. Diffusion of innovation theory is used to explain how relative advantages, compatibility, complexity, trialability, and observability shape adoption. The study contributes to a governance-oriented FinTech framework in which digital payment adoption is understood as both a financial inclusion mechanism and a potential risk-reduction and formalisation pathway that could influence the sustainability of businesses. Its effectiveness depends on digital literacy, affordable infrastructure, institutional trust, enabling regulation, and multi-stakeholder collaboration.

title: Resource Dependence and Uneven Green Innovation Responses to Green Finance: Evidence from China’s Initial Pilot Cohort
summary: Green finance reforms may elicit different green invention responses across places with different inherited production structures. We examine the green finance reform and innovation pilot zones using a panel of 282 Chinese prefecture-level cities (2011–2024), with the main comparison drawn from the eight cities in the initial treatment cohort (three resource-based and five non-resource-based). Full-sample staggered-treatment estimators yield mixed diagnostics, motivating a common-timing difference-in-difference-in-differences design. The estimated resource–response differential is −0.657 log points (Webb wild-cluster p = 0.0049); the resource-city marginal response is imprecisely estimated rather than established as zero. The differential remains negative under province-by-year effects, alternative controls, and mapped-area exclusions, although saturated baseline-characteristic adjustments reduce its precision. Conventional and Webb pre-treatment tests disagree. An HonestDiD analysis shows that the confidence interval includes zero under modest departures from parallel trends, limiting a strong causal interpretation. Synthetic difference-in-differences fits pre-policy outcomes more closely in non-resource-based than resource-based cities. Pre-reform firm data indicate more concentrated brown-industry assets in resource-based cities but do not establish a mechanism. The results provide suggestive initial-cohort evidence of uneven responses to pilot designation, not direct evidence that green finance volumes or capability redeployment mediated the difference.

title: When Does ESG Misconduct Cost the CEO ? Sustainability Orientation and Compensation Outcomes Across European Firms
summary: ABSTRACT This study provides new evidence on when environmental, social, and governance (ESG) controversies are associated with adverse CEO compensation outcomes and whether these consequences depend on firms' prior ESG orientation. Using 9131 firm‐year observations from listed firms in 11 European countries over 2015–2023, we examine the associations between ESG performance, controversy exposure, and CEO total compensation. The results show that ESG performance is positively associated with CEO compensation, whereas controversy exposure is negatively associated with compensation on average. Importantly, the adverse controversy–compensation association strengthens as ESG performance increases and is concentrated among firms with stronger prior ESG performance. These findings are robust to firm fixed effects, lagged ESG, dynamic‐panel GMM, propensity score matching, a continuous controversy measure, and event‐time analysis. The results are consistent with an expectations‐violation or corporate‐hypocrisy interpretation rather than an insurance‐based view of prior ESG reputation and highlight the importance of credible ex‐post accountability in sustainability‐related executive compensation.

title: REVISÃO SISTEMÁTICA SOBRE A RELAÇÃO ENTRE PRÁTICAS DE GESTÃO LOCAL-SUSTENTÁVEL E A SAÚDE MENTAL DE TRABALHADORES EM TELETRABALHO
summary: A expansão do teletrabalho, intensificada a partir da pandemia da COVID-19, trouxe implicações significativas para a saúde mental dos trabalhadores, evidenciando a necessidade de práticas organizacionais sustentáveis voltadas ao bem-estar psicológico. Neste contexto, o presente estudo teve como objetivo analisar as evidências científicas disponíveis acerca da relação entre práticas de gestão local-sustentável, orientadas pelos princípios do ESG, e a saúde mental de trabalhadores em regime de teletrabalho. Metodologicamente, realizou-se uma revisão bibliográfica sistemática, de natureza exploratória e descritiva, conduzida conforme o protocolo PRISMA 2020. Os resultados indicam que a saúde mental dos teletrabalhadores é fortemente influenciada pela qualidade das práticas de gestão sustentável, sendo o estresse identificado como mediador central entre as condições de trabalho remoto e os desfechos psicossociais. Evidenciam-se, como principais riscos, a sobrecarga digital, a fadiga decorrente de reuniões virtuais, o isolamento social e o borramento das fronteiras entre vida pessoal e profissional. Em contrapartida, práticas de ESG efetivamente implementadas, como suporte organizacional, liderança orientada por propósito e políticas de cuidado com o trabalhador, atuam como fatores protetivos da saúde mental. Conclui-se que a saúde mental no teletrabalho configura-se como um indicador relevante da gestão local-sustentável, exigindo que as práticas de ESG se materializem em ações organizacionais contínuas e integradas, capazes de mitigar riscos psicossociais e promover ambientes de trabalho mais saudáveis e sustentáveis.

title: From Artificial Intelligence to Circularity: How Finance, Governance, and Risk Shape Circular Economy Performance in G10 Countries
summary: ABSTRACT The present research focuses on evaluating the determinants of the performance of the circular economy in G10 countries (Belgium, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and the United States) throughout the years 2000–2023 by incorporating financial, technological, institutional, macroeconomic, and risk‐related aspects in one unified panel structure. The performance of a circular economy is assessed through a composite index named the Circular Economy Index (CEI), and Public Green Innovation Finance (GF), AI‐related industrial automation intensity (AI), Economic Risk (ER), Financial Risk (FR), Government Effectiveness (GOVS), Economic Growth (GDP), Geopolitical Risk (GR), and Environmental Technology (ET) are used as the explanatory variables. The analysis uses genuine panel econometric methods that consider cross‐sectional dependence, slope heterogeneity, mixed orders of integration, and long‐run cointegration, such as fixed‐effects regression with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and Panel FMOLS estimation. The findings indicate that AI and GDP have a strong and positive impact on CEI, which demonstrates the significance of automation intensity and the size of an economy in improving the performance of the circular economy in developed economies. Conversely, FR and GOVS are found to have a strong and negative correlation with CEI, showing that financial instability and forms of government could be a barrier to circular transformation. GF is statistically significant in the baseline model and selectively in FMOLS, but the other estimations (GR, ER, ET) are only significant in the baseline estimations and much less robust when other specifications are used. In general, according to the results, technological capability and economic growth are the key success factors of the circular economy performance in G10 countries, whereas financial risk and institutional orientation are the key constraining factors. The findings justify the policy actions that are in line with the Sustainable Development Goals, especially SDGs 8, 9, 12, 13, and 16.

title: The Conscious Capitalism Paradigm: A Comparative Analysis of Strategic Integrity and Financial Performance for a New Age Leadership of Peace and Sustainability
summary: This article examines the connection between conscious leadership practices and financial performance in a comparative study based on the Conscious Capitalism framework using a simulation. Based on modeled scenarios in the 3D-printed carbon fiber bicycle industry, the article uses the Conscious Scorecard and Balanced Scorecard to evaluate the environmental stewardship, human capital investment, community relations, health and wellness, and supply chain integrity of six companies. The results of the simulation indicate that purpose-oriented leadership practices could be linked to higher organizational resilience, whereas profit seems to be a by-product of developing a conscious culture (Bhaskar et al., 2023; Jum’a et al., 2024; Rodríguez-Aldana et al., 2024). Companies that had preinvested in staff welfare, environmental, and community relations showed better simulated recovery dynamics, and those that concentrated on short-term profits were unstable and had reputational risks. Such results add some preliminary knowledge to the Conscious Profit Matrix, suggesting that conscious leadership is a possible strategy in modeled settings. Although the findings are not supposed to be causal evidence, they can provide conceptual directions for future empirical study, as well as show possible applicability to other contexts like the Global South, where corporate social responsibility can become systemic value creation based on conscious variables.

title: Does water resource taxation improve firm productivity and regional ecological performance? Evidence from China
summary: Introduction Water scarcity is increasingly constraining global sustainable development, making it a critical policy challenge to improve economic performance while strengthening resource conservation. Methods Using the 2018 expansion of China’s Water Resource Tax Pilot Policy (WRTP) as a quasi-natural experiment, this study applies a difference-in-differences approach to firm-level and county-level data from 2012 to 2022. Results The results show that the WRTP significantly improves the total factor productivity of water-intensive firms, particularly in cities with stronger industrial foundations, the Yangtze River Economic Belt, regions with relatively abundant water resources, and larger listed firms. Environmental performance disclosure strengthens this productivity effect. Green innovation and pollution treatment disclosure exhibit significant positive moderating effects, whereas environmental supervision disclosure does not exhibit a significant moderating effect. County-level evidence further shows that the WRTP reduces water consumption intensity and the area affected by soil erosion while increasing sewage treatment capacity and investment in wastewater treatment. Discussion Overall, water resource taxation improves firm productivity while enhancing regional ecological performance, providing policy insights for advancing sustainable water governance in resource-constrained economies.

title: Surgical treatment of primary cardiac angiosarcoma: a case report
summary: Primary cardiac angiosarcoma is a rare and highly aggressive vascular malignant neoplasm, with an autopsy detection rate of approximately 0.0017%–0.28% and accounting for 30%–40% of primary cardiac malignant tumors. The disease predominantly affects males aged 40–60 years, with a male-to-female ratio of about 2:1. Approximately 80% of lesions are located in the right atrium, and cases occurring in young patients are exceedingly rare. Clinical manifestations are non-specific, and most patients present with local tissue invasion or distant metastasis at the time of diagnosis, with a median natural survival of only 3–6 months. We report a 22-year-old male patient with primary right atrial angiosarcoma who presented with left eyelid edema as the initial symptom.Pericardial effusion analysis was unremarkable, and transvenous endomyocardial biopsy conducted at an external hospital yielded negative pathological results. The false-negative biopsy result is further discussed in the Discussion section.Subsequent examinations suggested a malignant tumor with possible mediastinal lymph node metastasis, accompanied by intermittent fever.The patient underwent surgical resection of the cardiac mass, coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), tricuspid valvuloplasty, and right atrial reconstruction under cardiopulmonary bypass in our hospital. Postoperative pathological and immunohistochemical examinations (positive CD31, positive CD34, positive TLE1) confirmed the diagnosis of angiosarcoma. The eyelid edema completely resolved spontaneously after relief of pericardial effusion and radical tumor resection. The patient recovered uneventfully postoperatively, remained stable at 1-month follow-up, and was undergoing chemotherapy at an outside hospital. In patients with cardiac angiosarcoma featuring extensive invasion, lymph node metastasis, and negative preoperative biopsy, active comprehensive surgical treatment (tumor resection + CABG + valvuloplasty + atrial reconstruction) effectively alleviates symptoms, establish a definitive diagnosis, and create favorable conditions for postoperative adjuvant chemotherapy. Early imaging screening, precise surgical intervention, and standardized postoperative adjuvant therapy are key to improving the short-term prognosis of such young patients.

title: Smart Industry and Ecological Sustainability: Industry 4.0 Technologies, Renewables, and the US Production Ecological Footprint
summary: ABSTRACT The United States ranks 5th globally in terms of the per capita ecological footprint (ECF) and 2nd in terms of the total ECF and is responsible for intensive energy consumption, resource exploitation, and carbon‐intensive industrial production. However, achieving sustainable industrial development requires understanding which ecological modernization pathways are associated with reducing environmental pressures in the long run. Our study evaluates the long‐term associations of AI and eco‐innovation, supply chain efficiency, industrial renewable energy consumption, GDP growth, and foreign direct investment with the ECF in the United States. In terms of methodology, the study employs autoregressive distributed lag (ARDL) using US data from 1990 to 2023. The long‐run ARDL estimation suggests that AI and eco‐innovation, supply chain efficiency, and industrial renewable energy consumption are statistically significant and negatively associated with the ECF in the country over the long run. In contrast, GDP growth and foreign direct investment are significant positive ECF drivers within long‐run dynamics. However, supply chain efficiency shows the largest estimated negative long‐term association with ECF among the modernization pathways examined. Nevertheless, this result is model‐specific evidence rather than proof of universal superiority in comparison with other modernization pathways. Alternative long‐run estimators provide additional support for the baseline associations, although the alternative‐indicator specifications reveal sensitivity to variable measurement. In addition, the Toda–Yamamoto Granger causality results suggest that FDI follows unidirectional predictive precedence toward ECF. Overall, the findings suggest that ecological modernization in the United States operates through innovation capability, operational efficiency, and energy transition, each of which is associated with ECF through a different mechanism. Federal policymakers may consider prioritizing these ecological modernizers as long‐term complementary pathways and set combined policy actions to reduce ECF in the country.

title: Improving sustainability for emerging economy firms
summary: Purpose This paper aims to review the latest management developments across the globe and pinpoint practical implications from cutting-edge research and case studies. Design/methodology/approach This briefing is prepared by an independent writer who adds their own impartial comments and places the articles in context. Findings Businesses in emerging economies facing demands for more sustainable performance can meet such requirements through a strong focus on green innovation initiatives. These goals are helped substantially when the firm places environmental values within an organizational culture that also prioritizes collaboration and a strong orientation toward learning. Resilience is likewise imperative and able to strengthen ability to acquire and absorb the knowledge that can stimulate additional green innovation Originality/value The briefing saves busy executives, strategists and researchers hours of reading time by selecting only the very best, most pertinent information and presenting it in a condensed and easy-to-digest format.

title: Financial Technology and the Financial Inclusion of Women Entrepreneurs in Nigeria: Evidence from a Qualitative Study
summary: Background: Financial technology (FinTech) has expanded rapidly in Nigeria and is increasingly seen as a way to address persistent gaps in financial access. Yet the extent to which digital financial services translate into meaningful inclusion for women entrepreneurs remains poorly understood, particularly where financial literacy, infrastructure, location, and trust shape their ability to use available services. Purpose: This study examined how FinTech contributes to the financial inclusion of women entrepreneurs in Nigeria, with particular attention to the benefits associated with its use, factors influencing engagement, users' experiences and continuing barriers to effective participation. Method: A qualitative, interpretivist design was adopted. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 47 participants, comprising 36 women entrepreneurs, 10 FinTech executives/providers and one Central Bank of Nigeria policymaker. Participants were purposively selected to capture perspectives from users, service providers and the regulatory environment. Interviews were analysed using narrative thematic analysis supported by NVivo. Results: FinTech expanded access to financial services through faster transactions, greater proximity to payment and cash services, less bureaucratic access to credit, savings functionality, reduced reliance on cash and income-generating opportunities associated with point-of-sale services. Engagement was strongly shaped by financial literacy, geographic location and perceived product efficiency. Important constraints remained, including unreliable telecommunications and electricity, limited smartphone capability, transaction costs, difficulties navigating digital services, slow complaint resolution, cybercrime and fake-transfer incidents. Trust was particularly important, with some women using FinTech for transactions while remaining reluctant to retain substantial business funds with providers lacking a physical presence. Conclusion: FinTech can widen financial opportunities for women entrepreneurs, but technological availability alone does not constitute meaningful financial inclusion. Effective inclusion depends on the capacity to use digital financial services independently, reliably, affordably and securely. The findings support a process-oriented conception of digital financial inclusion in which technological access interacts with individual capability, entrepreneurial agency and wider institutional and infrastructural conditions.

title: ENHANCING THE ROLE OF BUSINESS VALUATION STANDARDS AND CORPORATE REPORTING IN ATTRACTING FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT IN UZBEKISTAN
summary: This study examines the role of business valuation standards and corporate reporting in attracting foreign direct investment (FDI) to Uzbekistan. It explores how valuation reliability, financial transparency, international accounting standards, and corporate governance influence investor confidence and investment decisions. The research combines institutional analysis, comparative assessment, and descriptive analysis of official investment statistics and Uzbekistan’s legal framework. The findings indicate that improving the comparability of financial statements, the credibility of enterprise valuations, and the disclosure of material risks can reduce information asymmetry and strengthen the investment attractiveness of domestic businesses. The article proposes an integrated approach connecting internationally aligned valuation practices, IFRS-based reporting, independent assurance, and corporate governance reforms.

title: DETERMINAN PENGELOLAAN KEUANGAN GENERASI Z DI DESA TUNGGARA, BANJARNEGARA
summary: Sound financial management is an essential competence for Generation Z, who grow up in a digital environment with heavy exposure to consumption trends. This study examines the effects of financial literacy, hedonistic lifestyle, self-control, Fear of Missing Out (FoMO), and financial technology (fintech) on the financial management of Generation Z in Tunggara Village, Banjarnegara Regency. A quantitative survey design was used. Primary data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire distributed via Google Forms to 100 respondents aged 16–29 years, selected by purposive sampling from a population of 479, and analyzed with multiple linear regression. Financial literacy (B = 0.591; p < 0.001), self-control (B = 0.165; p < 0.001), and fintech (B = 0.142; p = 0.010) have positive and significant effects on financial management, whereas hedonistic lifestyle (p = 0.614) and FoMO (p = 0.675) have no significant effect. The model is feasible (F = 57.954; p < 0.001) and explains 75.5% of the variance in financial management. Financial literacy is the most dominant determinant (standardized beta = 0.561). The findings highlight the need for applied financial education, stronger self-control, and prudent fintech use among rural Generation Z.

title: ICT Infrastructure Readiness for Accrual-Based IPSAS in Zimbabwean Government Schools
summary: ABSTRACT: Zimbabwean government schools must now report on accrual-based International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS). This requires them to record and report assets, liabilities, revenues and expenses as they arise. This study assessed whether schools in Marondera District have the information and communication technology (ICT) infrastructure the reform assumes. A convergent mixed-methods case study was used. In the study 71 of 73 sampled school heads, bursars, accounts and administrative staff and Ministry officials completed a questionnaire (97.3% response rate). Ten key informants were interviewed. Likert data (0–4) were tested against the neutral midpoint, and interviews were analysed thematically. ICT infrastructure averaged 2.52. All five items were rated significantly above neutral, but effects were small to moderate (d = 0.32–0.58). About 36.6% of respondents rejected the view that infrastructure adequately supports accrual reporting. Interviewees cited outdated computers, weak power back-up and software that is not IPSAS-native, especially in rural schools. Infrastructure was present though too limited for accrual reporting. A district ICT baseline for school finance offices, an IPSAS-compliant Ministry platform and rural solar back-up were recommended. KEYWORDS: Accrual based accounting, IPSAS, ICT infrastructure, Government schools, Digital transformation. Abbreviations: ICT, information and communication technology; IPSAS, International Public Sector Accounting Standards; TOE, Technology–Organisation–Environment framework; ZFRM, Zimbabwe Financial Reporting Manual.

title: Boards of Directors and Voluntary Carbon Disclosure: Evidence From Italy
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether Italy's concentrated ownership environment alters the effectiveness of board‐level governance mechanisms as drivers of voluntary carbon disclosure quality, in line with the institutional theory, challenging the assumptions of standard agency and stakeholder theories. Using a sample of 60 Italian listed non‐financial companies over 2015–2023, we employ the Carbon Disclosure Project scores as a measure of disclosure quality. The presence of a corporate social responsibility committee is the only governance mechanism consistently associated with the disclosure quality across all specifications. Board independence exhibits a significant negative effect, consistent with the symbolic compliance hypothesis, according to which independent directors in blockholder‐dominated firms may function as compliance figures rather than effective monitors. Board size, gender diversity, and CEO duality are not significantly associated with disclosure quality. Further analysis shows that the CSR committee effect is stronger in carbon‐intensive industries and weaker in family‐controlled firms. Family ownership also attenuates the negative effect of board independence, suggesting that concentrated ownership selectively conditions, rather than uniformly suppresses, governance effectiveness. Results are robust to alternative estimators, lag structures, and endogeneity tests. Overall, the findings provide novel evidence that governance–disclosure relationships documented in dispersed ownership settings do not readily extend to blockholder‐dominated environments, with important implications for governance reforms in similar institutional contexts.

title: The Impact of Cashless Payment Adoption on Impulsive Spending Behavior Among Generation Z: Empirical Evidence from Vietnam
summary: The rapid expansion of digital payment infrastructures and e-wallets has fundamentally altered consumer transaction habits, particularly among digital natives. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) and mental accounting theory, this study investigates the empirical impact of cashless payment adoption on the impulsive spending behavior of Generation Z consumers in Vietnam. A quantitative survey was administered to 320 Gen Z respondents across major metropolitan areas, utilizing a 5-point Likert scale. Multiple linear regression and reliability tests were deployed to evaluate the proposed hypotheses. The empirical findings reveal that perceived convenience, promotional incentives, and subjective social norms exhibit a statistically significant positive effect on spending frequency and impulsive purchasing. Notably, the reduction in the psychological 'pain of paying' significantly diminishes financial self-control among younger cohorts. Based on these insights, the paper proposes actionable recommendations for higher education institutions, fintech platforms, and policymakers to foster financial literacy.

title: Avon International: Imagining a Refill Program in Turkey
summary: The case explores the role of sustainability initiatives in Avon's business strategy and how they align with its mission of empowering women. It also discusses the potential financial and operational implications of the yet-to-be implemented idea of a refill program, including changes to supply chain, production, and logistics. Additionally, the case highlights the importance of stakeholder engagement and the potential impact on Avon's Turkish associates and women entrepreneurs.

title: Power Beyond Organizational Boundaries: Sustainable Supply Chain Management and External Evaluation Consistency
summary: ABSTRACT Sustainable supply chain management (SSCM) is an important vertical governance mechanism transcending organizational boundaries. Previous studies have primarily emphasized its contribution to sustainable performance, while its role as a firm‐manageable dimension relevant to external evaluation consistency remains underexplored. Using 10,656 firm‐year observations from Chinese A‐share listed firms during 2009–2023, this study constructs a text‐based multidimensional co‐occurrence measure of SSCM and examines its association with rating divergence. Results show that stronger SSCM is associated with lower ESG rating divergence, with evidence consistent with information quality and vertical relationship governance channels. The association is stronger for internal‐process and customer‐related SSCM. Divergence is associated with lower risk‐taking propensity and higher supply‐chain cost sharing, while these adverse relationships are weaker at higher SSCM levels. This study extends research by highlighting SSCM as a firm‐manageable dimension associated with greater evaluation consistency. It also highlights SSCM's potential to limit the adverse consequences of persistent rating disagreement.

title: Strategic autonomy in orbit: how small and middle powers navigate technology, markets, and norms in Space 4.0
summary: Space 4.0—marked by commercialization, modular technologies, actor diversification, and intensifying geopolitical competition—has lowered barriers to participation while relocating hierarchy into supply chains, platforms, standards, and commercial infrastructure. This conceptual analysis asks how, and under what geopolitical conditions, small and middle powers (SMPs) convert technological specialization, market embeddedness, and normative positioning into selective strategic autonomy. Using analytic eclecticism, the article, by integrating Science and Technology Studies (STS), International Political Economy (IPE), and constructivism, distinguishes strategic agency—the capacity to act purposively under constraint—from strategic autonomy—the contingent outcome of preserving meaningful options and limiting determinative dependence. The framework identifies three corresponding practices: niche specialization, which converts selective technological capability into capability leverage; agile hedging, which uses procurement, supply-chain positioning, and institutional diversification to create bargaining leverage; and norm entrepreneurship, which converts legitimacy and rule-making participation into influence. The evidentiary base is a structured synthesis of scholarship and purposively selected illustrations from South Korea, Australia, and New Zealand, with India and the European Union used as boundary comparators. The analysis argues that autonomy emerges when capability, bargaining, and legitimacy leverage are strategically coupled, but that the same coupling can deepen upstream dependence, security exposure, or implementation gaps. It further proposes competitive pluralism as a boundary condition: SMP room for manoeuvre is greatest when great-power rivalry creates credible alternatives without hardening into closed blocs. The article therefore recasts secondary-state agency in high-technology geopolitics as the capacity to organize and recalibrate interdependence rather than escape it.

title: India Payments Industry Outlook 2027
summary: India payments industry outlook 2027: funding trends, M&A and consolidation, FY23-FY25 financials of 303 payments companies, the 29 profitable payment companies and 20 startups to watch, UPI and digital payments search trends, fintech regulation news and payment app data for payment gateways, aggregators and merchant acquirers in India. A 2027 monitoring brief on India's payments sector built from company filings, funding histories, deal records, corporate news events and app-store listings. It keeps the separate record sets separate: 303 companies with accounts for every year FY23-FY25 (combined revenue up 21% while combined net income stays negative), 787 recorded funding rounds across tracked payments companies, 155 matched M&A deal records, 2,400 corporate news-event records and 397 matched Play listings. It lists the 29 companies that pass a strict consistent-profit screen and 20 younger profitable companies to watch next, and ends with a 2027 monitoring agenda and a plain statement of what the data does and does not measure. title: Mapping the Landscape of Marketing Innovation in the Digital Era: A Bibliometric Synthesis and Strategic Intelligence Framework for Planning
summary: Purpose – This study maps the structural evolution of marketing innovation scholarship from 1998 to 2026 and develops an integrated marketing intelligence and strategic planning framework. Design/methodology/approach – A bibliometric network synthesis of 1,751 Scopus-indexed peer-reviewed documents was carried out with VOSviewer, following the PRISMA 2020 systematic review protocol. Findings – Six thematic clusters were identified: e-commerce and digital marketing; competitive strategies and organizational aspects; effectiveness of innovative marketing; SME-oriented innovation and empirical measurement; the human factor; and eco-oriented marketing for sustainable development. The field has shifted from basic organizational innovations towards AI-driven marketing intelligence, big data analytics, metaverse platforms and ESG-oriented sustainable planning. Practical implications – The proposed Integrated Marketing Intelligence and Innovation Planning Architecture (MIIPA) shows chief marketing officers how to embed predictive data intelligence into marketing decision-making and innovation planning cycles. Originality/value – The study bridges the gap between fragmented marketing innovation literature and operational strategic marketing planning by linking market sensing, organizational capabilities and planning outcomes in one framework and by setting out a structured future research agenda.

title: Maintaining Irrigation Infrastructure Under Rising Climate Hazards: An Optimal Control Analysis of Financing Regimes with Reference to Vietnam
summary: Irrigation networks in low-lying deltas are deteriorating faster than their design assumed, as salinity intrusion, floods and land subsidence add to ordinary wear. Whether they are kept in working order depends less on engineering than on how maintenance is financed and who decides when it is done. This paper builds a deterministic optimal control model in which a maintenance agency chooses the path of maintenance outlays to sustain the service capacity of an irrigation network whose deterioration rate rises with climate hazard intensity. Financing arrangements enter through two interpretable parameters: the social cost of one unit of maintenance funding and the discount rate applied by the deciding agency. The analysis is analytical and qualitative. We derive the steady state, the saddle-path dynamics and a complete table of comparative statics, and we state six propositions. Budget-cycle financing produces chronic under-maintenance, and the resulting gap separates cleanly into a financing component and a horizon component that call for different remedies. The horizon component widens as hazards intensify. Optimal maintenance spending is hump-shaped in the deterioration rate, and a short-sighted agency reaches the turning point, beyond which it lets the system contract, earlier than society would. The share of maintenance that farmers can afford to pay falls as hazards rise, a mechanism we call the climate squeeze on cost recovery. Finally, maintenance norms calibrated to historical deterioration erode capacity once hazards intensify. Read against Vietnam’s shift from irrigation fees to irrigation service prices, the results suggest that multi-year earmarked maintenance funds and affordability-capped prices are the main levers where hazards are moderate, while low-cost climate finance and planned transformation become decisive where hazards are severe.

title: Does Financial Slack Matter? Corporate Governance, Corporate Activities, And Sustainability Reporting Quality in Indonesia
summary: This study examines the effects of corporate governance mechanisms and asset turnover on sustainability reporting quality, with particular emphasis on the moderating role of financial slack. Drawing on agency, legitimacy, and stakeholder theories, the study employs a quantitative approach using panel data from 33 companies consistently included in Indonesia's ESGQ-KEHATI Index between 2021 and 2024, yielding 132 firm-year observations. Sustainability reporting quality is assessed through content analysis of 33 environmental, social, and governance (ESG) indicators, while financial slack is measured as the ratio of free cash flow to total revenue. The data are analyzed using fixed-effects panel regression and moderated regression analysis. The findings reveal that the proportion of independent commissioners, audit committee, and total asset turnover positively and significantly influence sustainability reporting quality, whereas managerial ownership has no significant effect. Financial slack exhibits a positive direct association with reporting quality and strengthens the effects of independent commissioners and the audit committee, but does not significantly moderate the relationships involving managerial ownership or asset turnover. The adjusted R² increases from 0.514 to 0.533 following the inclusion of financial slack in the regression specification. Firm age is positively associated with reporting quality, while firm size has no significant effect. These findings suggest that financial flexibility complements formal corporate governance oversight in improving sustainability reporting quality. The study contributes to sustainability governance literature by demonstrating that the moderating role of financial slack differs across governance and operational mechanisms, highlighting the importance of resource availability in supporting effective sustainability oversight.
