title: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) Disclosure in Africa: Current State of Play
summary: ABSTRACT Purpose: This paper evaluates the operational landscape, regulatory architectures, and corporate adoption patterns of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosures across four key African capital markets: South Africa, Nigeria, Ghana, and Kenya. Design/methodology/approach: Utilizing a multi-jurisdictional documentary review protocol across the period 2018–2025, regulatory instruments, listing requirements, national accounting codes, and corporate sustainability reports (N = 240 corporate firm-years) were evaluated against a 7-dimension structural framework. Findings: The results demonstrate significant institutional heterogeneity. South Africa exhibits a mature statutory regime anchored by King IV and mandatory JSE listing rules. Nigeria and Kenya are undergoing rapid regulatory formalization driven by Central Bank mandates and stock exchange sustainability principles, while Ghana maintains a predominantly voluntary framework. Across all markets, a substantial implementation gap persists between regulatory adoption and third-party assurance. Originality/value: The study provides an empirical diagnostic matrix for capital market regulators and establishes a baseline for tracking the implementation of IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 standards across emerging African economies.

title: Reimagining nature finance
summary: Natural capital markets (NCMs) are widely heralded as an important solution to the biodiversity crisis. Extensive effort, energy, time, and resources have been invested into making them function. NCMs are intended to catalyse financial flows from the private sector to conservation and nature recovery projects, helping to close the ‘nature finance gap’. Whilst this rhetoric is appealing, there is growing evidence that NCMs (principally voluntary biodiversity and carbon offset markets) are unlikely to ever protect or recover nature at the necessary scale and speed required, nor deliver wide-ranging socio-ecological benefits to a diversity of communities, organisms, and ecosystems. Drawing on interdisciplinary evidence, we outline five established flaws associated with NCMs: persistent barriers to scaling, a compensatory rather than restorative character, the prioritisation of financial returns over socio-ecological outcomes, justice and equity concerns, and measurement challenges. Collectively, they lead us to offer a central claim: NCMs have absorbed a disproportionate amount of political and research attention relative to their limited impact. We call for reimagining nature finance, based on a central tenet: raising funds should be a means to an end, not an end in itself. This reimagined approach requires greater attention to how the structures and requirements of finance shape which regions, ecological outcomes, and forms of governance become visible, valuable, and ultimately financeable. A reimagined approach demands redirecting research and policy attention towards what really matters: finding effective and equitable ways to finance conservation and nature recovery projects which deliver beneficial socio-ecological outcomes.

title: ESG Performance, Board Gender Diversity, and Dividend Policy: Evidence from Australian-Listed Firms
summary: This paper examines whether board gender diversity conditions the association between ESG performance and dividend policy in Australian-listed firms. We employ an unbalanced panel of 127 ASX-listed companies over 2013–2023, and firm fixed-effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors. The findings reveal that ESG performance is positively associated with dividends per share (DPS). Moreover, female board representation has no direct association with DPS, although it is positively associated with ESG performance. Further analysis shows that the ESG–dividend association strengthens with female representation and is concentrated in boards that have reached a critical mass of women; the marginal effect of ESG on DPS is statistically indistinguishable from zero on boards with fewer than 30% women, but positive and significant once female representation reaches about 30%, where a one-standard-deviation higher ESG score is associated with A$ 0.13 higher DPS (28% of the sample mean). This critical-mass pattern is robust to year fixed effects, winsorisation, and additional governance controls, but it is weaker under firm-clustered standard errors and specific to dividends per share rather than the payout ratio or the dividend yield. Investors and boards should therefore evaluate ESG performance and board composition jointly when assessing dividend capacity.

title: Digital Accounting Disclosure and Market Valuation of Listed Non-Financial Companies in Nigeria
summary: The increasing use of digital technologies in accounting has changed not only how financial information is generated but also how companies communicate the quality and reliability of their reporting processes to capital-market participants. This study examines the relationship between digital accounting disclosure and market valuation of listed non-financial companies in Nigeria, focusing on real-time financial reporting disclosure, automated tax reporting disclosure and automated internal control disclosure. The study adopts an ex-post facto design and uses archival information from annual reports and corporate disclosures of 66 listed non-financial companies over 2016–2025. Market valuation is proxied by market capitalization growth, while firm size, measured as the natural logarithm of total assets, is included as a control variable. Disclosure indices are constructed from corporate reports. The reduced model was re-estimated from the underlying firm-year observations rather than transferring coefficients from the original seven variable model. Robust ordinary least squares estimates based on 538 complete observations show positive but statistically insignificant coefficients for real-time financial reporting disclosure (β = 0.515; p = .333), automated tax reporting disclosure (β = 0.889; p = .264), and automated internal control disclosure (β = 1.216; p = .492). The findings suggest that disclosure of these technologies, by itself, did not provide sufficiently strong incremental information to explain short-term market capitalization growth during the study period. The study concludes that the valuation relevance of digital accounting disclosure may depend on the credibility, depth and usefulness of the information communicated rather than disclosure presence alone.

title: Environmental Sustainability of Palm Oil Exports in Riau Province: Evidence from Deforestation, Carbon Emissions, and RSPO Certification
summary: The rapid expansion of Indonesia’s palm oil industry has raised concerns regarding deforestation and carbon emissions, particularly in major producing regions such as Riau Province. This study aims to examine the relationship between palm oil exports and environmental sustainability by considering deforestation, carbon emissions, and RSPO certification during 2013–2023. The study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data, descriptive analysis, and regression-based assessment. The findings indicate that increases in palm oil export values are not consistently accompanied by higher deforestation, although export growth remains associated with environmental pressure through carbon emissions. Meanwhile, RSPO-certified plantation areas tend to be associated with lower deforestation and carbon emissions. These results suggest that environmental outcomes in the palm oil sector are influenced not only by export performance but also by sustainability governance mechanisms. The study recommends strengthening sustainability certification and environmental governance to support competitive and environmentally responsible palm oil development in Riau Province.

title: Strategic imperatives for the development of public administration in the context of digitalization: methodological and legal aspects
summary: Purpose. To develop a dynamic mathematical model of the digital maturity index for public administration in Ukraine as a tool for quantitatively assessing the effectiveness of digital transformation in the context of European integration and martial law. Methodology. The comparative analysis method was applied to systematize conceptual approaches to digital transformation (human-centeredness, interoperability, transparency, data-driven management, security by design, inclusivity). Structural-functional analysis was used to examine the institutional architecture (the Ministry of Digital Transformation (MDT), the “Trembita” system, and the “Diia” portal), cybersecurity mechanisms, and the legal framework. The weighted aggregation method of five sub-indices was applied to construct a digital maturity index based on data from the MDT, CERT-UA, and Eurostat for 2019–2024. Findings. It has been established that the methodology of digital public administration in Ukraine is based on six key principles, which are implemented through a cyclical approach. The legal framework ensures the legal equivalence of electronic and paper documents. The digital maturity index rose from 0.34 in 2019 to 0.63 in 2024 and 0.72 in the first half of 2026. Trends in the components: the effectiveness of digital services rose from 0.31 to 0.80; the level of cybersecurity temporarily declined to 0.40 in 2022 before stabilizing at 0.53; interoperability increased from 0.28 to 0.78; citizen engagement – from 0.19 to 0.63; legal compliance – from 0.41 to 0.79. Systemic barriers were identified: inconsistencies in legislation, the need for harmonization with the GDPR and eIDAS, and insufficient implementation of business continuity plans. Originality. For the first time, a comprehensive combination of methodological, legal, and quantitative aspects of digital transformation has been proposed. An original dynamic model of the digital maturity index has been developed based on five weighted sub-indices. The four-level interoperability framework and the structure of legal compliance have been refined through the aggregation of harmonization with the GDPR, eIDAS, cybersecurity legislation, and administrative codes. Practical value. The results can be used by the Ministry of Digital Transformation of Ukraine and international partners to set priorities for digital transformation, assess the impact of cyber threats, and monitor progress in harmonization with the GDPR and eIDAS in the context of European integration.

title: BNVT Capital: Insights into the Investor Perspective
summary: This case blends canonical and contemporary themes in entrepreneurship. It tackles the canonical question of screening for entrepreneurial opportunities and the value of a rigorous investment thesis. It addresses these issues with a contemporary approach, capturing the AI-led approach that investors utilise these days.The case follows Chris Corbishley and Rory Mounsey-Heysham as they build BNVT Capital, a new venture fund grounded in a data-driven, impact-oriented investment thesis. Chris brings an operational and investment background including roles at Molten Ventures and Hedesophia, with a particular focus on fintech. Rory comes with deep experience in impact investing, most recently at the Gates Foundation. Their complementary skill-sets are reinforced by distinguished advisors including Harley Finkelstein (co-founder of Shopify) and Greg Jackson (founder of Octopus Energy).

title: Corporate social responsibility in aviation management: The impact of sustainable marketing on brand equity
summary: This study seeks to investigate the impact of various aspects of corporate social responsibility (CSR) activities on sustainable marketing practices and brand equity in the aviation industry. The study used a quantitative approach, and data were collected from 490 employees working in the Turkish aviation industry using a well-structured questionnaire. The data were analyzed using the structural equation modeling (SEM) approach in the AMOS software package. Findings reveal that CSR practices targeting employees negatively affect strategic integration, while ethics-based practices positively influence strategic integration and ethical capabilities. CSR efforts aimed at society harm ethical capabilities but enhance social participation. Strategic integration and ethical capabilities positively affect brand equity components, whereas social participation has a negative impact. The findings suggest that the success of CSR efforts hinges on the strategic fit and ethical dimension of CSR rather than the social aspect of it alone. This research makes its contribution to the existing literature on CSR by expanding knowledge of the multidimensional links between CSR activities, sustainable marketing strategy, and brand equity in the aviation management setting.

title: Green Innovation Through Artificial Intelligence: Sectoral and Regional Perspectives of China
summary: ABSTRACT The rapid adoption of artificial intelligence (AI) has transformed manufacturing and promotes firms' green innovation. Concurrently, the significance of green innovation plays an important role in supporting firms' environmental transformation. Against this backdrop, the present study investigates the dynamic relationship between AI and firms' green innovation (FGI), with a specific focus on Chinese manufacturing firms. The results show that manufacturing companies with extensive AI adoption demonstrate heightened levels of green innovation. Furthermore, the study explores the heterogeneous impact of AI on FGI across different types of firms and regions. Notably, AI has a stronger effect on FGI within the eastern region and significantly drives green innovation in non‐SOE, high‐tech, and non‐labor‐intensive firms compared to their counterparts in SOE, labor‐intensive, and non‐tech industries. Additionally, AI contributes to the enhancement of FGI by stimulating investments in green research and development (R&D), reducing operational costs, and facilitating digital transformation initiatives. The study also illuminates the influence of environmental regulations in amplifying AI's promotion of FGI in manufacturing firms. Finally, based on the pragmatic assessments, valuable policy implications are discussed.

title: Pengaruh Tata Kelola Perusahaan, Rasio Pembayaran Dividen Dan Total Perputaran Aset Terhadap Nilai Perusahaan Sektor Pertambangan Di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: This study aims to determine the effect of Corporate Governance, Dividend Payout Ratio and Total Asset Turnover on the value of mining companies. The population in this study consists of mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the period 2019-2023. The non-probability sampling method with Purposive Sampling technique resulted in a sample of 6 out of 63 mining companies. Secondary data was obtained from the official website of the Indonesia Stock Exchange in the form of data from mining sector companies included in the LQ45 index and processed using EVIEWS-12. The data was then analyzed using multiple linear regression. The results of the study indicate that Corporate Governance, Dividend Payout Ratio, and Total Asset Turnover jointly affect Company Value in mining sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the period 2019-2023. Partially, the three independent variables have a positive and significant influence on Company Value in mining sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the period 2019-2023.

title: AKSIYADORLIK JAMIYATLARIDA KORPORATIV BOSHQARUV SAMARADORLIGINI OSHIRISHNING FUNKSIONAL ASOSLARI
summary: Assessing corporate governance effectiveness solely through governing body composition or profitability obscures the link between decisions and implementation. Institutional comparison and structural-functional analysis organize the activities of the general shareholders’ meeting, supervisory board and executive body around transparency, accountability, responsibility and fairness. A functional matrix connects the three bodies with these four principles. Assessment distinguishes formal structure, evidence of activity and economic outcomes. The framework provides a conceptual basis for identifying governance gaps and evaluating decision implementation. The supervisory board’s role linking the general shareholders’ meeting and the executive body is specifically substantiated

title: Empowering MSMEs through Digital Branding and Marketing Strategies to Enhance Competitiveness
summary: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) play an important role in supporting local economic growth, yet many business owners continue to face challenges in building consistent digital branding and implementing effective marketing strategies to compete in an increasingly digital marketplace. This community empowerment activity aimed to strengthen the digital branding capabilities and marketing strategies of MSME actors to improve their business competitiveness. The activity was designed to enhance participants’ understanding and practical skills in developing a consistent business identity, creating promotional content, utilizing digital platforms, and applying appropriate marketing strategies based on their business characteristics. The implementation used an educational and participatory approach consisting of several stages, including identification of participants’ needs, preparation, education and training, demonstration and hands-on practice, mentoring, and evaluation. The activities combined presentations, discussions, demonstrations, direct practice, and individual guidance to encourage participants to apply the materials to their respective businesses. The results indicated that participants demonstrated increased understanding of digital branding and marketing strategies and were able to apply the training materials through the development of business identities, promotional content, and digital marketing practices. The mentoring stage further supported participants in adapting digital branding and marketing strategies to their business conditions. Overall, the activity contributed to strengthening MSME capabilities in utilizing digital platforms and developing more structured marketing practices, thereby supporting efforts to improve business competitiveness in the digital economy. The activity also demonstrates the relevance of community empowerment programs in supporting sustainable MSME development through digital transformation and capacity building.

title: Studi Kasus Eksplorasi Sosial-Teknis: Demarkasi Etika dan Hukum antara Ethical Hacking dan Cybercrime
summary: Kesamaan instrumen teknis antara ethical hacking dan cybercrime seringkali menyamarkan perbedaan fundamental di ranah hukum dan etika. Penelitian kualitatif ini menggunakan pendekatan studi kasus untuk menganalisis tiga insiden eksploitasi sistem yang terjadi di sektor kesehatan, fintech, dan e-commerce. Dengan menelaah aspek otorisasi, motif pelaku, dan dampak sosial-ekonomi, riset ini merumuskan batas demarkasi yang jelas antara praktik peretasan yang sah dan tindak pidana siber. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa niat baik tidak menghapus status ilegal suatu tindakan jika dilakukan tanpa persetujuan eksplisit. Riset ini merekomendasikan pentingnya kontrak uji keamanan (PenTest Agreement) dan kebijakan Responsible Disclosure sebagai instrumen kunci untuk mencegah kriminalisasi peneliti keamanan, serta perlunya pemisahan tegas dalam penegakan hukum siber di Indonesia.

title: Engaged research and its implications for transformation in climate adaptation sciences
summary: Transformative climate adaptation efforts, which call for the fundamental reshaping of social systems that inform vulnerability to climate risk, introduce significant ethical and procedural questions for researchers. Engaged research practices, such as co-production and participatory action research, may be useful in addressing these complex questions and pushing adaptation research towards more transformative ends. However, there are also ethical and procedural concerns plaguing participatory knowledge production, and scholars claim engaged research efforts have failed to meet goals for transforming scientific practice. Recent literature in adaptation, climate services, sustainability science, and environmental governance, illustrates the ongoing challenges and unresolved tensions holding engaged research practices back from its transformative aims. This essay suggests three areas of growth for engaged researchers in climate services and adaptation: interrogate the aims of research projects, focus on learning outcomes, and evaluate research governance. The essay addresses a wide audience and serves three primary purposes: 1) as a primer for students and early career researchers beginning to explore the history and use of engaged research in climate services and adaptation, 2) as a summary of common challenges for researchers designing and implementing engaged research projects with communities and other stakeholders, and 3) as a blueprint for institutional supporters, including funders and research convenors aiming to improve engaged research outcomes and advance more transformative adaptation.

title: The economic dimension of implementing IT and media technologies in Russian shipbuilding
summary: The economic dimension of introducing IT and media technologies into the domestic shipbuilding industry is gaining priority importance in the context of the accelerated digital transformation of the industrial complex, as well as the growing requirements for construction timeframes, quality characteristics, and the cost of complex ship equipment. The Russian shipbuilding industry is characterized by significant capital intensity, long production cycles, and an extensive system of inter organizational cooperation. Under such conditions, digital solutions should be considered not only as a technological tool but also as a managerial and economic factor of competitiveness, determining the rational use of resources and the stability of enterprises in domestic and foreign markets. The aim of this study is to substantiate the economic consequences and determine the conditions for the effective implementation of IT and media technologies in the Russian shipbuilding industry, taking into account sectoral limitations and the specifics of the institutional environment.

title: Digital Payments and Risk in E-Commerce: A Systematic Bibliometric Review and Future Research Agenda
summary: This study presents a systematic, bibliometric review of research on digital payments and risk in e-commerce. Following the PRISMA protocol and the four-step bibliometric procedure of Donthu et al. (2021), data were retrieved from Elsevier’s Scopus database on 16 September 2026 using the search string “Digital Payments AND Risk”, and 805 peer-reviewed journal articles and reviews published between 2016 and 2026 were analysed in Biblioshiny. The literature is young and expanding rapidly, with an annual growth rate of 40.38%, yet it remains concentrated in a small set of journals and countries, notably China and India. Thematic mapping and keyword co-occurrence analysis show blockchain, electronic money and risk assessment as the best-developed themes, while fintech, digital payments, financial inclusion, cryptocurrency and central bank digital currency remain weakly developed and peripheral. Research on payment infrastructure and fraud and research on consumer adoption and trust continue to develop in parallel. The paper proposes a future research agenda, structured around the 5W1H framework, that targets neglected users, the e-commerce checkout, under-represented markets, longitudinal designs and integrated models linking safeguards with consumer trust.

title: Scaling AI in heavy industry: Can Ultratech’s ecosystem model take it from 10 to 100?
summary: This case examines the AI journey of UltraTech Cement, the flagship cement company of the Aditya Birla Group and one of the largest cement producers globally. The case follows Rahul Chopade, Head of Digital Transformation for Manufacturing, as the organisation transitions from early experimentation with AI to a broader phase of enterprise scaling.UltraTech operates at extraordinary operational scale across multiple manufacturing facilities and logistics networks. The company’s digital transformation effort focuses on improving decision-making across operations, rather than simply digitising processes or building dashboards. AI thus becomes a mechanism to enhance productivity, reliability, safety and operational efficiency across plants.

title: Digital Financial Reporting Technologies and Financial Reporting Quality of Listed Manufacturing Firms in Nigeria: Evidence from Cloud Accounting, Real-Time Reporting and Artificial Intelligence Integration
summary: The rapid digitalisation of accounting functions has altered the way listed manufacturing firms in Nigeria capture transactions, process financial information and prepare corporate reports. While accounting automation is generally expected to strengthen reporting quality, the benefits of individual technologies may differ according to their depth of adoption, integration and organisational context. This study focuses specifically on three emerging dimensions of digital financial reporting technology—cloud accounting adoption, real-time financial reporting capability, and artificial intelligence and analytics integration—and examines their expected relationship with financial reporting quality among listed manufacturing firms in Nigeria. Financial reporting quality is operationalised through discretionary accruals, with lower discretionary accruals interpreted as evidence of higher reporting quality. The study is framed by agency theory and signalling theory. An ex post facto panel research design is proposed for the 2015–2024 period, using information obtained from published annual reports and audited financial statements of sampled listed manufacturing firms. The empirical model specifies discretionary accruals as a function of cloud accounting adoption, real-time financial reporting capability, artificial intelligence and analytics integration, and firm size. The Modified Jones Model provides the basis for estimating discretionary accruals. Existing evidence from the underlying broader accounting-automation study indicates negative associations for the three retained technology dimensions, with real-time financial reporting reaching conventional statistical significance in the original seven-variable specification, while cloud accounting and artificial intelligence/analytics did not reach the 5 percent threshold. However, those coefficients were estimated in the original seven-variable model and should not be reported as the final coefficients of the present reduced model until the reduced specification is re-estimated. The article therefore provides a complete publication-oriented framework while maintaining this empirical integrity. The study is expected to contribute to the Nigerian accounting-technology literature by isolating three increasingly important digital reporting capabilities and showing why adoption depth, system integration and organisational readiness matter for reporting quality.

title: The Accounting Frontier of Biodiversity: A Socio-Economic Critique of ESG Reporting Frameworks and the Promise of Ecological Debt
summary: Purpose – This article examines whether contemporary ESG biodiversity reporting frameworks can fulfill their stated objective of making nature visible, comparable, and governable within economic and financial systems.Methodology – The study adopts a critical qualitative approach grounded in the sociology of quantification and neo-institutional theory. It analyzes the main biodiversity reporting frameworks, including GRI, TNFD, and ESRS E4.Findings – Biodiversity emerges as a boundary object whose complexity, locality, and irreversibility challenge the standardization logic required by financial reporting. Existing frameworks tend to produce a form of “narrated biodiversity” that primarily serves institutional legitimacy rather than effective ecological stewardship.Conclusions – The article argues for a shift toward an ecological debt perspective inspired by the CARE model. By recognizing ecosystem maintenance obligations within accounting systems, this approach offers a more robust framework for ecological accountability and sustainability governanceKeywords: Biodiversity accounting; ESG reporting; institutional legitimacy; CARE model; ecological debt.JEL Codes: M41; Q51; Q56; Q57; G34.

title: Administrative Reform and Governance Performance in Vietnam: Evidence from a Decade of PAR Index and PAPI Data
summary: Vietnam measures the progress of its public administration reform with two very different instruments. The Public Administration Reform Index (PAR Index), compiled by the Ministry of Home Affairs, scores ministries and provinces on how far they have carried out the reform tasks assigned to them. The Provincial Governance and Public Administration Performance Index (PAPI), produced by an independent research consortium with the United Nations Development Programme, asks citizens how governance actually feels from the receiving end. This article reads the two series side by side for the decade 2015–2024, together with the government’s citizen satisfaction index (SIPAS). It relies only on published secondary data and uses descriptive longitudinal comparison and source triangulation rather than econometric modelling. Three patterns emerge. First, official reform scores rose steadily: The provincial mean of the PAR Index climbed from 74.64% in 2016 to 88.37% in 2024, and the distance between the best and worst province shrank from 27.77 to 13.22 points. Second, citizen-reported governance improved far more slowly and unevenly. Dimensions linked to the supply of services, such as administrative procedures and public service delivery, sit comfortably above the midpoint of the PAPI scale, while participation, vertical accountability, environmental governance and e-governance remain below it in every province. Third, the two instruments often rank the same province very differently, and several episodes of compromised survey data since 2023 show that the pressure created by league tables now reaches the measurement process itself. The article interprets these patterns as a gap between reform compliance and governance experience, and argues that the PAR Index is approaching a ceiling at which it can no longer separate strong from weak performers. It closes with proposals for linking the two instruments, protecting survey integrity and redesigning indicators for the two-tier local government system introduced in 2025.

title: Measuring ICT Governance Compliance in South Africa’s Public Service: A Systematic Multivocal Review and Conceptual Framework
summary: Digital transformation in the public sector has intensified the need to demonstrate not only adoption of ICT governance frameworks but sustained compliance with governance requirements. This systematic multivocal literature review developed a conceptual ICT Governance Compliance Measurement Framework for South Africa’s public service and was reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. Peer-reviewed and authoritative grey literature published from January 2004 to May 2026 was searched across Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, EBSCOhost, Google Scholar, and targeted institutional sources; the academic searches were updated through 31 May 2026. The protocol was registered on the Open Science Framework (DOI: 10.17605/OSF.IO/YZVB3). Of 1380 records identified, 130 full texts were assessed, 91 proceeded to source-appropriate quality appraisal, and 72 sources (52 academic and 20 grey/postgraduate) met the final quality threshold and informed an abductive thematic synthesis. Six interrelated compliance dimensions emerged: Strategic Alignment; Governance Structures and Accountability; Risk and Security Governance; ICT Investment and Procurement Governance; Regulatory and Policy Compliance; and Performance Monitoring and Continuous Improvement. These were integrated into a six-stage conceptual compliance-measurement workflow linking normative requirements, compliance dimensions, evidence triangulation, implementation rating, a six-dimensional compliance profile, and remediation/reassessment, bounded by organisational antecedents and public-value consequences. The framework offers a traceable basis for self-assessment and audit readiness, but requires empirical validation before formal scoring, benchmarking, or assurance use.

title: Ecologically Compatible Autonomous AI Production
summary: Increasingly autonomous AI-mediated production can expand task-level capabilities while leaving the renewal of machinery, energy provision, knowledge, labour, and material supply dependent on wider productive relations. This exploratory paper examines the conditions under which those capacities can be reproduced without undermining affected ecological processes. Historical-materialist analysis and a provisional generative-relational (GR) representation are used to distinguish operational autonomy, continued productive capacity, changes in critical dependencies, ecological viability, and institutional authority over feasible alternatives. Domain-specific reviews assess documented capabilities and limits in robotics, automated laboratories, production control, computing, power and cooling, supply chains, repair, and materials recovery. A typed relational model makes physical flows, enabling conditions, evidentiary provenance, and decision rights jointly inspectable without treating them as interchangeable quantities. Its incremental value relative to life-cycle assessment, material-flow analysis, reliability engineering, conventional production networks, and established provenance methods remains to be tested. Conditional formal constructions are connected to proposed counterfactual comparisons, empirical measurement protocols, and explicit identification and falsification criteria. The paper distinguishes technical feasibility, ecological effects, distributional consequences, and normative justification, allowing incompatibility or indeterminate results. It reports no original production experiment, causal ecological estimate, or demonstrated self-reproducing AI factory and establishes no general ranking of ownership forms. Its contribution is a bounded research architecture and staged empirical programme for investigating the historically constituted conditions of ecologically compatible autonomous production.

title: A Multimodal Explainable AI Architecture for Dynamic ESG Performance Prediction: Integrating Sustainability Intelligence, Investor Relevance, and Risk Dynamics in Saudi Listed Companies
summary: This study develops an explainable machine-learning framework for predicting Environmental, Social and Governance Index Performance (ESGIP) of Saudi listed companies by integrating sustainability indicators, investor-relevance measures, and financial-risk dynamics. The framework combines descriptive statistics, Augmented Dickey–Fuller and Phillips–Perron stationarity tests, correlation analysis, ANOVA, principal component analysis, XGBoost, long short-term memory, Random Forest optimized by genetic algorithm and particle swarm optimization, and SHapley Additive exPlanations. All variables were stationary at level I(0). Sustainability Reporting Quality showed the strongest positive correlation with ESGIP (r = 0.8663), while Tobin’s Q was the strongest positive investor-relevance predictor (r = 0.6531) and Financial Distress Score the strongest negative predictor (r = −0.5921). PCA revealed a dominant sustainability–governance structure, with PC1 explaining 82.71% of variance in C1, compared with 45.01% in C2. In testing, RF-PSO improved NSE by 1.93% and reduced MAE by 4.84% for C1, while also outperforming XGBoost and LSTM for C2. SHAP identified Sustainability Reporting Quality and Tobin’s Q as leading ESGIP parameters. The framework supports transparent ESG assessment, sustainable investment screening, and risk-aware decision-making aligned with Saudi Vision 2030. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating corporate sustainability information with market and risk indicators to improve interpretable ESG intelligence in emerging markets.

title: TRANSFORMING OPERATIONAL KNOWLEDGE INTO DIGITAL CAPABILITIES IN MINING: THE BUSINESS KNOWLEDGE TRANSFORMATION MODEL
summary: This study proposes the Business Knowledge Transformation Model (BKTM), a conceptual framework explaining how operational knowledge is transformed into executable digital capabilities in mining. The study addresses the fragmentation of expertise, technical documents, business rules, and information flows among mining companies, laboratories, logistics operators, and industrial users. A conceptual research design integrates Business Process Management, Knowledge Management, Digital Transformation, and Requirements Engineering. Six interrelated constructs are organized into a continuous sequence: Business Knowledge, Business Rule Formalization, Process Standardization, Digital Capability, Operational Intelligence, and Organizational Learning. The framework is illustrated by its industrial instantiation in the SIGECAM platform, which supports coal quality management across multiple stakeholders in Brazil. The analysis identifies conceptual correspondence between formalized decision criteria, standardized workflows, digitally supported execution, traceability, and operational learning. The BKTM offers an organizational explanation of digital transformation beyond the adoption of isolated technologies. As the model is illustrated through a single industrial implementation, its theoretical relationships require empirical testing in additional organizations and sectors. The framework provides a reference for knowledge-driven digitalization and continuous process improvement.

title: From responsibility to reputation: how perceived corporate social responsibility shapes corporate brand image
summary: Purpose This study aims to examine how perceived corporate social responsibility (PCSR) shapes corporate brand image by unpacking the psychological mechanisms and boundary conditions underlying this relationship in the telecommunications service sector. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the Stimulus–Organism–Response framework, this study develops an integrated moderated–mediation model in which brand familiarity and brand equity function as cognitive and affective mediators respectively, and customer trust operates as a key boundary condition. Survey data from 350 customers of leading telecommunications providers in India were analysed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling. Findings The results show that PCSR has a non-significant direct effect on corporate brand image and indirect effects through both brand familiarity and brand equity, indicating complementary full mediation. PCSR strengthens brand familiarity by enhancing cognitive accessibility and recognition, while simultaneously increasing brand equity through value based and emotional evaluations. Customer trust significantly moderates these relationships, amplifying the branding effects of perceived CSR under high trust and weakening them when trust is low. Practical implications The findings highlight the importance of treating PCSR as a strategic, trust anchored branding capability rather than a symbolic reputation tool, particularly in service intensive and trust sensitive markets. Originality/value By combining dual mediation and trust based moderation, this study provides a holistic and decision relevant understanding of how PCSR translates into corporate brand image, reflective of quality the brand offers.

title: Digital payments in Morocco and cash persistence: prioritizing barriers and enablers through a Delphi study
summary: Purpose Cash remains the dominant payment instrument in Morocco despite continued infrastructure upgrades and a more active FinTech ecosystem. Prior research identifies many determinants of digital payment adoption, but rarely clarifies their relative importance from the perspective of ecosystem actors. This study aims to identify and prioritize the barriers sustaining cash use and the enablers most likely to expand digital payment adoption in Morocco. Design/methodology/approach A three-round Delphi study was conducted with 29 payment-ecosystem experts. Round 1 used open-ended questions. Round 2 retained eight barriers and eight enablers based on a majority rule. Round 3 asked experts to rank the retained items; ranks were aggregated to obtain collective priorities and Kendall’s W measured consensus. Findings Cultural attachment to cash and behavioral inertia are ranked as the most influential barriers, followed by merchant-side economic constraints and transaction costs. These barriers matter because they shape the effective cost-benefit calculus of payment choice and slow the conversion of formal access to digital tools into routine use. Interoperability and digital skills receive lower priority. On the enabling side, targeted fee reductions for low-value transactions, lower merchant acceptance costs and the digitization of recurring payments emerge as the top priorities. Consensus is low to moderate (W = 0.21 for barriers; W = 0.18 for enablers), reflecting heterogeneous assessments. Research limitations/implications Results are context-specific and based on expert judgment; rather than direct behavioral observation; future studies may triangulate with merchant and consumer evidence or transaction-level data. Practical implications Accelerating adoption requires prioritizing economic incentives and embedding digital payments into everyday use cases rather than relying solely on technological improvements or the mere expansion of payment infrastructure. Originality/value Provides an ecosystem-based Delphi prioritization of barriers and enablers of digital payment adoption in Morocco and shows that the main challenge lies less in the availability of technology than in the economic and behavioral conditions governing everyday payment use.

title: Privatization, ownership structure and policy trade-offs: The sale of Íslandsbanki
summary: This paper examines the three-stage privatization of the Icelandic bank Íslandsbanki in 2021–2025 as a case of how public sellers balance revenue maximization against ownership and governance objectives. Using official reports, auction documentation, order-book data, market prices and post-sale shareholder lists, the study evaluates whether discounts granted to buyers produced durable benefits in ownership structure. All three offerings were heavily oversubscribed. In the 2022 accelerated book-building (ABB) sale, demand remained many times the amount offered even at prices above the chosen sale price. Yet dispersed ownership declined after the public offerings, foreign participation remained limited, and common ownership across competing Icelandic banks became substantial. The findings suggest that discounted pricing and initial allocation are weak instruments for shaping long-run ownership when shares are freely tradable. The case contributes to corporate governance research by linking privatization design to ownership structure, institutional ownership and principal–agent problems in public asset sales.

title: LA GOUVERNANCE DU SYSTÈME JUDICIAIRE MAROCAIN À L'ÉPREUVE DE LA MODERNISATION : UNE LECTURE PAR LA THÉORIE DE L'AGENCE ET LE MODÈLE DE MINTZBERG
summary: RÉSUMÉ : Cette étude analyse la gouvernance du système judiciaire marocain dans un contexte marqué par des transformations institutionnelles et numériques croissantes. Elle mobilise conjointement la théorie de l’agence et le modèle organisationnel de Mintzberg afin d’examiner les relations entre les acteurs institutionnels ainsi que les mécanismes de coordination qui structurent le fonctionnement des juridictions. Fondée sur une approche qualitative, documentaire et conceptuelle, l’analyse s’appuie sur la littérature scientifique et sur des sources institutionnelles marocaines. Les résultats mettent en évidence une configuration proche de la bureaucratie professionnelle, caractérisée par une forte autonomie des professionnels, qui coexiste avec des mécanismes de coordination, de responsabilisation et de contrôle institutionnel. Ils montrent également que la transformation numérique contribue à améliorer la circulation de l’information et les capacités de pilotage, tout en introduisant de nouvelles formes de standardisation. Le croisement des deux cadres théoriques révèle ainsi que la modernisation de la gouvernance judiciaire repose sur la recherche d’un équilibre entre autonomie professionnelle, coordination organisationnelle, circulation de l’information et contrôle institutionnel. L’étude souligne enfin la nécessité de préserver l’indépendance judiciaire tout en accompagnant l’évolution des dispositifs de gouvernance et de transformation numérique. Mots-clés : Gouvernance judiciaire ; Théorie de l’agence ; Bureaucratie professionnelle ; Mintzberg ; Transformation numérique ; Système judiciaire marocain. ABSTRACT: This study examines the governance of the Moroccan judicial system in a context characterized by ongoing institutional and digital transformations. It jointly draws on agency theory and Mintzberg’s organizational framework to examine relationships among institutional actors and the coordination mechanisms that shape the functioning of courts. Based on a qualitative, documentary, and conceptual approach, the analysis relies on both academic literature and Moroccan institutional sources. The findings reveal an organizational configuration close to professional bureaucracy, characterized by a high degree of professional autonomy that coexists with mechanisms of coordination, accountability, and institutional control. They also show that digital transformation contributes to improving information flows and governance capacities while introducing new forms of standardization. Combining the two theoretical frameworks reveals that the modernization of judicial governance depends on achieving a balance between professional autonomy, organizational coordination, information flows, and institutional control. Finally, the study emphasizes the need to preserve judicial independence while supporting the development of governance mechanisms and digital transformation. Keywords: Judicial governance; Agency theory; Professional bureaucracy; Mintzberg; Digital transformation; Moroccan judicial system.

title: Digital Dubai: Making Dubai the Digital Capital of the World
summary: When the Dubai Government announced in 2021 that it had processed its last-ever paper transaction, becoming the first government in the world to go paperless, it completed a 20-year journey of digital transformation that changed people’s lives across the emirate fundamentally.Since launching its e-Government initiative in 2001, Dubai had been on a mission to digitalise life in Dubai, making city services as easy, efficient and effective as possible, in alignment with the leadership’s vision to make Dubai the best city in the world to live in.

title: ITS Implementation in Smart Ports: Evidence from Five Comparative Case Studies
summary: This study examines the real-world operational applications of Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) technologies in smart ports and their implications for port management and digital transformation strategies. While ITS applications for road and passenger transportation have been widely discussed in the literature, fewer studies have considered their use in maritime and port operations. To address this gap, this study applies a multiple case study approach to five ports (Shanghai, Singapore, Rotterdam, Hamburg, and Los Angeles) to identify ITS components, technology usage patterns, and current application levels. Data were obtained from the port authorities’ official websites, resources, technical reports, and publicly available documents. The analysis identified 15 active ITS applications and 14 applications under development among the five ports, with the most intensive being Advanced Traffic Management Systems (ATMS), Advanced Traveler Information Systems (ATIS), Advanced Vehicle Control Systems (AVCS), and Advanced Commercial Vehicle Operations Systems (ACVOS) categories, reflecting the ports’ strategic prioritization of traffic management, operational efficiency, and security. Conversely, there were no active applications in Advanced Public Transportation Systems (APTS) and Advanced Urban Transportation Systems (AUTS) categories. Key technologies supporting smart port transformation included autonomous vehicles, digital twin platforms, vehicle-to-everything communication (V2X), AI-powered control systems, and cybersecurity solutions. These findings provide managerial, practical, and policy-relevant insights for port authorities and industry stakeholders while prioritizing ITS components, identifying dominant technological trends, and supporting evidence-based digital transformation strategies.

title: The Economic Effects of Digital Transformation on Chinese Listed Companies: An Investment Efficiency Perspective
summary: As China’s growth decelerates and its economic structure adjusts, the competitive advantages of traditional enterprises have eroded and corporate investment efficiency has declined. Understanding how corporate digital transformation transmits to the real economy is therefore the motivation for this study. Using Python-based text analysis, this paper constructs a corporate digital transformation index and, drawing on data from China’s A-share listed non-financial firms over the period 2012–2025, examines the impact of digital transformation on corporate investment efficiency. The analysis further explores the heterogeneous effects of digital transformation across firms differentiated by ownership structure, investment opportunities, and the intensity of external monitoring. The results show that higher levels of digital transformation alleviate financing constraints and reduce corporate governance costs, thereby enhancing investment efficiency. To address potential endogeneity concerns, a series of robustness checks are conducted, including instrumental-variable estimation, propensity score matching, the replacement of core variables and alternative estimation strategies, all of which yield results consistent with the baseline findings. Moreover, the positive effect of digital transformation on investment efficiency is particularly pronounced among firms with weaker external monitoring, non-state ownership, and more abundant investment opportunities.

title: "Digital transformation in accountancy: a study of emerging technologies, adoption challenges, and future implications"
summary: Abstract The field of accountancy has undergone a paradigm shift in the last two decades due to rapid technological advancements. Traditional bookkeeping and manual ledger systems have been replaced by cloud-based accounting software, artificial intelligence, blockchain, and data analytics tools. This paper explores the integration of technology in accountancy, examining how automation, AI-driven audit tools, cloud ERP systems, and blockchain are redefining accounting practices. It further analyses the benefits such as enhanced accuracy, real-time reporting, fraud detection, and cost efficiency, alongside challenges including cybersecurity risks, skill gaps, and resistance to change. The study employs a mixed-method approach, reviewing secondary literature and industry reports from 2020-2026 to assess technology adoption trends among small, medium, and large enterprises in India. Findings suggest that while large firms have embraced digital transformation, MSMEs lag due to cost and awareness barriers. The paper concludes that technology in accountancy is no longer optional but a strategic necessity, recommending continuous upskilling, regulatory support, and phased digital adoption for sustainable growth.

title: FINANCIAL PERFORMANCE: GOVERNANCE, RISK, COMPLIANCE AND DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION
summary: The disparity between aggregate banking profitability and individual bank performance, coupled with inconclusive evidence on Governance, Risk, Compliance, and Digital Transformation, necessitates further investigation. The study aims at examining their effects on the financial performance of conventional commercial banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. Using 80 firm-year observations, this study employs a Random Effects Model with cluster-robust standard errors. Financial performance is measured by Return on Assets (ROA), while Governance is represented by the Board of Directors, Audit Committee, and Independent Board of Commissioners; Risk by the Non-Performing Loan (NPL) ratio; Compliance by a Compliance Disclosure Index based on GRI Standards 2021; and Digital Transformation by a Digital Transformation Index. The results show that NPL and Digital Transformation negatively affect ROA, while Governance, Compliance, CAR, and OEtOI have no significant effects. The study provides an integrated assessment of these factors in Indonesian banking.

title: Foreign Direct Investment, Poverty Reduction and Employment Generation in Rivers State, Nigeria, 2015-2025
summary: This study examined the effect of foreign direct investment (FDI) on poverty reduction and employment generation in Rivers State, Nigeria, between 2015 and 2025. Despite cumulative FDI stock exceeding $60 billion by 2024, concentrated overwhelmingly in petroleum and petrochemical operations, Rivers State continued to exhibit poverty rates of approximately 45 per cent and unemployment exceeding 30 per cent, a disconnect that motivated the study's two objectives. The study was anchored on Dunning's Eclectic Paradigm (OLI Theory) and Dependency Theory, which jointly explain why resource-seeking FDI concentrates in Rivers State's petroleum sector and why such capital-intensive, enclave-structured investment has historically generated limited broad-based local development. A convergent parallel mixed methods design was adopted across Port Harcourt City, Obio/Akpor, Eleme and Bonny Local Government Areas. A structured four-point Likert questionnaire was administered to a Taro Yamane-derived sample of 400 respondents, drawn from a target population of 2,350,000 and analysed using descriptive statistics and simple linear regression, while thirty semi-structured key informant interviews supplied qualitative triangulation. Findings showed that FDI had a statistically significant but substantively weak effect on both poverty reduction (R² = 0.081, p < .001) and employment generation (R² = 0.097, p < .001), with respondents overwhelmingly disagreeing that foreign investment had reduced household poverty or generated substantial direct local employment, instead reporting that environmental degradation had eroded farming and fishing livelihoods and that domestic labour remained confined to casual, low wage positions while technical and managerial roles were staffed by expatriates. The study recommends converting discretionary corporate social responsibility palliatives into legally enforceable host community development trusts and reforming local content enforcement to measure genuine technical skills transfer rather than contract value.

title: The critical foundations of truly sustainable environmental auditing
summary: This essay addresses the urgent need for transformative action in environmental governance and examines how environmental auditing can support diagnostic and transformative agency within social-ecological systems. This requires a radical conceptual reconfiguration of environmental audit. To this end, the essay advances five conceptual foundations for a more impactful and sustainable approach. These include: an overarching commitment to Earth system stability; transcending an organization-centric paradigm; repositioning environmental auditing as a first-order function that drives, rather than follows, accounting; leveraging diverse forms of accounts to generate diagnostic insights into what truly matters within social-ecological systems; and actively coordinating accountability processes. Collectively, these foundations reposition environmental audit as a dynamic practice for nurturing meaningful change in social-ecological systems.

title: Supply chain agility enablers and SME performance: The roles of supply chain risk management performance and risk management culture
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines associations between three proactive enablers of supply chain agility, SME performance, and supply chain risk management performance, and assesses the mediating and moderating roles of supply chain risk management performance and risk management culture. Data were collected through an online survey using convenience sampling and analyzed via PLS-SEM. The study included 224 SMEs operating in the West Bank, Palestine. The findings indicated that market sensing (β = 0.358, p < 0.01) and supply chain integration (β = 0.318, p < 0.01) were positively and significantly associated with SME performance. In contrast, strategic sourcing (β = 0.050, p > 0.05) was not significant. Market sensing (β = 0.383, p < 0.01), strategic sourcing (β = 0.311, p < 0.01), and supply chain integration (β = 0.321, p < 0.01) were positively and significantly related to supply chain risk management performance. Supply chain risk management performance (β = 0.626, p < 0.01) was significantly related to SME performance. The results showed no moderating effect of risk management culture on the relationships between the three supply chain agility enablers and supply chain risk management performance (p > 0.05). Supply chain risk management performance significantly mediated the relationships between all three enablers and SME performance, with full mediation for strategic sourcing and partial mediation for supply chain integration and market sensing. Moreover, the model explains 77.3% of the variance in SME performance (R² = 0.773) and 61.3% of the variance in supply chain risk management performance (R² = 0.613).

title: Readiness Analysis and Cloud-Based AIS Design for ISAK 35-Based Mosque Financial Management at Darul Falah Mosque, Sleman
summary: This study aims to analyze the readiness and propose a cloud-based Accounting Information System (AIS) design for ISAK 35 compliance at Darul Falah Mosque, Sleman. Given the rapid growth of religious entities managing public funds, standardized financial governance is critical, yet many mosques struggle with conventional reporting. This descriptive qualitative study evaluates the existing financial framework and designs a modernized AIS utilizing the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC) method. Data were collected through direct observations, document analysis, and in depth interviews with five key informants, including the Head of Takmir, Treasurer, and congregation representatives. Data credibility was ensured through source triangulation and analyzed using NVivo 12 thematic coding. The findings reveal that the mosque's current reporting lacks standardized account classifications. Transitioning to ISAK 35 requires a comprehensive restructuring into five primary components. Consequently, a cloud based AIS architecture encompassing database, process, and interface design was proposed. This proposed framework is expected to improve real time transparency, internal control, and accountability of congregational funds compared to traditional manual methods. Ultimately, this study contributes by theoretically and practically integrating Indonesia's latest non-profit accounting standards (ISAK 35) with cloud computing architecture, providing a scalable blueprint for mosque financial digitalization.

title: Burberry’s Digital Strategy - Abridged
summary: The case analyses how Burberry developed and executed a strategy centered on millennial consumers, British appeal and distinctive digital capabilities, transforming the sesquicentennial brand into an international luxury powerhouse. Burberry’s digital transformation was spearheaded by CEO Angela Ahrendts and Chief Creative Officer (CCO) Christopher Bailey. Between 2006 and 2014, the duo launched a multitude of initiatives, such as innovative social media campaigns, livestream fashion shows, and a new e-commerce platform, enabled by a state-of-the-art technological infrastructure and a closely connected organisational culture. When Ahrendts left to join Apple, Bailey assumed the position of CEO and CCO at Burberry. In May 2015, 10 months into his new dual role, Bailey prepared to report mixed results for the last financial year and reveal his plans to address the challenges presented by the changing competitive landscape.

title: MANAGING DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN SECONDARY SCHOOLS: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF CHINA AND KAZAKHSTAN
summary: Worldwide, digital change is central to education modernization. For secondary schools, it involves more than computers, internet and digital platforms. It reshapes school governance, educational leadership, classroom practice, teacher development, data management and organizational culture. This paper compares digital‑transformation management in Chinese and Kazakh secondary schools. Drawing on policies and existing literature, it analyses national digital‑education strategies, infrastructure, teaching platforms, teachers’ digital skills, school leadership, data governance and digital equity. Both countries prioritize digital reform for educational modernization under different institutional backgrounds. China applies a centralized service‑driven model exemplified by the National Smart Education Platform. Kazakhstan integrates school digitalization into national education and digital‑economy strategies. They share common challenges: uneven digital infrastructure, varying teacher digital skills, data‑management troubles, cybersecurity threats and insufficient digital leadership at school level. Technical investment alone cannot guarantee successful transformation. School leaders need to combine digital tools with strategic planning, teacher training, institutional adjustment and evidence‑based decision‑making.

title: Sustainability reporting readability, stock liquidity and the role of corporate governance: evidence from an emerging market
summary: Purpose This study investigates whether the readability of sustainability reports affects stock liquidity and how corporate governance mechanisms shape this relationship. Drawing on agency theory, we ask whether investors reward clear non-financial disclosure. By answering this in Iran – a sanctioned emerging market with concentrated ownership – we test the boundaries of Western-developed theories and offer novel evidence from an institutionally distinct context. Design/methodology/approach Our sample comprises 612 firm-year observations from the Tehran Stock Exchange over 2016–2024. We measure sustainability report readability using the Gunning Fog Index and capture stock liquidity using three proxies: the bid-ask spread, Amihud’s illiquidity ratio and the average daily transactions. We examine four governance moderators: blockholder ownership, institutional ownership, board independence and audit firm type. The analysis employs panel data models with fixed effects and Newey–West adjustments. Findings More readable sustainability reports are associated with higher stock liquidity. However, this relationship depends on governance structures. Blockholder ownership and board independence significantly amplify the positive effect of readability on liquidity. Institutional ownership does not emerge as a significant moderator, and audit firm type matters only for specific liquidity measures. These findings suggest that governance mechanisms are not interchangeable; the institutional environment shapes their effectiveness. Originality/value This study offers one of the first empirical examinations of how corporate governance moderates the relationship between sustainability reporting readability and stock liquidity in an emerging market context. By locating the study in Iran – an economy shaped by prolonged sanctions – we provide a robust test of agency theory’s boundaries. The result is a refinement: some expected relationships hold, others do not, revealing how context conditions the financial consequences of disclosure transparency. These findings offer actionable insights for policymakers designing disclosure regulations and for investors and boards seeking to enhance market efficiency in institutionally challenging environments.

title: Digital Transformation in Personal Protective Equipment Management: Design and Implementation of a Web-Based Digital Custody and Audit Trail System
summary: Paper-based personal protective equipment (PPE) custody documentation remains widespread in Turkish small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and public institutions despite traceability obligations under the Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) Law No. 6331, generating recordretention vulnerabilities and audit liability risks. Adopting a Design Science Research (DSR) framework, this study presents a web-based PPE digital custody artifact evaluated against three legislatively grounded design criteria: audit integrity (C1), regulatory compatibility (C2), and institutional adoptability (C3). The artifact operationalizes Walsh and Ungson’s organizational memory framework, transferring custody records from individual-dependent and physically vulnerable repositories to a relational database, markedly reducing staff-departure and archive-destruction failure modes. Indicative process measurements (n=15 digital transactions against an n=3 paper baseline) yield reductions of approximately 87% in record generation time and 94% in archive retrieval time, pending larger-sample replication. Normative legal analysis establishes that Canvas-based handwritten signatures constitute a simple electronic signature recognized under EU eIDAS, US ESIGN/UETA, and Turkish Law No. 5070. Although not a qualified-signature equivalent, the composite audit trail can serve as an evidentiary record where public key infrastructure (PKI) is absent, subject to judicial determination. Twelve role-based access control (RBAC) functional test cases confirm that the hierarchical architecture enforces the separation of duties required by Law No. 6331. The findings provide a replicable artifact specification and a DSR evaluation template for the OHS management information system (OHS-MIS) deployment in resource-constrained settings.

title: A SWOT Analysis of the U.S. National Artificial Intelligence Strategy And Its Implications for Smart Mobility
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is a cutting-edge technology that enhances efficiency across multiple sectors through the effective analysis of diverse data sources. Governments are continuously publishing strategic AI plans to adapt to AI-centric digital transformation. These plans address various concepts, including infrastructure investments, ethical and human values, innovation speed, political barriers, inclusiveness, and transparency. These efforts are critical for establishing the necessary infrastructure for the development of smart cities that integrate innovative systems and improve citizens’ quality of life. Smart mobility constitutes a key pillar of smart cities and is directly linked to the efficiency of these systems. Experience in AI governance underscores the importance of evaluating how national strategies affect such critical sectors. This study first evaluates the United States Artificial Intelligence Action Plan, published by The White House on July 10, 2025, using the SWOT analysis method. Subsequently, recommended policy actions and their potential impacts on smart mobility are examined in the light of literature findings. The SWOT analysis highlights advantages such as accelerated innovation and increased inter-institutional collaboration, as well as some disadvantages such as environmental and ethical concerns. Accordingly, this study presents recommendations for the transportation industry, which necessitates a strategic approach to diversity and inclusion. The findings of this study offer valuable insights for policymakers, urban planners, and transportation professionals in understanding the practical impact of AI strategies on smart mobility.

title: The Sahyadri Is Not Expendable: An Environmental Economics Assessment of the Saidongar Pumped Storage Project, Karjat, Maharashtra
summary: This working paper examines the Saidongar-1 pumped storage project (3,000 MW, Torrent Power) in Karjat, Raigad district, Maharashtra, which requires the diversion of about 233 hectares of forest land in the northern Western Ghats. It combines an essay, a verified evidence dossier and an economic analysis. Using an externality framework, it sets out the negative externalities of forest loss (biodiversity, water regulation, soil, carbon and the livelihoods of local tribal communities) and the positive externalities of the standing forest, and compares them with the project's claimed climate benefits. The developer's carbon claim is re-estimated under alternative charging scenarios: avoided emissions fall from about 5.85 Mt CO2 in the implied case to about 1.9 Mt if half of charging power comes from solar, and the project could add around 0.5 Mt CO2 if charged from the current grid mix. Benefit-transfer estimates value the forest's ecosystem services at roughly ₹0.4 to ₹10.5 crore per year. The paper argues that the decision process lacked transparency, a monsoon-season biodiversity baseline and meaningful public participation, and it proposes twelve policy demands and twenty-four open research questions on valuation, carbon accounting, displacement and governance.
