title: Confirmatory Factor Analysis of an Innovative Leadership Model for Private Universities in Hainan
summary: Purpose: This study examined and quantitatively validated an innovative leadership model for administrators of private universities in Hainan Province, China, in response to increasing demands for organizational innovation and digital transformation within the Hainan Free Trade Port context. Research design, data and methodology: The study reports the quantitative phase of a broader research project on innovative leadership. Preliminary variables were identified and refined through literature review and structured interviews in the first qualitative phase. In the present phase, quantitative data were collected from 429 faculty members using a 48-item questionnaire. Exploratory factor analysis and second-order confirmatory factor analysis were employed, with 45 retained items aggregated into 15 composite indicators for examine the factor structure and validate the proposed model. Results: The results initially supported 16 innovative leadership variables. One variable, Models Learning, was removed because of weak factor loadings in the exploratory factor analysis. The remaining variables were organized into five dimensions: Supportive Organizational Environment, Digital Connectivity, Innovative Capability, Collaborative Team Culture, and Innovative Strategic Orientation. Conclusions: The findings suggest that innovative leadership in private universities is a multidimensional construct. The validated model provides a context-specific structure for understanding and assessing innovative leadership among administrators in private universities in Hainan Province.

title: Facilitating the Digital Payment Transition: QRIS Assistance for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises in Duren Sawit, East Jakarta
summary: Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) make a significant contribution to the Indonesian economy, both in terms of job creation and contribution to Gross Domestic Product (GDP). However, in the rapidly evolving digital era, most MSMEs still face various challenges, particularly in utilizing digital technology for business development. Based on these conditions, this article presents the results of community service activities conducted by researchers through an MSME digitalization mentoring program in the Duren Sawit area of ​​East Jakarta. This activity aimed to increase the capacity of MSMEs in digital marketing and the use of electronic payment systems through QRIS. The method used was descriptive qualitative, encompassing field observations, in-depth interviews with MSMEs, activity documentation, and evaluation and follow-up stages. The mentoring program targeted two MSMEs with different business characteristics, who were then provided direct education on how to register for QRIS through the Gopay Merchant application. The results showed that both MSMEs experienced significant improvements in their digital capabilities. This was demonstrated by their ability to process non-cash transactions using QRIS and their businesses becoming more recognized through digital searches. The final evaluation revealed a positive response from business owners to the mentoring program, which they found to be very helpful in developing their business strategies. Thus, the MSME Go to Digital program has proven effective as a technology-based community empowerment program that can sustainably increase the competitiveness of MSMEs. This article recommends the importance of collaboration between the government, academics, and business owners in expanding the scope of digital transformation for MSMEs in Indonesia.

title: Inclusive Leadership in the Era of Artificial Intelligence: Strengthening Local Wisdom
summary: Research Aim: This study aims to analyze the role of Artificial Intelligence in shaping inclusive leadership and to formulate strategies for strengthening local wisdom as a foundation for sustainable leadership. Design/Methods/Approach: The study employs a Literature Review approach, synthesizing scholarly works from Scopus, Web of Science, and Sinta (2010–2026). Thematic analysis is used to identify patterns and relationships among inclusive leadership, AI, and local wisdom. Research Finding: The findings reveal that inclusive leadership plays a critical role in bridging technological advancement and human values. It enhances employee engagement, innovation, and decision-making quality while mitigating algorithmic bias. Additionally, integrating local wisdom strengthens ethical governance, social legitimacy, and organizational sustainability through value-based and culturally grounded practices. Theoretical Contribution/Originality: This research offers a novel integrative framework combining AI, inclusive leadership, and local wisdom, addressing the gap between technological and humanistic perspectives in leadership studies. Practitioner/Policy Implication: The study provides strategic guidance for leaders and policymakers to implement human-centered AI, promote inclusivity, and embed cultural values into digital transformation. Research Limitation: This study relies on secondary data; future research should incorporate empirical validation and sector-specific analysis.

title: Reconstruction of Islamic Green Banking: Fiqh Al-Bi’ah As A Model Of Sustainable Islamic Finance
summary: Despite the growth of green financing, Islamic banking remains largely reliant on secular Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks, overlooking the normative foundations of Fiqh al-Bi’ah (Islamic environmental jurisprudence). This study reconstructs an Islamic green banking model grounded in Fiqh al-Bi’ah to advance Sustainable Islamic Finance. Using a qualitative socio-legal approach, it combines bibliometric analysis, Natural Language Processing (NLP), and Ijtihadi Maqashidi analysis to examine 34 Indonesian Islamic banks from 2017 to 2024. NLP-based text mining reveals isomorphic mimicry, with Fiqh al-Bi’ah terminology appearing in less than 1% of sustainability reports. In response, the study proposes an operational model integrating principles such as fasād, mīzān, and ḥimā into banking mechanisms, including Eco-Haram Screening, Maqasid-based Credit Scoring, and Conservation-Linked Financing. The model offers a framework for regulators and Sharia standard-setters to shift Islamic banking from compliance-based practices toward value-based sustainable finance.

title: HDFC ERGO: A Product Ecosystem Built on Mindshare
summary: Anuj Tyagi, Joint Managing Director of HDFC ERGO, is facing the challenge of transcending the traditional limitations of insurance interactions and establishing a significant presence in customers’ minds beyond annual transactions. The case explores the context of the insurance industry in India before 2019, spans HDFC ERGO’s history, exploring the impetus for digital transformation with an emphasis on “multi-product” ecosystems, the evolving regulatory landscape, market shifts, and the inception and strategies behind the Control N vertical – the spearhead of HDFC ERGO’s digital innovation. The case delves into HDFC ERGO’s pursuit of expanding its market presence beyond traditional insurance through an ecosystem play and illustrates one of the facets of industry convergence and the rise of digitally-enabled broad firms that span several sectors.The case focuses on Anuj, a key decision-maker in HDFC ERGO, as he is confronted with the need to enhance customer engagement (mindshare). The case then analyses HDFC ERGO’s assessment of the healthcare and mobility sectors, examining opportunities for ecosystem expansion. This case can be taught independently or paired with its sister case, “From Ping An’s inspiration to HDFC ERGO’s journey: Building an insurance-based ecosystem” (CS-24-009) for a more in-depth analysis of the sequential steps HDFC ERGO took in this transformation. The present case focuses on the “what” and the linked case focuses on the “how”.

title: Mapping the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of sustainable supply chain management: a science-mapping approach
summary: Although SSCM research has grown rapidly, prior reviews remain fragmented, context-specific, or based on relatively small or dated datasets, which limits understanding of how the field’s intellectual structure has developed. This study maps the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of sustainable supply chain management (SSCM) and identifies major research gaps and emerging directions. A bibliometric and science-mapping analysis was conducted using 4,324 English-language Scopus articles and reviews published between 1999 and 2026. Performance analysis was combined with co-citation analysis, keyword co-occurrence analysis, strategic mapping, and thematic evolution analysis using VOSviewer and SciMAT. The co-citation results identify three foundations of SSCM research: (1) green supply chain management (GSCM) drivers and firm performance, (2) SSCM conceptual frameworks, and (3) core theories and methodologies. The keyword analysis reveals four major clusters: SSCM, circular economy, and digital technologies; green supply chain management, environmental management, firm performance; optimization and decision-making; and carbon emissions, costs, and profitability. The thematic evolution results show a shift from early research on sustainable development, green supply chains, costs, and industry applications toward carbon management, closed-loop supply chains, digital technologies, organizational performance, and resilience. Recent keywords, including circular economy, blockchain, artificial intelligence, Industry 4.0, and green innovation, indicate increasing attention to circular and data-driven supply chains. The study contributes by combining multiple science-mapping techniques to provide an integrated understanding of the SSCM field and identifying underexplored areas, including social sustainability, multi-tier implementation, digital technology effectiveness, carbon–performance trade-offs, and sustainable resilience. It also provides directions for developing sustainable, circular, low-carbon, digitally enabled, and resilient supply chains.

title: Stimulating the digital transformation of the construction industry in the Russian Federation
summary: The purpose of the study is to substantiate a system of economic and institutional instruments for stimulating the digital transformation of the Russian construction industry, taking into account the achieved level of information modelling adoption, regulatory changes and persistent digitalization constraints. The methodology combines system, comparative and structural-functional analysis, grouping and logical modelling. Official data and current Russian regulations are used. The study shows that mandatory information modelling requirements created a significant institutional impulse, while further adoption is constrained by high initial costs, skills shortages, uneven digital maturity, software interoperability problems and discontinuities of data acros lifecycle stages. The scientific novelty consists in a multi-level incentive mechanism that differentiates support by digital maturity and links public incentives to measurable operational outcomes.

title: Research on the Influencing Factors and Implementation Path of Digital Transformation Driven by Digital Innovation in Enterprises
summary: Against the backdrop of rapid development in the digital economy, digital innovation is reshaping enterprise innovation models and value creation methods, becoming an important driving force for promoting digital transformation of enterprises. However, digital transformation of enterprises is not a simple process of technology application, but a systematic process involving strategic adjustment, organizational change, resource integration, and ecological collaboration. This article is based on the theory of innovation ecology and dynamic capability, analyzing the internal logic of digital innovation driving enterprise digital transformation, and exploring the key factors and implementation paths that affect enterprise digital transformation. Research suggests that the empowerment of digital intelligence technology, integration of innovative resources, reshaping of organizational capabilities, and construction of innovative ecosystems are important factors driving digital transformation in enterprises; Enterprises should achieve deep integration of digital technology and business development by strengthening digital strategic leadership, enhancing digital technology application capabilities, optimizing organizational management models, and building an open innovation ecosystem. This article expands the research perspective of enterprise digital transformation under the background of digital innovation, and provides theoretical reference and practical inspiration for enterprise digital upgrading.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Small and Medium-Sized Enterprises: Mapping Research Evolution and Future Directions
summary: The rapid diffusion of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly following the emergence of generative AI and large language models, has accelerated digital transformation among small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), leading to a substantial increase in academic research. Despite this growth, the literature remains fragmented regarding its intellectual foundations, conceptual evolution, and organizational implications. This study aims to systematically map and synthesize the scientific literature on AI in SMEs by integrating bibliometric analysis with a systematic literature review (B-SLR). Bibliographic data were retrieved exclusively from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC). Following the PRISMA 2020 protocol, 345 peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2018 and 2026 were retained for analysis. Bibliometric performance analysis and science mapping were conducted using Bibliometrix (Biblioshiny), including publication trends, thematic evolution, co-occurrence analysis, thematic mapping, country collaboration and Three-Fields Plot synthesis of the literature. The findings reveal a rapid expansion of AI research in SMEs, particularly after 2023, accompanied by a gradual shift from technology-oriented studies toward organizational value creation, strategic management, innovation, and sustainability. Machine learning emerged as the dominant and most persistent research theme, while generative AI, human–AI collaboration, AI governance, and employee-centered perspectives were identified as promising but underexplored research directions. By integrating bibliometric science mapping with systematic evidence synthesis, this study provides a comprehensive overview of the intellectual, conceptual, and social structures of the field and proposes a future research agenda that contributes to organizational behavior, strategic management, and AI adoption research in SMEs.

title: Assessing Public Sector AI Readiness in Monkayo, Davao de Oro, Philippines: A Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) Framework Analysis
summary: This study evaluates Artificial Intelligence (AI) readiness in the public sector of Monkayo, Davao de Oro, Philippines, using the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework. For purposes of this study, the public sector refers to the Local Government Unit (LGU) and National Government Agency (NGA) offices operating within the municipality, whose personnel are responsible for delivering frontline administrative and public services to constituents. Using a descriptive-quantitative approach, the researcher collected data from 300 public-sector respondents to assess the Technological, Organizational, and Human Resource dimensions of AI readiness. Statistical analysis yielded an overall AI readiness mean of 3.68, indicating High AI readiness. Human Resource Readiness was identified as the most prepared and consistent dimension (M=3.91, SD=1.17), reflecting a workforce that is psychologically receptive to digital transformation. Although Technological (M=3.46) and Organizational (M=3.68) dimensions also attained high levels, they demonstrated greater internal variation, underscoring disparities in infrastructure and policy standardization across municipal offices. Within the TOE framework, the three dimensions are treated as interrelated components that jointly determine overall AI readiness rather than as independent predictors, with Human Resource Readiness acting as the strongest and most consistent component. The findings suggest that, while the workforce is ready for transition, the main obstacles to effective AI adoption are inconsistent technological resources and the lack of centralized protocols. The study recommends that local government units in developing economies prioritize technology parity programs and unified AI governance ordinances rather than culture-change initiatives. These results offer a strategic roadmap for bridging the digital divide in decentralized government structures and advancing data-driven public service delivery in similarly situated local governments in developing economies.

title: Digital Competence and Perceived Work Readiness: Exploratory Evidence from Selected Indonesian Vocational Hospitality Participants
summary: Digital transformation is changing the competencies expected of hospitality graduates, requiring them not only to encounter industry technologies but also to use digital information, communicate through digital platforms, adapt to unfamiliar systems, and perform technology-supported tasks. This study explored the relationships among technology exposure, digital learning integration, digital competence, simulation-based learning, institutional support, perceived barriers, and perceived work readiness among participants from Indonesian vocational hospitality-related programmes. A quantitative-dominant exploratory mixed-methods design with an embedded qualitative component was employed. Quantitative survey data were obtained from 26 purposively selected participants and analysed using descriptive statistics, preliminary internal-consistency diagnostics, Spearman’s rank-order correlations, bootstrap confidence intervals, and sensitivity analysis. Qualitative data from four open-ended survey questions were analysed using content analysis to contextualise the quantitative patterns. Participants reported relatively high levels of perceived work readiness, digital competence, digital learning integration, simulation-based learning, and institutional support, alongside more uneven exposure to hospitality technologies. Participants reported greater exposure to digital payment systems, online booking platforms, guest-messaging applications, and property-management systems, while exposure to business-intelligence dashboards, channel-management systems, smart-room technologies, and service robots was more limited. Digital competence, institutional support, simulation-based learning, and digital learning integration showed comparatively larger positive associations with perceived work readiness, whereas technology exposure and perceived barriers showed smaller and less precisely estimated associations. Within digital competence, digital ethics received the highest ratings, while data literacy was comparatively weaker. Open-ended responses emphasised the need for more authentic technology practice, improved access to industry-relevant systems, stronger instructor guidance, and closer alignment between educational technology use and workplace practice. Given the small purposive sample, institutional concentration, cross-sectional design, and reliance on self-report measures, these findings should be interpreted as preliminary and should not be generalised to Indonesian hospitality students more broadly. The study provides an exploratory basis for distinguishing technology exposure, self-reported digital competence, and perceived work readiness as related but conceptually distinct aspects of digital preparation in vocational hospitality education.

title: Dynamic Graph Learning for Core Data Asset Discovery Using Data Lineage Graphs
summary: The rapid growth of the digital economy has made the accurate identification of Core Data Assets (CDAs) increasingly important for enterprise data governance. Existing approaches, however, often rely on static, homogeneous dependency modeling or node-centric analysis, limiting their ability to capture complex value propagation patterns and the structural importance of data in enterprise business processes. To address these limitations, this study proposes a graph learning framework with dynamic (structure-adaptive) edge weighting for automated CDA discovery using data lineage graphs. The framework first introduces a dynamic edge-weighting mechanism that integrates node influence and relationship scarcity to represent heterogeneous value propagation between data entities. The framework then constructs a comprehensive feature representation by combining global influence, local topological characteristics, and functional connectivity patterns, enabling the model to capture different aspects of data-table importance. Based on these representations, we develop an ensemble learning model with group-based cross-validation and automated hyperparameter optimization for robust CDA classification. Experiments on five real-world lineage graphs from a single enterprise data warehouse demonstrate the framework’s effectiveness. The model achieves average AUC and F1 scores of 0.926 and 0.753, respectively, and outperforms the evaluated baseline methods in terms of F1-score and Precision; the strongest competing baseline attains higher AUC and Recall but substantially lower Precision and F1-score. The results show that the multidimensional structural features provide the main share of the improvement, that the dynamic weighting mechanism contributes a modest additional benefit, and that the approach is effective for lineage graphs of moderate scale in enterprise data governance.

title: Measuring What Matters: Constructing an ESG Controversy Index Using AI and Institutional ESG Frameworks
summary: ABSTRACT Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) controversies increasingly influence investment decisions, corporate accountability, and sustainability regulation. However, existing commercial controversy measures often rely on proprietary methodologies that limit transparency and make it difficult to understand how controversy assessments are generated. This paper aims to develop an ESG Controversy Index (ESGCI) that combines internationally recognised ESG principles with explainable artificial intelligence to provide a systematic approach to measuring firm‐level ESG controversy exposure. The ESGCI is constructed from more than 5000 annual and sustainability reports issued by S&P 500 firms between 2010 and 2023, together with ESG doctrines published by the United Nations, the Principles for Responsible Investment, the Organisation for Economic Co‐operation and Development and the International Labour Organisation. Natural language processing and supervised machine‐learning techniques are used to identify, classify and aggregate ESG controversies within a structured measurement framework. The proposed index is evaluated through a multi‐layer validation strategy incorporating conceptual assessment, document‐level out‐of‐sample testing, external comparison with Refinitiv ESG controversy measures, inter‐rater reliability, incremental validity and complementary robustness analyses. The findings show that the ESGCI captures controversy‐related information recognised by existing commercial measures while providing additional insights through a fully documented measurement process. The reported relationships remain consistent across alternative weighting schemes, lagged specifications and instrumental‐variable estimations, supporting the robustness of the empirical evidence. Rather than replacing existing ESG controversy ratings, the ESGCI offers a complementary approach that improves methodological transparency and facilitates reproducible ESG controversy measurement. By integrating institutional ESG principles with explainable AI and comprehensive validation procedures, this research seeks to contribute to the advancement of ESG measurement and provide a practical foundation for future research, investment analysis and sustainability reporting.

title: Information Spillovers Across Media Markets: Risk Perceptions and Cyclospora Outbreaks in U.S. Bagged Salads
summary: From 2018 to 2022, contamination of fresh produce by Cyclospora cayetanensis, primarily affecting bagged salads, caused more than 3,300 outbreak-associated illnesses across the United States. Yet the economic consequences of these outbreaks, and the role of information exposure in shaping consumer responses, remain poorly understood. This study quantifies changes in bagged salad purchases and associated retail losses during six selected large multistate outbreaks occurring from 2018 to 2022 and examines how risk perceptions evolve across outbreak-affected and neighboring regions. Guided by a risk perception framework emphasizing risk proximity and information-driven belief updating, we integrate epidemiologic outbreak data, designated market area (DMA)-level Google Trends search intensity as a geographically granular proxy for information exposure, and NielsenIQ household purchase data. Because DMAs often cross state lines, this design identifies information spillovers to non-outbreak states sharing a media market. A Heckman selection framework accounts for purchase participation and unobserved heterogeneity, while complementary retail scanner data assess whether retailer stocking adjustments contributed to the observed purchase declines. Across the outbreak periods examined in this study, weekly bagged salad purchases declined by an average of 3.89%, implying cumulative retail losses of approximately $373.67 million. Outbreak-specific searches (e.g., "Cyclospora") were associated with greater perceived risk and larger purchase reductions, while general salad-related searches were associated with smaller reductions. Spillovers across shared media markets further reduced purchases in non-outbreak states by 3.33% per week. Retailer analysis found no statistically significant store-level stocking reductions during outbreak or recall periods, supporting the interpretation that the observed purchase declines were primarily demand-driven. These findings highlight the economic significance of information-driven consumer responses and the importance of timely, accurate, and geographically targeted risk communication during foodborne outbreaks.

title: Accounting Treatment of BPJS Health Insurance Claims Using PSAK 74 Principles at PKU Wonosobo
summary: BPJS Kesehatan claims constitute a major source of revenue for PKU Muhammadiyah Wonosobo Hospital. However, claim submission, verification through the Berita Acara Hasil Verifikasi (BAHV), and post-audit adjustments may affect the value of receivables reported at the end of the accounting period. This study examines the recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure of revenue from BPJS Kesehatan claims, using the principles of PSAK 74 as an analytical benchmark rather than an accounting standard directly applicable to the hospital. A descriptive-comparative qualitative approach was employed. Data were collected from finance staff and the finance manager through unstructured interviews, observations of financial reporting practices, and a review of claim submission documents, BAHV records, accounting policies, and journal entries. A detailed examination of the January 2026 service period was conducted within the broader context of financial reporting for 2024–2025. The findings indicate that the hospital recognizes revenue on an accrual basis upon completion of healthcare services, initially measures claims based on applicable hospital tariffs and Indonesian Case-Based Groups (INA-CBGs) reimbursement rates, and subsequently adjusts receivables according to claim submission, verification, and audit outcomes. BPJS Kesehatan receivables are presented as a single current asset account without systematic classification by claim aging or verification status, while disclosures concerning claim-related uncertainties remain limited and general. The findings suggest that the principles of PSAK 74 can provide a useful comparative framework for strengthening risk-based receivables classification and financial statement disclosures.

title: Pengaruh Penerapan Green Accounting, Kinerja Lingkungan dan Intellectual Capital Terhadap Kinerja Keuangan Dengan Good Corporate Governance Sebagai Variabel Moderasi Pada Perusahaan Perkebunan Kelapa Sawit
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan menguji dan menganalisis pengaruh penerapan green accounting, kinerja lingkungan, dan intellectual capital terhadap kinerja keuangan dengan Good Corporate Governance (GCG) sebagai variabel moderasi pada perusahaan perkebunan kelapa sawit yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) periode 2021-2025. Sampel ditentukan dengan purposive sampling dan diperoleh 19 perusahaan dengan 95 observasi. Data dianalisis menggunakan regresi data panel dengan EViews. Hasil menunjukkan green accounting dan kinerja lingkungan tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap ROA, sedangkan intellectual capital berpengaruh positif signifikan. GCG memoderasi pengaruh green accounting secara negatif, namun memperkuat pengaruh kinerja lingkungan dan intellectual capital terhadap ROA. Temuan ini mengimplikasikan bahwa GCG berperan penting dalam mengonversi kinerja lingkungan dan modal intelektual menjadi kinerja keuangan.

title: Corporate sustainability disclosure: systematic literature review of materiality, carbon, assurance, and ESG
summary: Corporate sustainability disclosure has become a major accountability instrument, yet prior studies in Indonesia remain fragmented by theme, sector, or company pair, and no integrated map of their development exists. This article systematically examined the development of research on the quality, materiality, and assurance of corporate sustainability disclosure. A qualitative systematic literature review was applied to twenty articles published in 2021–2026 and indexed in SINTA and other academic databases, and thematic content analysis grouped them by similarity of topics, methods, and research objects. Five themes emerged: conformity with the Global Reporting Initiative Standards, materiality assessment, carbon emissions and climate-related disclosure, assurance statement quality, and integrated environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices with corporate governance. Disclosure quality among Indonesian companies was uneven across sectors and tended to be lower than that of multinational companies, and assurance practices were inconsistent because different standards, such as AA1000AS and ISAE3000, were used. Regulators and professional associations should issue more uniform assurance guidelines and apply double materiality more consistently, while companies should strengthen ESG committees and integrate sustainability risk management into governance to improve disclosure credibility.

title: Debt Crowdfunding Growth and MSME Credit Risk in Indonesia’s Sustainable Digital Economy
summary: Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Indonesia often lack the collateral that banks require, and Peer-to-Peer (P2P) lending, the debt form of crowdfunding, has become a channel through which they raise capital in the digital economy. Lending now grows fastest outside Java, where platforms hold the shortest records on their borrowers. This study builds a monthly panel of 34 provinces from official statistics of the Financial Services Authority (Otoritas Jasa Keuangan/OJK) for December 2023 to December 2024 and estimates two-way fixed-effects models with standard errors clustered by province. The models test whether faster growth of outstanding loans is followed by a higher share of loans more than 90 days overdue (Tingkat Wanprestasi 90 Hari / TWP90) and whether this link differs between Java and the other regions. Outstanding loans rose by 29.1% to Rp 77.02 trillion, by 20.5% in Java and by 57.8% elsewhere, and MSMEs held 36.7% of the stock at the end of 2024. Current growth shows no significant link with TWP90. Growth three months earlier is followed by a lower TWP90 in Java, with a coefficient of −0.084 (p < 0.01), while outside Java the coefficient is only −0.011 (p = 0.079), and the gap between the two regions is significant (p < 0.01). Rapid P2P expansion was not associated with higher TWP90 during the study period, while the observed negative relationship between earlier loan growth and TWP90 in Java was substantially weaker outside Java. Platforms and regulators therefore need closer credit assessment where lending grows fastest if debt crowdfunding is to support MSME capital formation and the targets of Sustainable Development Goals 8 and 9. The evidence is associational and covers thirteen months, so longer panels with data specific to MSMEs are needed.

title: Digital Transformation and Carbon Dioxide Emissions in Arab Countries: The Role of Energy Structure within an Extended STIRPAT Framework
summary: Digital transformation has become a fundamental element of sustainability strategies across the globe; However, its environmental implications remain inconclusive, particularly in economies that depend heavily on fossil fuels. Although digital technologies can improve energy efficiency, optimize resource allocation, and support low-carbon development, their expansion may also increase electricity demand and energy consumption. This concern is particularly important in the energy sector, which remains the principal source of carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions in many Arab countries. This study investigates the impact of digital transformation on CO₂ emissions, consequently climate change, in 18 Arab countries during 2018–2024 within an extended STIRPAT framework, emphasizing the role of the prevailing energy structure. Digital transformation is measured using the Arab Digital Economy Index, and the empirical analysis utilizes the two-step System Generalized Method of Moments (System GMM) to address potential endogeneity and unobserved heterogeneity while accounting for the dynamic structure of the data. Post-estimation diagnostic tests and an alternative quadratic specification are used to assess model adequacy and the robustness of the findings. The results indicate that digital transformation is positively and statistically significantly associated with CO₂ emissions. Energy consumption, oil consumption, industrial activity, and population growth are also significant drivers of emissions, whereas imports are statistically insignificant. The robustness analysis provides preliminary evidence that the positive association becomes more pronounced at higher levels of digital development; However, longer time series are required to confirm its nonlinear dynamics. Overall, digital transformation should not be considered as environmentally neutral. Its contribution to climate-change mitigation depends on complementary energy-sector reforms, particularly renewable-energy deployment, improved energy efficiency, electricity-system modernization, and the integration of digital technologies into broader low-carbon strategies. By extending the STIRPAT framework to fossil-fuel-dependent Arab economies, this study provides new empirical evidence for countries pursuing simultaneous digital and energy transitions.

title: The Study of Digital Transformation, Artificial Intelligence and Their Implications for Future Research
summary: Digital transformation changes the conditions under which organizations produce and use knowledge. Artificial intelligence adds new ways to search, predict, generate, and evaluate information. Yet greater use of these tools does not establish that research becomes more reliable or more original. This paper develops a critical narrative review and descriptive secondary-data analysis to examine that distinction. Selected publications on organizational change, AI-assisted work, scientific discovery, and governance provide the conceptual foundation. Published statistics from Stanford's AI Index and Eurostat illustrate changes in adoption between 2023 and 2025. The two series are analysed separately because their populations and measurement procedures differ. The evidence indicates expanding use, but adoption statistics cannot demonstrate causal improvements in research quality. An original conceptual framework links digital foundations and AI capabilities with changes in research practice, conditioned by human expertise, institutional arrangements, and governance. Four propositions translate the framework into questions for future testing. The proposed agenda prioritizes reproducibility, task-specific evaluation, skill development, equitable participation, and preservation of intellectual diversity. The paper concludes that future research should evaluate the complete knowledge-production process, including verification and correction costs, rather than treating faster output as sufficient evidence of progress. No primary survey, experiment, or model validation is claimed. The contribution is an integrated account of how organizations can study AI-enabled transformation while maintaining the evidentiary standards needed for credible knowledge

title: Mobile Edge AI Framework for Real-Time ESG Compliance Auditing through NLP and Blockchain Ledger Verification
summary: The Mobile Edge artificial intelligence (AI) framework is introduced as an environmental, social, and governance (ESG) verification system that integrates natural language processing (NLP) and permissioned blockchain to facilitate near-real-time ESG compliance auditing. A lightweight transformer model is employed to identify ESG-related claims and extract relevant indicators, numerical values, units, locations, and reporting times. Extracted claims are structured and recorded on the blockchain to ensure verifiable, tamper-resistant records. A discrepancy assessment mechanism then classifies each claim as supported, partially supported, contradictory, or unsupported. The prototype was evaluated using a synthetic Kaggle dataset containing 11,000 annual company records from 1,000 organizations across nine regions and multiple sectors. The ESG classification model achieved a true positive rate of approximately 93.2%, with F1-scores of 0.945, 0.915, and 0.895 for environmental, social, and governance claims, respectively. Claim verification rates ranged from 93.1% to 98.4%. Edge deployment reduced verification latency to 124 ms compared to 231 ms in the cloud environment, representing a 46.3% reduction. These findings indicate that the framework can enable proactive ESG auditing, enhance claim traceability, accelerate verification, and deliver explainable compliance-risk signals.

title: ESG Disclosure, Political Connections, and Financial Risk: The Moderating Role of Accounting Information Systems in Indonesian SOEs
summary: Background: Financial risk remains a critical governance concern for Indonesian state-owned enterprises (SOEs), particularly regarding sustainability disclosure, political connections, and accounting information systems (AIS). Objective: This study examines the effects of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure and political connections on financial risk and evaluates the moderating role of AIS. Methods: A quantitative explanatory approach was applied to 34 SOEs listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024, comprising 170 firm-year observations. Secondary data were obtained from annual reports, sustainability reports, and financial statements. Financial risk was assessed using the Altman Z-score proxy, ESG disclosure through GRI indicators, political connections through board affiliation proportions, and AIS through ERP implementation. Data were analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS. Results: ESG disclosure had no significant effect on financial risk (β = 0.099; p = 0.234), whereas political connections showed a positive and significant association (β = 0.521; p < 0.001). AIS did not significantly moderate the ESG disclosure–financial risk relationship (β = 0.071; p = 0.280) or the political connections–financial risk relationship (β = −0.097; p = 0.296). Including moderation terms increased R² marginally from 0.260 to 0.275. Conclusion: Political connections are significantly associated with financial risk, whereas ESG disclosure and AIS moderation show no significant effects. These findings highlight the importance of strengthening SOE governance alongside accounting information system development.

title: Investigating the Health Benefits of Climate Finance: Evidence From Developing Countries
summary: ABSTRACT Although climate finance has expanded considerably over the past decades as part of the global response to climate change, many developing countries continue to experience persistently high infant mortality, widespread undernourishment, low life expectancy, and rising mortality burdens. This paradox raises an important question: does climate finance merely support environmental objectives, or does it also contribute meaningfully to improving population health in developing countries? Despite growing scholarly attention to climate finance, existing studies have largely focused on environmental sustainability, carbon emissions, and economic growth, while providing limited evidence on its broader health implications. To address this gap, this study examines the effect of climate finance on health outcomes in 61 developing countries over the period 2003–2021. Specifically, the study investigates the effect of climate finance on infant mortality, prevalence of undernourishment, life expectancy, and death rates. Employing the Driscoll–Kraay estimator and the Instrumental Variable Generalized Method of Moments techniques, the findings consistently reveal that climate finance significantly reduces infant mortality, undernourishment, and death rates while improving life expectancy. These results remain robust after controlling for endogeneity, omitted‐variable bias, alternative data structures, additional covariates, and disaggregated climate‐finance measures. Further evidence shows that both adaptation and mitigation finance contribute positively to population health. The study concludes that climate finance constitutes not only an environmental instrument but also an important mechanism for improving public health and human wellbeing in developing countries.

title: Research on the Follow-up Audit of Inclusive Finance Policies
summary: This paper studies the follow-up audit of inclusive finance policy implementation in China. Based on the policy life cycle theory, it constructs an audit tracking framework covering policy formulation, implementation, and evaluation. By analyzing 150 audit announcements from 2019 to 2023, the paper identifies major problems such as policy implementation deviations, fund management loopholes, and insufficient audit coverage. It proposes three optimization suggestions: building a fintech-based information sharing platform, strengthening composite audit teams, and establishing a multi-party coordination mechanism to improve audit effectiveness and policy implementation performance.

title: From Goals to Results: An Analytical Perspective on Three Global Challenges Through the Lens of Project Management
summary: This independent analytical paper examines three major global challenges: biodiversity protection, the future of work in the age of artificial intelligence, and global supply chain resilience. Through the lens of project management, the paper explores the gap between global commitments and effective implementation, the unequal distribution of opportunities and resources, and the importance of accountability, education, and human empowerment. It argues that meaningful progress should be measured not only by stated goals, technological advances, or economic indicators, but also by tangible and lasting improvements in people's lives and opportunities. The paper reflects the author's personal perspective and applies project management principles to the analysis of complex global challenges.

title: Capability-Aware Digital Transformation: Adaptive Deployment Strategies for Enterprise AI
summary: A Falsifiable Multidimensional Policy for Sequencing, Capacity-Building, and Reversible Rollout / Enterprise AI implementation increasingly depends on organizational capabilities, governance, and behavior, but these requirements are already recognized in organizational readiness and phased-rollout research. This paper proposes the Capability-Aware Deployment Policy (CADP) as a bounded, testable method rather than a demonstrated technology. CADP represents each enterprise unit through task-specific capability, process, governance, support, benefit, risk, and observed-outcome variables, and uses a transparent policy to choose among capacity-building, pilot, expansion, maintenance, suspension, and rollback. It distinguishes mandatory noncompensatory constraints from soft objectives, explicitly protects safe low-readiness units from automatic exclusion, and accounts for measurement error, intervention overhead, irreversible consequences, and resource contention. A four-policy comparison contrasts simultaneous deployment, fixed staged rollout, technology-readiness ordering, and CADP, with an expert-governed fixed strategy as the strongest practical challenger. The proposed research program specifies adversarial synthetic environments, ablation tests, outcomes for sustained effective adoption, and a conditional prospective cluster evaluation. No simulation, organizational intervention, empirical uplift, algorithmic superiority, or global novelty is reported. The candidate contribution is an independently reproducible policy and falsification contract that will be valuable only if it adds measurable decision quality beyond existing readiness assessments, dynamic treatment methods, and well-designed staged deployment.

title: Peculiarities of accounting policy formation at unitary enterprises
summary: The relevance of the research topic is due to the need to study the specifics of the formation of accounting policies of unitary enterprises in the context of constant changes in legislation and increased requirements for transparency of financial reporting. A well-formed accounting policy makes it possible to ensure the reliability of accounting information, increase the efficiency of enterprise management and minimize financial risks. The work is based on the study of international financial reporting standards and federal accounting standards, scientific works of leading Russian and foreign scientists in the field under study. The research uses methods of analysis and synthesis, expert assessments and logical generalization. The purpose of this work is to consider the specifics of the accounting policy of unitary enterprises, identify the main problems of its formation and analyze the specifics of accounting in these organizations.

title: Social Media Influence on ESG Investment Intentions: Herding Effects Among Young Investors
summary: The rapid growth of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) investing has coincided with the increasing reliance of young investors on social media for financial decision-making. While digital platforms and financial influencers ("finfluencers") accelerate information dissemination, limited empirical work explains how digital cues interact with psychological biases in emerging markets. Drawing upon the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) and Social Influence Theory, this conceptual study proposes a framework to investigate the effect of social media exposure on ESG investment intentions among young retail investors in Malaysia, while examining herding behavior as a moderating mechanism. The proposed framework outlines a quantitative cross-sectional research design utilizing Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to test the structural relationships. The paper provides theoretical insights into the convergence of digital media dynamics, psychological biases, and sustainable finance in emerging markets, offering practical implications for policymakers, financial institutions, and regulators.

title: China Evergrande Group's High-Leverage Capital Structure: Formation Logic and Risk Evolution from a Corporate Finance Perspective
summary: The real estate sector is by nature capital-intensive, and high leverage has long been a standard practice for property developers across global markets. In China, the debt-fueled high-turnover growth model has backed the rapid expansion of the property industry for decades, but it has also built up considerable hidden debt risks. The launch of the "Three Red Lines" regulatory policy in 2020 has sharply tightened financing rules for developers, and the risks tied to extreme leverage strategies have gradually come to the surface. As the most representative player with an aggressive leverage strategy in the industry, China Evergrande Group's 2021 debt default has become a landmark case of corporate financial distress. This paper uses a literature review combined with case study analysis, and draws on trade-off theory and financial distress cost frameworks, supplemented by an accounting perspective, to explain how Evergrande's high-leverage capital structure formed and how its risks evolved and spread. The study finds that Evergrande's leverage level moved far past the optimal range predicted by traditional theory, pushed by scale expansion incentives, implicit expectations of policy support, and internal managerial agency problems. Accounting tools such as off-balance-sheet financing further hid the true size of its debt burden. Once external financing conditions tightened, accumulated risks set off a spiral of rising financial distress costs, which eventually grew into a full-scale liquidity crisis.

title: Independent Commissioners, Audit Committee, Ownership Structure, and Financial Statement Quality of Indonesian Consumer Cyclicals Firms
summary: This study examines associations between Good Corporate Governance (GCG) mechanisms and financial statement quality in Indonesian consumer cyclicals companies during 2022–2025, controlling for Return on Assets (ROA). Signed Discretionary Accruals (DA) indicate the direction of abnormal accrual adjustments rather than overall reporting quality. Purposive sampling yielded 19 companies and 76 firm-year observations. DA were estimated using the modified Jones model and analyzed through fixed-effects panel regression with Heteroskedasticity-Consistent Standard Errors, Type 1 (HC1) robust standard errors. Independent commissioners (β = 0.047787, p = 0.7227), audit committee meetings (β = −0.010318, p = 0.4797), and institutional ownership (β = −0.003788, p = 0.9574) showed insignificant associations. Managerial ownership was positively associated with DA (β = 0.430569, p = 0.0271), contrary to expectations. ROA was also positively associated (β = 0.562850, p = 0.0032). Although the overall model was significant (p = 0.002878, R² = 0.527732), the joint governance test was insignificant (p = 0.219619). Thus, H1–H5 were unsupported. Governance mechanisms did not consistently constrain income-increasing accrual adjustments. Positive signed DA does not independently establish manipulation or declining reporting quality. Findings are restricted by the sector-specific sample, four-year observation period, and accrual-model assumptions. This study provides sector-specific evidence challenging uniform agency-theory expectations and demonstrates why governance indicators alone cannot establish monitoring effectiveness.

title: Robust global supply chain reconfiguration under tariff and geopolitical uncertainty
summary: Global supply chains are increasingly exposed to trade policy shocks and physical disruptions arising from common geopolitical events. We develop a robust optimization framework with two decision stages for strategic supply chain reconfiguration. Supplier qualification and transportation arc activation decisions are made before uncertainty is realized, while operational flows adapt afterward. Geopolitical uncertainty is represented through country level shocks that can jointly trigger tariff escalation, policy induced restrictions on cross border capacity, facility disruptions, and physical transportation failures. The resulting min max min problem is reformulated by dualizing the operational recourse problem, yielding a nonconvex mixed integer bilinear adversarial problem solved within a column and constraint generation procedure. Comparison with complete enumeration verifies the implementation on small instances, while experiments on 60 synthetic supply chain networks of varying sizes assess computational performance. The results show that omitting geopolitical transmission channels during strategic design can lead to substantial deterioration in cost and service under full geopolitical stress. Broader protection is achieved primarily through changes in transportation network configuration rather than increased supplier qualification. Robust performance also depends on the severity and composition of geopolitical consequences, with restrictions on cross border capacity exerting a stronger effect than comparable proportional changes in tariff severity over the tested ranges. A geographically grounded case analysis further shows that the value of individual uncertainty channels depends on network structure and geographic exposure.

title: How does digital economy development influence foreign direct investment inflows?
summary: This study explores the impact of digital economic development (DED) on foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows using panel data from the Yangtze River Delta (YRD) city cluster (2012–2023) and a two-way fixed-effects model. Empirical results demonstrate that DED significantly enhances FDI inflows. These findings remain robust across a series of endogeneity and robustness checks, including instrumental variable (IV) methods, difference-in-differences (DID), dynamic effect models, and propensity score matching-DID (PSM-DID). Mechanism analyses reveal that DED facilitates FDI by driving technological innovation, reducing transaction costs, and expanding consumer markets. Heterogeneity tests indicate that this positive effect is more pronounced in metropolitan areas characterized by robust intellectual property protection, advanced digital infrastructure, and superior economic development. Furthermore, DED exerts the most substantial influence on FDI in the YRD and Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei (BTH) regions. Spatial spillover analyses indicate that while DED stimulates local FDI inflows, it simultaneously diverts investment away from neighboring areas. Ultimately, this paper enriches the theoretical understanding of DED as a crucial determinant in FDI location decisions and offers actionable policy implications for leveraging the digital economy to attract foreign investment and stimulate regional economic growth. title: PROBLEMS OF YOUTH EDUCATION IN THE PROCESS OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION OF EDUCATION
summary: This article analyzes the current problems of educating young people in spiritual and moral, intellectual, and social aspects in the context of the digital transformation of the education system. It examines the influence of digital technologies, the Internet, social networks, and artificial intelligence tools on young people's worldviews, moral values, independent thinking, and social behavior. In addition, scientific and practical recommendations are developed for fostering information culture in the digital environment, developing media literacy, ensuring cybersecurity, and improving cooperation between families and educational institutions.

title: Digital Transformation of Fundraising in Non-Profit and Cultural Projects
summary: The article examines the process of digital transformation of fundraising in non-profit and cultural organizations at the current stage of development in Russia and abroad. The authors survey the theoretical foundations of digital fundraising, highlight its main digital tools (social networks, crowdfunding platforms, CRM systems, PR campaigns, email marketing). The paper also presents a comprehensive model of digital fundraising, which includes a methodology for setting goals (SMART), strategic analysis (SWOT), and a system of efficacy evaluation indicators (KPI, ROI, NPS). The statistical data analysis of the crowdfunding platform Planeta.ru is performed and the main trends in the development of digital fundraising in Russia are identified. The research results demonstrate that the integration of traditional fundraising mechanisms with digital tools contributes to the sustainable development of cultural organizations in the culture field. It is concluded that the last needs a modernization at the expense of the skilled workers renewal, the uprise of their digital competence, electronic platforms distribution in the regional institutes, and the adoption of the experience of financing them by the effect of multiple stakeholders.

title: DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION AND SERVICE DELIVERY IN THE NIGERIAN TELECOMMUNICATIONS INDUSTRY
summary: This study examined the effect of digital transformation on service delivery in the Nigerian telecommunications industry. An ex-post facto design was adopted, using annual secondary data from 2001 to 2024 (24 observations) sourced from the Nigerian Communications Commission, the Central Bank of Nigeria and the National Bureau of Statistics. Service delivery was proxied by a composite Service Delivery Quality Score, which averaged 0.1714. Digital transformation was captured by mobile phone penetration, internet penetration, mobile money transaction and telecommunication network coverage, with literacy rate as a control. Unit root tests revealed a mixture of I(0) and I(1) series. The Autoregressive Distributed Lag bounds test confirmed cointegration (F = 4.8293), exceeding the 1% upper bound of 4.15. Long-run estimates showed that mobile phone penetration (β = 0.1598, p = 0.0171), telecommunication network coverage (β = 0.0119, p = 0.0000) and literacy rate (β = 0.0591, p = 0.0082) significantly improved service delivery. Internet penetration (β = −0.0503, p = 0.2750) and mobile money transaction (β = −0.1473, p = 0.2782) were negative and insignificant. The error correction term (−0.6007, p = 0.0000) indicated that about 60.07% of disequilibrium is corrected annually, and the short-run model explained 89.58% of the variation in service delivery. Diagnostic tests confirmed normal residuals, no serial correlation, homoskedasticity and parameter stability. The study concluded that infrastructural reach, rather than usage intensity, sustains service quality. It recommended prioritised investment in network coverage, deeper mobile access and targeted digital literacy programmes.

title: Where to Site Direct Air Capture? Optimal Global Supply Chains from Capture to Storage
summary: The cost and net removal efficiency of direct air capture with CO2 storage (DACCS) depend strongly on siting, power supply, and how captured CO2 reaches storage. Here, we present a globally resolved (1° × 1°) assessment of solid-sorbent DACCS supply chains for near-term and mid-century scenarios, coupling hourly techno-economic optimization, (prospective) life-cycle assessment, and multimodal CO2 transport to storage to estimate net levelized costs of carbon dioxide removal that account for cradle-to-grave greenhouse gas emissions. In the near-term, the cheapest sites require ∼1,100–1,200 USD/tCO2 in the central United States and western Australia; cost is governed less by CO2 capture than by access to CO2 transport and storage and the regional cost of capital, while local wind resources enable the cheapest sites. A siting hierarchy emerges: proximity to geological storage is preferred, and a well-connected port is a near-equivalent substitute where storage is distant. By 2050, a lower-carbon global economy, cheaper CO2 transport, and technological learning broaden low-cost deployment, with ∼98% of sites below 1,000 USD/tCO2 (cheapest ∼370) at a median ∼93% removal efficiency. Near-term first-mover regions remain the lowest in cost, indicating low risk of stranded assets.

title: Indirect tax accountability as record agreement: inventory accounting and auditing under digital technologies and big data
summary: An industrial enterprise keeps three accounts of the same goods. Operations hold a physical record of what moved, the enterprise system holds a transactional record of what was documented and priced, and the tax function holds a fiscal record of what was declared. Indirect taxation works to the extent that the three records agree. The standard evasion schemes in manufacturing, namely unrecorded output, invented purchasing, disguised disposal and elastic valuation, all drive the records apart while leaving each one internally plausible. Serialized marking, sensor networks, enterprise event logs and clearance-model electronic invoicing have changed what can be tested, because the three records now exist at population scale and in machine-readable form. Drawing on tax compliance economics, big data research in auditing, continuous assurance and organizational capability theory, this article reconstructs indirect tax accountability as a property of agreement among the three records rather than of any one of them. It first states the conditions under which agreement is evidence at all. A reconciliation carries weight only where its two sides descend from causally separate processes, so the records must contain measurement anchors generated outside the enterprise transaction-processing layer. Integrated systems violate that condition by default. Agreement is then formalized as a set of reconciliation residuals, and a detection condition is derived from stated assumptions. A scheme survives only while its divergence stays inside the noise floor of the tightest independent check that sees it, so the sustainable tax gap is the sum of those noise floors rather than a function of the number of controls in place. A sensitivity analysis shows how the bound moves when the assumptions of separability, exogenous tolerances and zero detection risk are relaxed. Four leakage channels are traced through the inventory cycle, matched to the reconciliation that exposes each, and condensed into four propositions with refuting observations and candidate measures. Uzbekistan is the instantiating setting, where clearance invoicing, serialized labeling and, from January 2026, automated invoice risk scoring have outrun enterprise capability, and where documented administrative reconciliation practice between 2021 and 2023 supplies a live episode and its governance failure mode.
